docs.title: ENUMs Usage Reference
docs.text:
How protobuf enums work across the RustMT5 layers — passing them in, the r#type fields, decoding them back, and a catalog of the ones you'll actually use.

All enums live under metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api (aliased pb throughout the docs).

docs.title: 1. Low-level (MT5Account): cast the enum to i32
docs.text:
The generated request structs store enum fields as i32. Pass Enum::Variant as i32:

use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoDoubleProperty as D;

let point = account.symbol_info_double(pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    r#type: D::SymbolPoint as i32,   // ← cast
}).await?.value;

docs.title: 2. Mid/high-level (MT5Service / MT5Sugar): pass the typed enum
docs.text:
The facade takes the enum directly and casts for you:

use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::SymbolInfoDoubleProperty as D;

let point = service.symbol_double("EURUSD", D::SymbolPoint).await?;  // ← typed, no `as i32`

docs.title: 3. Decoding an enum you received: try_from
docs.text:
Reply fields are also i32. Convert back with Enum::try_from(value):

use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode as Mode;

let s = account.account_summary().await?;
match Mode::try_from(s.account_trade_mode) {
    Ok(Mode::MrpcAccountTradeModeReal) => println!("REAL"),
    Ok(Mode::MrpcAccountTradeModeContest) => println!("CONTEST"),
    _ => println!("DEMO"),
}

docs.title: ⚠️ The r#type field
docs.text:
Several request/reply structs have a field literally named type — a Rust keyword — so prost emits it as the raw identifier r#type. Write it as-is in struct literals and field access:

pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), r#type: D::SymbolPoint as i32 }
//                                                      ^^^^^^
let side = position.r#type;  // Bmt5EnumPositionType: 0 Buy, 1 Sell

Structs with r#type: SymbolInfoDoubleRequest / …IntegerRequest / …StringRequest, PositionInfo, OpenedOrderInfo, OrderHistoryData, DealHistoryData, MrpcMqlBookInfo, and the streaming On*Data event structs.

account_info_* requests use property_id (not r#type); symbol_info_margin_rate uses order_type.

docs.title: A tiny decode helper
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::Bmt5EnumPositionType as Side;

fn side_str(p: &metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::PositionInfo) -> &'static str {
    match Side::try_from(p.r#type) {
        Ok(Side::Bmt5PositionTypeSell) => "SELL",
        _ => "BUY",
    }
}

docs.text:

// ✓ self-documenting

docs.title: Getting Started with RustMT5
docs.text: Start automating MetaTrader 5 from Rust in minutes — connect, read the account, place a trade.

docs.title: 🎯 What is RustMT5?
docs.text: RustMT5 is a type-safe, async Rust client for MetaTrader 5 terminals over gRPC. No C++ DLL wrappers — direct, typed, reliable programmatic trading.

docs.title: Three-layer architecture
docs.text:
Layer Type What it gives you Low MT5Account Raw gRPC, auto-metadata, typed …Data payloads Mid MT5Service Friendly args (typed enums, &str), clean scalar returns High MT5Sugar One-liners: balances, prices, order construction, risk sizing

Build on top with ready Strategies.

docs.title: 📦 Installation
docs.text:
Add the crate and an async runtime:

# Cargo.toml
[dependencies]
metarpc-mt5 = "*"           # this SDK
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
tokio-stream = "0.1"        # only if you consume streams

The SDK is async-first and built on tokio; every API call is .awaited.

Windows without MSVC? Build against the GNU toolchain (x86_64-pc-windows-gnu) with a MinGW-w64 install on PATH. See the project README for the exact toolchain setup.

docs.title: 🔑 API key & authentication
docs.text:
Connecting to MetaRPC production (mt5.mrpc.pro:443) needs an API key:

  1. Sign up — free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Generate a key — in the portal at https://mrpc.pro/my, under API Keys.
  3. Provide it — the SDK reads MRPC_API_KEY from the environment (falling back to "TRIAL"), and sends it as the apikey metadata header on every call.

docs.title: Session id is automatic
docs.text: Two things authenticate each request: your apikey and a terminal session id. You don't fetch the id yourself — connect_* obtains it from the gateway (ConnectEx → terminalInstanceGuid), the SDK stores it, and attaches it to every later unary call and stream. Read it any time with account.id().

docs.title: 🔌 Minimal connection example
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::MT5Account;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // user, password, grpc_server (None → mt5.mrpc.pro:443)
    let mut account = MT5Account::new(12_345_678, "password", None);

    // connect by broker cluster name (timeout in seconds)
    account.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;

    let s = account.account_summary().await?;
    println!("balance {:.2} {}  equity {:.2}", s.account_balance, s.account_currency, s.account_equity);

    account.disconnect().await?;
    Ok(())
}

Prefer the high-level API? Wrap it:

use metarpc_mt5::{MT5Account, MT5Service, MT5Sugar};

let mut sugar = MT5Sugar::new(MT5Service::new(MT5Account::new(12_345_678, "password", None)))
    .with_default_symbol("EURUSD");
sugar.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;

println!("balance {:.2}, bid {:.5}", sugar.balance().await?, sugar.bid(None).await?);
let ticket = sugar.buy_market_with_pips(None, 0.10, Some(20.0), Some(40.0), "first trade", 1001).await?;
println!("opened #{ticket}");
sugar.disconnect(false).await?;

docs.title: 🧩 Error handling
docs.text:
Every call returns Result<_, MT5Error>. A returned Ok means the API worked — for trading calls, also check the returned_code (10009 = success). See Return Codes.

let res = sugar.service().place_order(req).await?;  // transport/gateway errors → MT5Error
if res.returned_code != 10009 {
    eprintln!("trade rejected: {} ({})", res.returned_code, res.returned_code_description);
}

docs.title: 📖 RustMT5 Glossary
docs.text: The terms and concepts used across the RustMT5 SDK and MetaTrader 5 trading — the three layers in depth, then the Rust, protocol, and trading vocabulary.

docs.title: MT5Account
docs.text:
🔹 Layer 1 — Low-level API

The base layer: direct access to the MT5 terminal over gRPC.

Key characteristics

  • Builds each protobuf …Request and attaches apikey + session id metadata.
  • Unwraps every reply's oneof { data, error } (or flat data/error) into Result<…Data, MT5Error>.
  • Returns the typed protobuf …Data payloads — full control, maximum detail.
  • Owns connection, session and streaming (on_symbol_tick, on_trade, …).
  • 39 feature methods across 6 groups, plus connection helpers.

When to use: you need a field or variant the higher layers don't surface, or raw protobuf control.

Location: src/mt5/account.rs

Docs: MT5Account overview

docs.title: MT5Service
docs.text:
🔸 Layer 2 — Typed facade

The middle layer: friendlier signatures without hand-building requests.

Key characteristics

  • Takes typed enums and &str symbols; does the as i32 casts and request-building for you.
  • Simple getters unwrap …Data to a clean scalar (f64 / i64 / String / bool).
  • Richer payloads (quotes, histories, streams) are returned as-is.
  • 36 methods across the same 6 groups, plus connection delegates.

When to use: you want ergonomic, typed calls but drive your own order shapes — the layer most code sits on.

Location: src/mt5/service.rs

Docs: MT5Service overview

docs.title: MT5Sugar
docs.text:
🔺 Layer 3 — Convenience API

The high-level layer: business logic and one-liners.

Key characteristics

  • Order construction from side/volume; pip-based SL/TP; risk-based position sizing.
  • A default symbol (with_default_symbol) so price/order calls can take None.
  • Compact result structs (SymbolInfo, AccountInfo, DailyStats) and a Period enum.
  • Maps a non-10009 trade result to MT5Error::Api, so ? handles rejections.
  • 58 methods across 10 groups — the best starting point for most apps.

Key examples

  • buy_market(symbol, volume, comment, magic) — open a position in one line.
  • buy_market_with_pips(symbol, volume, sl_pips, tp_pips, …) — open with a pip bracket.
  • calculate_position_size(symbol, risk_percent, sl_pips) — size by risk.
  • balance() / equity() · close_all_positions(symbol) — quick reads and an emergency exit.

When to use: rapid development, prototyping, simple strategies.

Location: src/mt5/sugar.rs

Docs: MT5Sugar overview

docs.title: Async / await
docs.text: Every API method is async fn; run them inside a tokio runtime and .await them. There is no blocking API. See Async Model.

docs.title: Result & MT5Error
docs.text: Calls return Result<_, MT5Error>. MT5Error variants: Api { code, message, mql_code }, EmptyResponse, NotConnected, Connection, Transport, Status, InvalidArgument. Propagate with ?.

docs.title: Stream (tokio_stream)
docs.text: Subscriptions return Result<impl Stream<Item = Result<…Data, MT5Error>>, MT5Error> — the outer Result is "subscription opened", each item is a frame or error. Read with tokio_stream::StreamExt::next. See gRPC Streaming.

docs.title: Result structs
docs.text: MT5Sugar returns small plain structs instead of raw protobuf: SymbolInfo (name, bid, ask, spread, digits, point, volume min/step/max, contract_size), AccountInfo (login, name, company, currency, leverage, balance, equity), DailyStats (deals, profit, wins, losses).

docs.title: Enums & r#type
docs.text: Protobuf enums are i32 under the hood. Low level: pass Enum::Variant as i32; mid/high level: pass the typed enum; decode a received value with Enum::try_from(v). Fields named type appear as the raw identifier r#type. See ENUMs Usage.

docs.title: 🔌 gRPC & protocol
docs.text:
• gRPC — the RPC protocol the SDK uses to reach the MT5 gateway.
  • tonic — the Rust gRPC client the SDK is built on.
  • protobuf / prost — the message format; prost generates the Rust structs/enums, vendored in package/mt5_term_api.rs.
  • …Request / …Data / …Reply — a call sends a …Request; the server answers a …Reply carrying a …Data payload or an Error.
  • oneof { data, error } — how most replies wrap the result; the SDK unwraps it to Result<…Data, MT5Error>.
  • apikey — your MetaRPC token (MRPC_API_KEY env, else "TRIAL"), sent as metadata on every call.
  • session id (terminalInstanceGuid) — the terminal session the gateway assigns on connect_*, auto-attached to later calls; read via account.id().
  • RetCode (returned_code) — the trade-server result after a trading call; 10009 = success. See Return Codes.

docs.title: 💹 Market & prices
docs.text: Term Meaning Symbol A tradable instrument (EURUSD); names are broker-specific (suffixes like .m). Bid / Ask Best sell / best buy price. Spread = ask − bid. Point Smallest price step (SYMBOL_POINT). Pip 10 × point on 3/5-digit symbols (EURUSD 1 pip = 0.0001). Digits Decimal places in the price (SYMBOL_DIGITS). Tick One price update; tick value = money per tick per lot. Contract size Units per lot (e.g. 100,000 for FX). Volume / lot Trade size; bounded by volume_min / volume_step / volume_max. Market Watch The terminal's selected-symbols list; some calls need a symbol selected (symbol_select). DOM (Depth of Market) Level-II order book; subscribe/read/release (market_book_add/get/release).

docs.title: 📈 Orders, positions & deals
docs.text:
In MT5, orders, positions and deals are distinct:

  • Order — an instruction to trade (market or pending).
  • Position — the open exposure from a filled order.
  • Deal — an executed transaction in history; realized P/L lives on deals.
  • Pending order — rests until a price triggers it: Limit (better price) / Stop (breakout) / Stop-Limit.
  • SL / TP — protective Stop-Loss / Take-Profit exit prices.
  • Stops level (SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL) — minimum distance SL/TP may sit from the market, in points.
  • Freeze level — distance within which modify/close is blocked.
  • Slippage / deviation — allowed price movement between request and fill.
  • Magic number — a client id tagging orders from one strategy/EA.
  • Ticket — the numeric id of an order / position / deal.

docs.title: 💰 Account & money
docs.text: Term Meaning Balance Realized funds, excluding floating P/L. Equity Balance + floating P/L (live account value). Margin Funds reserved to hold open positions. Free margin equity − margin; available for new positions. Margin level equity / margin × 100, in percent (margin-call/stop-out below thresholds). Leverage Borrowing ratio (e.g. 1:100). Floating / unrealized P/L Profit of still-open positions (equity − balance). Realized P/L Profit of closed positions (from history).

docs.title: 🛡️ Strategy mechanics
docs.text:
• Breakeven — moving SL to (around) the entry once in profit, to remove risk.
  • Trailing stop — an SL that follows price in the favorable direction, ratcheting and never loosening.
  • Risk sizing — choosing lot size so a stop-out risks a fixed % of balance (calculate_position_size).
  • Period — a predefined reporting window enum: Today, Yesterday, ThisWeek, ThisMonth.
  • Orchestrator — a ready async fn strategy driving MT5Sugar (Market One-Shot, Bracket + Trailing, Pending Bracket).
  • Preset — StrategyPreset (what to trade) / RiskPreset (how much, how to protect). See Strategies.

docs.title: gRPC Streaming & Subscription Management
docs.text: How real-time subscriptions work in RustMT5 — how to open one, consume it, stop it cleanly, and the patterns you'll reuse.

docs.title: The streaming model
docs.text:
A streaming method returns:

Result<impl tokio_stream::Stream<Item = Result<…Data, MT5Error>>, MT5Error>
//     └─ outer: did the subscription OPEN? ──┘        └─ inner: each FRAME or an error ┘
  • Outer Result — resolves once, when you .await the call: Ok(stream) means the subscription opened; Err means it never started.
  • Inner Result per item — each .next().await yields Some(Ok(data)) (a frame), Some(Err(e)) (a stream error), or None (the stream ended).

Bring the .next() method into scope with use tokio_stream::StreamExt;.

use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut stream = account
    .on_symbol_tick(pb::OnSymbolTickRequest { symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into()] })
    .await?;                              // outer: opened

while let Some(item) = stream.next().await {
    match item {
        Ok(d) => if let Some(t) = d.symbol_tick { println!("{} {:.5}", t.symbol, t.bid); },
        Err(e) => { eprintln!("stream error: {e}"); break; }
    }
}
// leaving scope drops `stream` → unsubscribes

Every frame carries the apikey + session id metadata automatically, the same as unary calls.

docs.title: The five streams
docs.text:
Available on MT5Account (and wrapped by MT5Service with friendlier args):

MT5Account MT5Service Item Trigger on_symbol_tick(req) stream_ticks(symbols) OnSymbolTickData every tick on_trade(req) stream_trade_updates() OnTradeData on trade events on_position_profit(req) stream_position_profits(ms, ignore_empty) OnPositionProfitData timer on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(req) stream_opened_tickets(ms) OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData timer on_trade_transaction(req) stream_transactions() OnTradeTransactionData on transactions
  • Tick stream pushes on every new tick for the subscribed symbols.
  • Timer streams push every timer_period_milliseconds; on_position_profit also takes ignore_empty_data to suppress no-change frames.
  • Event streams push only when something changes (quiet otherwise).

docs.title: Stopping a stream
docs.text:
Drop it. When the Stream value goes out of scope (loop ends, break, function returns), the subscription is torn down — there's no explicit unsubscribe for these feeds.

let mut s = service.stream_ticks(vec!["EURUSD".into()]).await?;
let mut n = 0;
while let Some(Ok(_)) = s.next().await {
    n += 1;
    if n >= 100 { break; }   // break → drop(s) → unsubscribed
}

Market Depth (DOM) is different — it's a subscribe/read/release trio (market_book_add → market_book_get → market_book_release), not one of these push streams. See Market Depth.

docs.title: 1) Take a fixed number of frames
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;

let mut s = service.stream_ticks(vec!["EURUSD".into()]).await?;
let mut got = 0;
while let Some(item) = s.next().await {
    if let Ok(d) = item { if d.symbol_tick.is_some() { got += 1; } }
    if got >= 10 { break; }
}

docs.title: 2) Stop on a deadline
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

let mut s = service.stream_position_profits(1000, true).await?;
let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(30);
while Instant::now() < deadline {
    match tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(1), s.next()).await {
        Ok(Some(Ok(d))) => { /* handle frame */ let _ = d; }
        Ok(Some(Err(e))) => { eprintln!("err: {e}"); break; }
        Ok(None) => break,            // stream ended
        Err(_elapsed) => continue,    // no frame this second — re-check the deadline
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Cancel from elsewhere (channel / token)
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;

let (tx, mut rx) = tokio::sync::oneshot::channel::<()>();
let mut s = service.stream_trade_updates().await?;

loop {
    tokio::select! {
        _ = &mut rx => break,                 // someone asked us to stop
        item = s.next() => match item {
            Some(Ok(d)) => { let _ = d; }
            _ => break,
        }
    }
}
// elsewhere: let _ = tx.send(());

docs.title: 4) Run a stream in a background task
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;

let mut s = service.stream_ticks(vec!["EURUSD".into()]).await?;
let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
    while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
        if let Some(t) = d.symbol_tick { /* push to a channel, update state, … */ let _ = t; }
    }
});
// ... later ...
handle.abort();   // dropping the task drops the stream → unsubscribes

docs.title: 5) Maintain a live position book
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use std::collections::HashMap;

let mut s = service.stream_position_profits(1000, true).await?;
let mut book: HashMap<i64, f64> = HashMap::new();
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    for p in d.new_positions.iter().chain(d.updated_positions.iter()) { book.insert(p.ticket, p.profit); }
    for p in &d.deleted_positions { book.remove(&p.ticket); }
    println!("floating {:+.2} ({} pos)", book.values().sum::<f64>(), book.len());
}

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
• Don't block the frame loop. Do heavy work off the loop (send to a channel, tokio::spawn), so you keep draining frames promptly.
  • Pick a sane timer period. 500–1000 ms is plenty for dashboards; smaller means more frames and more work.
  • Use ignore_empty_data: true on stream_position_profits to stay quiet when nothing changed.
  • Handle both Result layers. An opened stream can still yield an Err item (e.g. a transient gateway hiccup) — decide whether to break or continue.
  • Snapshot vs stream. For a one-off value, use the unary call (symbol_info_tick, opened_orders); stream only when you need continuous updates.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Likely cause .next() doesn't resolve / method missing Forgot use tokio_stream::StreamExt;. No frames arrive Symbol not selected/synchronized (ticks), or market closed / nothing changed (event streams). Stream "leaks" / keeps running The Stream value is still alive — drop it or abort() its task. Flood of frames Timer period too small, or ignore_empty_data is false.

docs.title: MT5 for Beginners: Your First Steps in Trading
docs.text: Welcome! This guide is for complete beginners who have never worked with MetaTrader 5 or trading. We'll get you from zero to a working demo account you can automate with RustMT5.

docs.title: What is MetaTrader 5 (MT5)?
docs.text:
MetaTrader 5 is a trading platform used by millions of traders worldwide. It lets you:

  • Trade forex, stocks, commodities, and cryptocurrencies
  • Analyze markets with charts and indicators
  • Execute automated trading strategies
  • Monitor your positions in real-time

Think of MT5 as the "cockpit" for the markets. RustMT5 lets you control that cockpit programmatically from Rust, over gRPC.

docs.title: Demo vs Live Account: Start Safely
Why start with a demo account?
docs.text:
A demo account is a risk-free practice account with virtual money. We strongly recommend demo first:

  • ✅ Zero risk — virtual funds (typically $10,000 – $100,000)
  • ✅ Real market conditions — live prices and behavior
  • ✅ Learn the platform — before risking real money
  • ✅ Test your code — perfect for developing RustMT5 apps

docs.title: Live Account
docs.text: A live account uses real money. Only go live once you understand MT5, have tested thoroughly on demo, and understand the risks.

docs.title: Quick Start: Creating a Demo Account
docs.text: The fastest way is to create a demo account directly in the MT5 terminal.

docs.title: Step 1️⃣: Download and install the MT5 terminal
docs.text:
1. Visit https://www.metatrader5.com/en/download
  2. Download the version for your OS (Windows/Mac/Linux)
  3. Install the application

docs.title: Step 2️⃣: Launch MT5 and find the Navigator panel
docs.text:
On first launch a popup usually offers to open a new account. If not, find the Navigator panel (left side, below Market Watch).

Inside Navigator you'll see Accounts, Subscriptions, Indicators, Expert Advisors, and more.

docs.title: Step 3️⃣: Open a new demo account
docs.text:
1. In Navigator, find Accounts
  2. Right-click "Accounts"
  3. Select "Open an account"

docs.title: Step 4️⃣: Select the MetaQuotes demo server
docs.text: In the broker search window, look for "MetaQuotes-Demo" (the standard demo server). Use the search field if needed, select it, and click Next.

docs.title: Step 5️⃣: Account type
docs.text: Choose "Open a new demo account" and click Next.

docs.title: Step 6️⃣: Fill in your details
docs.text: Name, email, account type, virtual deposit (e.g. $10,000), leverage (1:100 is fine to start), currency. Agree to the terms and click Next.

docs.title: Step 7️⃣: Save your credentials
docs.text:
MT5 creates the account and shows:

  • Login — your account number (e.g. 591129415)
  • Password — your master (trading) password
  • Investor Password — read-only password
  • Server — e.g. "MetaQuotes-Demo"

⚠️ Save these now — you need Login, Password, and Server to connect from RustMT5. Click Finish.

docs.title: Step 8️⃣: Connect from RustMT5
docs.text:
There's no config file to edit — you pass the credentials straight to MT5Account::new and connect_by_server_name, and provide your MetaRPC key via the MRPC_API_KEY environment variable.

export MRPC_API_KEY=your_mrpc_token    # from https://mrpc.pro/my

use metarpc_mt5::MT5Account;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // Login, password, grpc_server (None → mt5.mrpc.pro:443)
    let mut account = MT5Account::new(591_129_415, "YourPasswordHere", None);
    account.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;  // exact server name
    let s = account.account_summary().await?;
    println!("balance {:.2} {}", s.account_balance, s.account_currency);
    account.disconnect().await?;
    Ok(())
}
  • Login / password — exactly what MT5 showed you.
  • Server name — the exact string (e.g. "MetaQuotes-Demo").
  • grpc_server / API key — None uses the default endpoint; the key comes from MRPC_API_KEY.

docs.title: Step 9️⃣: Verify the MT5 connection
docs.text: In the MT5 terminal, the bottom-right corner should show a green connection indicator and your balance (e.g. $10,000).

docs.title: Step 🔟: Run it
docs.text:
cargo run

Trades your program makes appear in the MT5 terminal in real time. It's virtual money — experiment freely. See Your First Project for a fuller walkthrough.

docs.title: Master password
docs.text: Full access — open/close trades, change settings. This is the one RustMT5 uses to trade.

docs.title: Investor password
docs.text: View-only — see trades/balance/history but cannot trade. Good for sharing performance or monitoring. Set it via Tools → Options → Server → Change (Investor Password).

docs.title: Choosing a Broker (optional)
docs.text:
The MetaQuotes demo server is fine for practice. For live trading later you may pick a specific broker for better conditions or regional support.

Not financial advice — do your own research. Popular MT5 brokers include IC Markets, Pepperstone, OANDA, XM, RoboForex, FxPro.

What to look for: regulation (FCA/ASIC/CySEC/…), genuine MT5 support (not just MT4), a free demo, tight spreads, responsive support.

docs.title: What's Next?
docs.text:
1. Getting Started — install the crate and make your first calls.
  2. Understand the layers:
  3. MT5Account — low-level gRPC foundation.
  4. MT5Service — typed, friendlier wrappers.
  5. MT5Sugar — high-level one-liners (most beginner-friendly).
  6. Strategies — ready orchestrators and presets.

docs.title: 🛡️ Security
docs.text:
• Never share your master password; use the investor password for monitoring tools.
  • Keep credentials safe (a password manager helps). Don't commit them to a repo.

docs.title: 📊 Risk management
docs.text: • Even on demo, build good habits: always use a stop-loss, risk ≤ 1–2% per trade, understand position sizing (MT5Sugar::calculate_position_size).

docs.title: 🧪 Testing
docs.text: • Test on demo first; verify strategies over weeks/months, not days. Demo results don't guarantee live results.

docs.title: 📚 Education
docs.text: • Trading has a steep learning curve — focus on learning, not earning.

docs.title: Useful commands (Rust)
docs.text:
# add the SDK to a project
cargo add metarpc-mt5
cargo add tokio --features full

# build / run / test
cargo build
cargo run
cargo test

# run a bundled example (see examples/)
cargo run --example strategies_demo

# check your Rust toolchain
rustc --version

Ready to code? Head to Getting Started. Good luck on your trading journey! 🚀

docs.title: 🗺️ RustMT5 Project Map
docs.text: The whole project as one annotated tree, with links. Links point to section overviews, never to individual method pages — open an overview to drill down into its methods.

docs.title: 🧱 The three layers
docs.text:
RustMT5 is built in three decoupled layers (composition, not inheritance). Your code can enter at any level.

Layer Source What it does Overview 3 · MT5Sugar src/mt5/sugar.rs Convenience on top of Service: risk-based sizing, pip-based SL/TP, price/volume helpers, batch close, position queries, history. MT5Sugar overview 2 · MT5Service src/mt5/service.rs Typed facade: &str symbols and typed-enum args; simple getters return clean scalars. What most code uses. MT5Service overview 1 · MT5Account src/mt5/account.rs Low-level gRPC: builds each proto …Request, attaches auth metadata, unwraps replies to Result<…Data, MT5Error>; connection & streaming. Everything builds on it. MT5Account overview 
Your code → MT5Sugar → MT5Service → MT5Account → gRPC → MetaRPC gateway → MT5 terminal

Mix freely: sugar.service() borrows the Service, service.account() borrows the Account.

docs.title: MT5 Return Codes (RetCodes) — Reference
docs.text: How the RustMT5 SDK surfaces MetaTrader 5 trade-server return codes, and what each code means.

docs.title: 🛡️ What is a RetCode?
docs.text:
A RetCode is the status the MT5 trade server returns after a trading operation. It tells you whether the trade succeeded or why it was rejected (no money, invalid stops, market closed, …).

RetCodes appear only on trading calls — order_send / order_modify / order_close (and their Service/Sugar wrappers) — because only those go through the broker and can be rejected. Read-only calls either return data or fail with an MT5Error.

docs.title: The two layers of error
docs.text:
A trading call returns Result<…Data, MT5Error>. There are two things to check:

  1. Did the request reach the server? Err(MT5Error) = transport/gateway failure (not connected, timeout, status). Handle it with ? or a match.
  2. Did the trade succeed? On Ok(data), inspect data.returned_code. 10009 (TRADE_RETCODE_DONE) = success. Anything else is a rejection or partial.
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let res = account.order_send(req).await?;          // ← layer 1: MT5Error on transport failure
if res.returned_code == 10009 {                     // ← layer 2: trade result
    println!("done — order #{}, deal #{}", res.order, res.deal);
} else {
    eprintln!("rejected {}: {}", res.returned_code, res.returned_code_description);
}

docs.title: Result fields that carry the code
docs.text:
OrderSendData / OrderModifyData / OrderCloseData expose:

Field Type Meaning returned_code u32 The numeric RetCode (10009 = done). returned_string_code String The symbolic name (e.g. "TRADE_RETCODE_NO_MONEY"). returned_code_description String Human-readable description from the server.

docs.title: The TRADE_RETCODE_DONE constant
docs.text:
MT5Sugar exposes it, and its boolean helpers use it internally:

use metarpc_mt5::sugar::TRADE_RETCODE_DONE; // = 10009

let ok = sugar.close_position(ticket).await?;  // true  ⇔ returned_code == TRADE_RETCODE_DONE

When a Sugar order helper sees a non-10009 code it raises MT5Error::Api { code, message, mql_code } — so with Sugar you can rely on ? and treat any Ok as a completed trade.

docs.title: ✅ Success & in-flight codes
docs.text:
Code Name Meaning 10008 PLACED Order placed (pending accepted). 10009 DONE Request completed — success. 10010 DONE_PARTIAL Only part of the volume filled. 10004 REQUOTE Price changed — requote offered. 10006 REJECT Request rejected. 10007 CANCEL Cancelled by trader.

Treat 10010 (partial) deliberately: the position/volume may differ from what you asked for.

docs.title: ⚠️ Common rejection codes
docs.text:
Code Name Typical cause / fix 10013 INVALID Malformed request — check required fields. 10014 INVALID_VOLUME Volume off the symbol's min/step/max — round it. 10015 INVALID_PRICE Bad price (e.g. pending on the wrong side of market). 10016 INVALID_STOPS SL/TP inside the stops/freeze level — widen them. 10017 TRADE_DISABLED Trading disabled for the account/symbol. 10018 MARKET_CLOSED Out of trade session — check symbol_info_session_trade. 10019 NO_MONEY Not enough free margin — size down / check margin. 10020 PRICE_CHANGED Price moved past deviation — retry or widen slippage. 10021 PRICE_OFF No quotes to process the request. 10022 INVALID_EXPIRATION Bad pending-order expiration. 10024 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS Throttled — back off. 10025 NO_CHANGES Modify requested no actual change. 10027 CLIENT_DISABLES_AT Autotrading disabled in the client. 10030 INVALID_FILL Unsupported filling mode for the symbol. 10031 CONNECTION No connection to the trade server. 10034 LIMIT_VOLUME Would exceed the volume limit for the symbol. 10036 POSITION_CLOSED The position is already closed. 10040 LIMIT_POSITIONS Max number of open positions reached. 10045 FIFO_CLOSE Account requires FIFO close order. Full numeric range (10004–10045) `10004 REQUOTE · 10006 REJECT · 10007 CANCEL · 10008 PLACED · 10009 DONE · 10010 DONE_PARTIAL · 10011 ERROR · 10012 TIMEOUT · 10013 INVALID · 10014 INVALID_VOLUME · 10015 INVALID_PRICE · 10016 INVALID_STOPS · 10017 TRADE_DISABLED · 10018 MARKET_CLOSED · 10019 NO_MONEY · 10020 PRICE_CHANGED · 10021 PRICE_OFF · 10022 INVALID_EXPIRATION · 10023 ORDER_CHANGED · 10024 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS · 10025 NO_CHANGES · 10026 SERVER_DISABLES_AT · 10027 CLIENT_DISABLES_AT · 10028 LOCKED · 10029 FROZEN · 10030 INVALID_FILL · 10031 CONNECTION · 10032 ONLY_REAL · 10033 LIMIT_ORDERS · 10034 LIMIT_VOLUME · 10035 INVALID_ORDER · 10036 POSITION_CLOSED · 10038 INVALID_CLOSE_VOLUME · 10039 CLOSE_ORDER_EXIST · 10040 LIMIT_POSITIONS · 10041 REJECT_CANCEL · 10042 LONG_ONLY · 10043 SHORT_ONLY · 10044 CLOSE_ONLY · 10045 FIFO_CLOSE`

Note: order_check (and MT5Sugar::can_open_position) use retcode 0 as the "would succeed" signal for the check, which is distinct from the send success code 10009.

docs.title: Low-level: branch on the code
docs.text:
let res = account.order_send(req).await?;
match res.returned_code {
    10009 => println!("done #{}", res.order),
    10019 => eprintln!("no money — size down"),
    10016 => eprintln!("invalid stops — widen SL/TP"),
    10018 => eprintln!("market closed"),
    other => eprintln!("rejected {other}: {}", res.returned_code_description),
}

docs.title: High-level: let Sugar convert to an error
docs.text:
// Sugar maps non-10009 to MT5Error::Api, so `?` handles rejections:
let ticket = sugar.buy_market_with_pips(None, 0.10, Some(20.0), Some(40.0), "x", 1).await?;

docs.title: Retry on transient codes
docs.text:
let transient = |c: u32| matches!(c, 10004 | 10020 | 10021 | 10024 | 10031);
// re-fetch price and resend on a transient code, with a small backoff and a retry cap.

docs.title: Async Model — How RustMT5 Executes
docs.text: The SDK is async-only, built on tokio. There is no blocking/sync API — this guide shows how to run it and when to use streams vs unary calls.

docs.title: 🎯 The short version
docs.text:
Every API method is async fn returning a Result (or, for subscriptions, a Stream). You run them inside a tokio runtime and .await them. There are no synchronous wrappers — if you need a blocking call, drive the future yourself (e.g. tokio::runtime::Runtime::block_on).

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let mut account = metarpc_mt5::MT5Account::new(12_345_678, "password", None);
    account.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;
    let s = account.account_summary().await?;
    println!("balance {:.2}", s.account_balance);
    account.disconnect().await?;
    Ok(())
}

docs.title: Unary vs streaming
docs.text:
Unary call Stream Shape async fn … -> Result<Data, MT5Error> async fn … -> Result<impl Stream<Item = Result<Data, MT5Error>>, MT5Error> Returns one value, once many frames over time Use for snapshots: balance, a quote, place/modify/close live feeds: ticks, trade events, position P/L Examples account_summary, symbol_info_tick, order_send on_symbol_tick, on_position_profit

Consume a stream with tokio_stream::StreamExt — see gRPC Streaming.

docs.title: Running concurrently
docs.text:
Because calls are futures, you can run independent ones together instead of sequentially:

// fetch three quotes concurrently
let (a, b, c) = tokio::join!(
    sugar.bid(Some("EURUSD")),
    sugar.bid(Some("GBPUSD")),
    sugar.bid(Some("USDJPY")),
);
println!("{:.5} {:.5} {:.5}", a?, b?, c?);

Run background work (e.g. a stream consumer) with tokio::spawn; cancel it with the task handle's abort().

One shared connection. MT5Account holds one channel/session. Prefer concurrency via join!/spawn over opening many accounts; the gateway tracks one terminal session per connection.

docs.title: Driving async from a sync context
docs.text:
If you must call the SDK from non-async code:

let rt = tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()?;
let summary = rt.block_on(async {
    let mut acc = metarpc_mt5::MT5Account::new(12_345_678, "password", None);
    acc.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;
    acc.account_summary().await
})?;

docs.title: 💡 Guidance
docs.text:
• Production bots, multi-symbol, GUIs/services → embrace async: #[tokio::main], join!, spawn, streams.
  • Quick scripts / one-offs → still async, just a small #[tokio::main] wrapper (or block_on).
  • Never block the runtime inside an async fn (no std::thread::sleep; use tokio::time::sleep).

docs.title: Your First Project in 10 Minutes
docs.text: Hands-on quick start — a working MetaTrader 5 bot in Rust, from empty folder to a live balance print and a demo trade.

docs.title: Step 0 — Get an API key
docs.text:
To reach MetaRPC (mt5.mrpc.pro:443):

  1. Register free at https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Generate a token in the portal at https://mrpc.pro/my.
  3. Expose it to your program: export MRPC_API_KEY=your_token (the SDK reads MRPC_API_KEY, falling back to "TRIAL").

You also need an MT5 demo account (login, password, server name) — see MT5 for Beginners.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create the project
docs.text:
cargo new my_rustmt5_bot
cd my_rustmt5_bot
cargo add metarpc-mt5
cargo add tokio --features full

docs.title: Step 2 — Write src/main.rs
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::{MT5Account, MT5Service, MT5Sugar};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // 1) construct: user, password, grpc_server (None → mt5.mrpc.pro:443)
    let account = MT5Account::new(12_345_678, "your-mt5-password", None);

    // 2) wrap in the high-level API, with a default symbol
    let mut sugar = MT5Sugar::new(MT5Service::new(account)).with_default_symbol("EURUSD");

    // 3) connect by broker cluster name (timeout seconds)
    sugar.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;

    // 4) read the account
    let info = sugar.get_account_info().await?;
    println!("#{}  balance {:.2} {}  equity {:.2}",
        info.login, info.balance, info.currency, info.equity);

    // 5) a quote
    println!("EURUSD bid/ask {:.5}/{:.5}", sugar.bid(None).await?, sugar.ask(None).await?);

    // 6) (optional, DEMO ONLY) a tiny risk-sized trade with a 20/40 pip bracket
    // let lots = sugar.calculate_position_size("EURUSD", 1.0, 20.0).await?;
    // let ticket = sugar.buy_market_with_pips(None, lots, Some(20.0), Some(40.0), "first", 1001).await?;
    // println!("opened #{ticket}");

    sugar.disconnect(false).await?;
    Ok(())
}

Replace the login/password/server with your demo credentials. Keep the trade block commented until you're on a demo account you're happy to trade.

docs.title: Step 3 — Run
docs.text:
cargo run

Expected output (values vary):

#12345678  balance 10000.00 USD  equity 10000.00
EURUSD bid/ask 1.08512/1.08531

If you see a connection error, re-check the server name, credentials and MRPC_API_KEY.

docs.title: MT5Account — Master Overview
docs.text:
One page to orient fast: the low-level async gRPC client for MetaTrader 5. Jump to any group overview or method spec from here.

MT5Account is Layer 1 — direct gRPC/protobuf calls to the MT5 terminal gateway. MT5Service (typed facade) and MT5Sugar (high-level helpers) build on top of it.

It exposes 39 feature methods across 6 groups (plus connection helpers). Defined in src/mt5/account.rs.

MT5 is richer than MT4: positions and deals are separate from orders, there is a Market Book (DOM), and pre-trade order_check / order_calc_* calculators.

docs.title: 🚦 Start here — Section Overviews
docs.text:
• 1. Account Information — Overview Balance/equity/margin/leverage, a complete snapshot or single typed properties.
  • 2. Symbol Information — Overview Quotes (ticks), symbol properties, trading rules, Market Watch select, bar history.
  • 3. Positions & Orders — Overview Open positions, pending orders, their ticket lists, and closed-deal/order history.
  • 4. Market Depth (DOM) — Overview Level-II order book: subscribe, read, release.
  • 5. Trading Operations — Overview Send/modify/close orders, pre-trade check and margin/profit calculators.
  • 6. Streaming Methods — Overview Real-time server streams: ticks, trade events, position profit, ticket lists, transactions.

docs.title: 🧭 How to pick a method
docs.text: If you need… Group Typical methods Account snapshot Account Information account_summary, account_info_double/integer/string Quotes & symbol properties Symbol Information symbol_info_tick, symbol_info_double, symbols_total, symbol_params_many Bar history Symbol Information price_history Current positions & orders Positions & Orders positions_total, opened_orders, opened_orders_tickets Historical trades Positions & Orders order_history, positions_history Tick value for P/L Positions & Orders tick_value_with_size Level-II / order book Market Depth market_book_add, market_book_get, market_book_release Trading operations Trading Operations order_send, order_modify, order_close Pre-trade calculations Trading Operations order_check, order_calc_margin, order_calc_profit Real-time updates Streaming Methods on_symbol_tick, on_trade, on_position_profit

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (Rust, async)
docs.text:
MT5Account is async (tokio): each call returns the reply's typed …Data payload, or an MT5Error. Every request carries the apikey + terminal id metadata automatically.

use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use metarpc_mt5::MT5Account;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // user, password, grpc_server (None -> mt5.mrpc.pro:443), api key from MRPC_API_KEY / "TRIAL"
    let mut account = MT5Account::new(12_345_678, "password", None);
    account.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;

    let s = account.account_summary().await?;
    println!("{} {} eq {:.2}", s.account_balance, s.account_currency, s.account_equity);

    let tick = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
    println!("bid/ask {:.5}/{:.5}", tick.bid, tick.ask);

    account.disconnect().await?;
    Ok(())
}

docs.title: 🧱 How the call contract works
docs.text:
Every feature method:

  1. builds the protobuf …Request,
  2. attaches the apikey + id metadata (authed),
  3. calls the right tonic service client,
  4. unwraps the reply — each …Reply carries a oneof { data, error }, returned as Result<…Data, MT5Error>.

So you always get the typed …Data directly, never a raw reply to inspect by hand. A few low-level methods take a raw …Request (MT5's requests often have many fields); friendly argument shapes live in MT5Service and MT5Sugar.

docs.title: 🔐 Constructor & connection
docs.text:
MT5Account::new(user: u64, password: impl Into<String>, grpc_server: Option<String>) -> MT5Account

Connect by broker server name or explicit host/port:

account.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;   // by cluster name
account.connect_by_host_port("mt5.broker.com", 443, 30).await?; // by address

The gateway assigns a terminal session id on connect (account.id()), reused on every later call. reconnect() re-establishes it; disconnect() drops the channel.

docs.title: 🧩 Layer map
docs.text:
Layer Type What it adds 1 — low-level MT5Account raw gRPC, auto-metadata, typed …Data returns 2 — facade MT5Service friendly args (property enums, symbols), clean values 3 — high-level MT5Sugar order construction, pip math, risk sizing, positions

See also: Getting Started · Return Codes · ENUMs Reference

docs.title: 1. Account Information — Overview
docs.text:
The account's money picture: a one-call snapshot, plus single typed properties (double/integer/string).

These four methods are read-only. They live on the mt5_term_api.AccountHelper (account_summary) and mt5_term_api.AccountInformation (account_info_*) gRPC services and return a typed …Data payload.

docs.title: Methods in this group
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner account_summary() AccountSummaryData Balance, equity, leverage, currency, trade mode, server time — one round-trip. account_info_double(req) AccountInfoDoubleData One double property (balance, equity, margin, profit, …). account_info_integer(req) AccountInfoIntegerData One integer property (login, leverage, trade mode, …). account_info_string(req) AccountInfoStringData One string property (currency, company, name, server).

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text:
• Startup banner / general overview / pre-trade snapshot → account_summary() (one round-trip for balance, equity, leverage, currency, …).
  • A single live value not in the summary (e.g. ACCOUNT_MARGIN, ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE, ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL, ACCOUNT_PROFIT) → account_info_double(property).
  • A single integer/string property → account_info_integer / account_info_string.

Note: AccountSummaryData carries balance/equity/credit but not the margin fields on this gateway — read those with account_info_double(ACCOUNT_MARGIN…). This is exactly the kind of thing the SDK's MT5Sugar::margin() / free_margin() wrap for you.

Back to: MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Account Info — Double
docs.text:
Read one floating-point account property (balance, equity, margin, profit, …) by its property id.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::account_info_double(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountInformation
  • RPC: AccountInfoDouble(AccountInfoDoubleRequest) -> AccountInfoDoubleReply
  • Payload: AccountInfoDoubleData → single field requested_value: f64

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The MQL5 AccountInfoDouble(property) call — one double property at a time.
  • Why you need it. The money properties not in account_summary live here: margin, free margin, margin level, live profit.
  • When to use. A single live value — e.g. check free margin before sizing a trade. For the whole picture at once, prefer account_summary().

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Read margin / free margin / margin level (missing from the summary)
  • Read live ACCOUNT_PROFIT (floating P/L)
  • Read any single double account property on demand

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn account_info_double(
    &self,
    request: pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest,
) -> Result<pb::AccountInfoDoubleData, MT5Error>

Request message:

message AccountInfoDoubleRequest {
  AccountInfoDoublePropertyType property_id = 1;
}

Reply message:

message AccountInfoDoubleReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountInfoDoubleData data = 1;
    Error error = 2;
  }
}

message AccountInfoDoubleData {
  double requested_value = 1;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description property_id i32 (AccountInfoDoublePropertyType) Which double property to read. Pass PropertyType::X as i32.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountInfoDoubleData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description requested_value f64 The property's value, in the account's deposit currency (or percent for margin level).

docs.title: 🧱 AccountInfoDoublePropertyType (from proto)
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning AccountBalance 0 Balance in deposit currency AccountCredit 1 Credit in deposit currency AccountProfit 2 Current floating profit AccountEquity 3 Equity in deposit currency AccountMargin 4 Margin used AccountMarginFree 5 Free margin AccountMarginLevel 6 Margin level, percent AccountMarginSoCall 7 Margin-call level (percent or currency, per SO mode) AccountMarginSoSo 8 Stop-out level (percent or currency, per SO mode) AccountMarginInitial 9 Initial margin reserved for pending orders AccountMarginMaintenance 10 Maintenance margin for open positions AccountAssets 11 Current assets AccountLiabilities 12 Current liabilities AccountCommissionBlocked 13 Blocked commission

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• This is where margin lives. AccountMargin, AccountMarginFree, AccountMarginLevel are not in AccountSummaryData — read them here.
  • Margin level is a percent, not currency (e.g. 842.0 means 842 %). The rest are in the deposit currency.
  • Need several values? One account_summary() beats four account_info_double() calls for the fields it already carries (balance, equity, credit).
  • Higher layers wrap this. MT5Service::account_double(prop) returns the bare f64; MT5Sugar::margin() / free_margin() / margin_level() name the common ones.

docs.title: 1) Free margin before sizing a trade
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::AccountInfoDoublePropertyType as P;

let req = pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest { property_id: P::AccountMarginFree as i32 };
let free = account.account_info_double(req).await?.requested_value;
println!("free margin: {free:.2}");
if free < 100.0 { println!("[WARN] not enough free margin"); }

docs.title: 2) Margin level (percent) as a health gauge
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::AccountInfoDoublePropertyType as P;

let lvl = account
    .account_info_double(pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest { property_id: P::AccountMarginLevel as i32 })
    .await?
    .requested_value;
println!("margin level: {lvl:.1}%");
if lvl != 0.0 && lvl < 200.0 { println!("[ALERT] margin level below 200% — reduce exposure"); }

docs.title: 3) Live floating profit
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::AccountInfoDoublePropertyType as P;

let profit = account
    .account_info_double(pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest { property_id: P::AccountProfit as i32 })
    .await?
    .requested_value;
println!("floating P/L: {profit:+.2}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Pass the enum as i32. The field is property_id: i32; use P::AccountMargin as i32, not the enum value directly.
  • Margin level units. It's a percent — don't compare it against a currency threshold.
  • Flat account. With no open positions AccountMargin is 0.0 and AccountMarginLevel is typically 0.0 (no division) — guard against the zero case before alerting.
  • One property per call. For a snapshot of many, use account_summary().

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Balance parity. account_info_double(AccountBalance) equals account_summary().account_balance.
  • With a position open. AccountMargin > 0 and AccountMarginFree < AccountEquity.
  • Profit sign. Open a losing position → AccountProfit is negative.

docs.title: Account Info — Integer
docs.text:
Read one integer account property (login, leverage, trade mode, permission flags, …) by its property id.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::account_info_integer(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountInformation

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The MQL5 AccountInfoInteger(property) call — one integer property at a time.
  • Why you need it. Identity and permissions: login, leverage, trade mode, and the boolean flags (trade_allowed, trade_expert, FIFO/hedging) that gate whether you may trade at all.
  • When to use. A pre-flight check before trading, or to read leverage for position sizing.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Read account identity (login) and leverage
  • Read trade mode (DEMO / CONTEST / REAL) as an enum value
  • Read permission flags: trade_allowed, trade_expert, FIFO, hedging
  • Read margin mode / stop-out mode / currency digits

docs.text:
pub async fn account_info_integer(
    &self,
    request: pb::AccountInfoIntegerRequest,

Request message:

message AccountInfoIntegerRequest {
  AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType property_id = 1;
}

Reply message:

message AccountInfoIntegerReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountInfoIntegerData data = 1;
    Error error = 2;
  }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description property_id i32 (AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType) Which integer property to read. Pass PropertyType::X as i32.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountInfoIntegerData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description requested_value i64 The property's value. Booleans come back as 1 / 0; enum properties as the enum's integer value.

docs.title: 🧱 AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType (from proto)
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning Decode as AccountLogin 0 Account number i64 AccountTradeMode 1 Trade mode MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode (0 demo / 1 contest / 2 real) AccountLeverage 2 Leverage i64 (e.g. 100) AccountLimitOrders 3 Max open positions + pending (0 = unlimited) i64 AccountMarginSoMode 4 Stop-out mode ENUM_ACCOUNT_STOP_OUT_MODE AccountTradeAllowed 5 Trading allowed for the account bool (1/0) AccountTradeExpert 6 Trading allowed for an EA bool (1/0) AccountMarginMode 7 Margin calculation mode ENUM_ACCOUNT_MARGIN_MODE AccountCurrencyDigits 8 Decimal places in account currency i64 AccountFifoClose 9 Positions must close FIFO bool (1/0) AccountHedgeAllowed 10 Opposite positions on one symbol allowed bool (1/0)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Booleans are integers. AccountTradeAllowed, AccountTradeExpert, AccountFifoClose, AccountHedgeAllowed return 1 (true) or 0 (false) — compare with == 1 or != 0.
  • Enum properties return the enum's number. AccountTradeMode returns 0/1/2 — decode with MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode::try_from(v as i32).
  • Pre-trade gate. Before sending orders, confirm AccountTradeAllowed == 1 and (for automated trading) AccountTradeExpert == 1.
  • Leverage for sizing. AccountLeverage here matches account_summary().account_leverage.

docs.title: 1) Pre-trade permission gate
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType as P;

async fn can_trade(account: &metarpc_mt5::MT5Account) -> Result<bool, metarpc_mt5::MT5Error> {
    let allowed = account
        .account_info_integer(pb::AccountInfoIntegerRequest { property_id: P::AccountTradeAllowed as i32 })
        .await?.requested_value;
    let expert = account
        .account_info_integer(pb::AccountInfoIntegerRequest { property_id: P::AccountTradeExpert as i32 })
        .await?.requested_value;
    Ok(allowed == 1 && expert == 1)
}

docs.title: 2) Trade mode via the enum
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::{AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType as P, MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode as Mode};

let v = account
    .account_info_integer(pb::AccountInfoIntegerRequest { property_id: P::AccountTradeMode as i32 })
    .await?.requested_value;
match Mode::try_from(v as i32) {
    Ok(Mode::MrpcAccountTradeModeReal) => println!("REAL account — be careful"),
    Ok(Mode::MrpcAccountTradeModeContest) => println!("contest account"),
    _ => println!("demo account"),
}

docs.title: 3) Leverage for position sizing
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType as P;

let lev = account
    .account_info_integer(pb::AccountInfoIntegerRequest { property_id: P::AccountLeverage as i32 })
    .await?.requested_value;
println!("leverage 1:{lev}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Pass the enum as i32. property_id: P::AccountLeverage as i32.
  • Don't treat bool properties as counts. AccountTradeAllowed is 1/0, not a quantity.
  • Enum decode needs as i32. requested_value is i64; MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode::try_from wants i32.
  • AccountLimitOrders == 0 means unlimited, not "zero orders allowed".

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Login parity. account_info_integer(AccountLogin) equals the user you constructed MT5Account with and account_summary().account_login.
  • Demo flags. On a demo account AccountTradeAllowed is usually 1; AccountTradeMode decodes to MrpcAccountTradeModeDemo.
  • Leverage parity. Matches account_summary().account_leverage.

docs.text:
• What it is. The MQL5 AccountInfoString(property) call — one text property at a time.

  • When to use. Building a header/banner, or reading ACCOUNT_CURRENCY to format money. Most of these are also in account_summary().

• Read the account owner's name
  • Read the broker/company and trade server names
  • Read the deposit currency (for formatting money amounts)

docs.text:

use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let name = account
    .account_info_string(pb::AccountInfoStringRequest { property_id: P::AccountName as i32 })

docs.text:
• Pass the enum as i32. property_id: P::AccountCurrency as i32.
  • Possible empty strings. Some brokers leave a field blank; guard before using it as a label.
  • AccountServer is here, not in the summary. If you need the server name, this is the only place to read it.

• Currency parity. account_info_string(AccountCurrency) equals account_summary().account_currency.
  • Name parity. AccountName equals account_summary().account_user_name.

docs.title: Account Summary (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
Complete account snapshot — balance, equity, leverage, currency, trade mode, server time — in a single call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::account_summary() (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: AccountSummary(AccountSummaryRequest) -> AccountSummaryReply
  • Payload: AccountSummaryData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One call that returns every essential account property.
  • Why you need it. The most efficient way to read balance/equity/leverage/currency at once — one round-trip instead of many single-property account_info_* calls.
  • When to use. At session start (banner / sanity check), and before any risk decision or order. For a single property not included here (e.g. margin), use account_info_double.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• RECOMMENDED way to read account state
  • Balance, equity, credit in one round-trip
  • Login, owner name, broker/company
  • Leverage and trade mode (DEMO / CONTEST / REAL)
  • Currency and server time (+ UTC offset)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn account_summary(&self) -> Result<AccountSummaryData, MT5Error>

No arguments. Returns the typed payload, or an MT5Error.

Request message:

message AccountSummaryRequest {}

Reply message:

message AccountSummaryReply {
  oneof response {
    AccountSummaryData data = 1;
    Error error = 2;
  }
}

message AccountSummaryData {
  int64  account_login = 1;
  double account_balance = 2;
  double account_equity = 3;
  string account_user_name = 4;
  int64  account_leverage = 5;
  MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode account_trade_mode = 6;
  string account_company_name = 7;
  string account_currency = 8;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp server_time = 9;
  int64  utc_timezone_server_time_shift_minutes = 10;
  double account_credit = 11;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: None. account_summary() takes no parameters.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountSummaryData
docs.text:
Fields are plain public fields on the prost struct (snake_case, same as the proto):

Field Rust type Description account_login i64 Account number account_balance f64 Balance in deposit currency (excludes floating P/L) account_equity f64 Equity = balance + floating P/L of open positions account_user_name String Account owner account_leverage i64 Leverage (e.g. 100 = 1:100) account_trade_mode i32 (MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode) DEMO / CONTEST / REAL account_company_name String Broker name account_currency String Deposit currency (e.g. USD) server_time Option<Timestamp> Current server time utc_timezone_server_time_shift_minutes i64 Server offset from UTC, minutes account_credit f64 Credit in deposit currency

This gateway's AccountSummaryData does not carry margin / free-margin / margin-level — read those with account_info_double (ACCOUNT_MARGIN, ACCOUNT_MARGIN_FREE, ACCOUNT_MARGIN_LEVEL) or the high-level MT5Sugar::margin() / free_margin() / margin_level().

docs.title: MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode — field account_trade_mode
docs.text:
Variant Value Meaning MrpcAccountTradeModeDemo 0 Demo / practice account MrpcAccountTradeModeContest 1 Contest account MrpcAccountTradeModeReal 2 Real (live) account

The stored field is an i32; compare via MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode::try_from(data.account_trade_mode).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One call beats many. account_summary() returns balance, equity, leverage and currency together — don't fan out into several account_info_* calls for these.
  • balance vs equity. Balance ignores open positions; equity includes their floating P/L. On a flat account they're equal; equity − balance is your current floating P/L.
  • Money is in the deposit currency. Every monetary field is in account_currency.
  • Server time. server_time is a protobuf Timestamp (Option); utc_timezone_server_time_shift_minutes is the broker's offset from UTC.
  • Snapshot, not a stream. Re-query before a risk check; for live equity/profit use on_position_profit.

docs.title: 1) Session-start banner
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode as Mode;

let s = account.account_summary().await?;
let mode = match Mode::try_from(s.account_trade_mode) {
    Ok(Mode::MrpcAccountTradeModeReal) => "REAL",
    Ok(Mode::MrpcAccountTradeModeContest) => "CONTEST",
    _ => "DEMO",
};
println!("Account #{} ({mode})  {}", s.account_login, s.account_company_name);
println!("Balance {:.2} {}  Equity {:.2}  (floating {:+.2})",
    s.account_balance, s.account_currency, s.account_equity, s.account_equity - s.account_balance);
println!("Leverage 1:{}", s.account_leverage);

docs.title: 2) Floating P/L from the snapshot
docs.text:
let s = account.account_summary().await?;
let floating = s.account_equity - s.account_balance;
println!("floating P/L: {floating:+.2} {}", s.account_currency);

docs.title: 3) Equity / drawdown monitor
docs.text:
let mut peak: Option<f64> = None;
loop {
    let eq = account.account_summary().await?.account_equity;
    let p = peak.map_or(eq, |pk| pk.max(eq));
    peak = Some(p);
    let dd = if p > 0.0 { (p - eq) / p * 100.0 } else { 0.0 };
    println!("equity {eq:.2}  peak {p:.2}  drawdown {dd:.2}%");
    if dd >= 10.0 { println!("[ALERT] drawdown ≥ 10% — de-risk"); break; }
    tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5)).await;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• No margin fields here. account_margin / account_margin_free / account_margin_level are not in this payload on this gateway — use account_info_double.
  • Snapshot, not live. Equity is a point-in-time read; don't cache it across time.
  • Currency mismatch. All money fields are in account_currency; converting an instrument's P/L into account currency is on you.
  • Trade mode is an i32. Convert with MrpcEnumAccountTradeMode::try_from(..) before matching.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Happy path (demo). Fields populated; account_currency non-empty; on a flat account equity == balance.
  • With open positions. equity != balance and the difference equals the summed floating P/L.
  • Trade mode. On a demo account account_trade_mode decodes to MrpcAccountTradeModeDemo.

docs.title: 2. Symbol Information — Overview
docs.text:
Everything about an instrument: does it exist, is it in Market Watch, its live tick, its properties and trading rules, session times, and bar history.

These methods are read-only (except symbol_select, which toggles Market Watch visibility). Most live on the mt5_term_api.MarketInfo gRPC service and return a typed …Data payload.

docs.title: Discovery & Market Watch
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner symbols_total(req) SymbolsTotalData How many symbols exist (all, or Market-Watch-only). symbol_exist(req) SymbolExistData Does a symbol name exist (and is it custom)? symbol_name(req) SymbolNameData Symbol name by index. symbol_select(req) SymbolSelectData Add / remove a symbol in Market Watch. symbol_is_synchronized(req) SymbolIsSynchronizedData Is the symbol's data synced with the server? symbol_list(req) SymbolListData The full list of symbol names.

docs.title: Quote (tick)
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner symbol_info_tick(req) MrpcMqlTick Latest tick: bid, ask, last, volume, time.

docs.title: Properties (one at a time)
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner symbol_info_double(req) SymbolInfoDoubleData One double property (point, bid, ask, volume step, …). symbol_info_integer(req) SymbolInfoIntegerData One integer property (digits, spread, trade mode, …). symbol_info_string(req) SymbolInfoStringData One string property (base/profit currency, description, …). symbol_info_margin_rate(req) SymbolInfoMarginRateData Initial/maintenance margin rates for an order type.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner symbol_info_session_quote(req) SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData Quote session window for a weekday. symbol_info_session_trade(req) SymbolInfoSessionTradeData Trade session window for a weekday.

docs.title: Bulk & history
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner symbol_params_many(req) SymbolParamsManyData Many symbols' full parameter sets in one call. price_history(req) PriceHistoryData OHLC bar history for a symbol/timeframe range.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text:
• "Is this symbol tradable right now?" → symbol_exist → symbol_select (make sure it's in Market Watch) → symbol_info_tick.
  • One live number (point size, digits, spread, volume step) → symbol_info_double / symbol_info_integer.
  • Everything about one symbol at once → symbol_params_many (pass a single name) — far fewer round-trips than many symbol_info_* calls.
  • Candles / backtest input → price_history.
  • Is the market open? → symbol_info_session_trade for today's weekday.

The single-property symbol_info_* calls mirror MQL5's SymbolInfoDouble/Integer/String. When you need several properties, symbol_params_many is the efficient choice — and MT5Service / MT5Sugar wrap the common ones (point, digits, bid, ask) for you.

Back to: MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Price History (Bars)
docs.text:
OHLC candle history for a symbol and timeframe — the input for charts, indicators and backtests.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::price_history(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: PriceHistory(PriceHistoryRequest) -> PriceHistoryReply
  • Payload: PriceHistoryData → bars: Vec<PriceBar>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 CopyRates-style bar history.
  • Why you need it. Candles for analysis: moving averages, ranges, swing highs/lows, backtests.
  • When to use. Any time you need historical OHLC. Make sure the symbol is selected and synchronized first.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn price_history(
    &self,
    request: pb::PriceHistoryRequest,
) -> Result<pb::PriceHistoryData, MT5Error>

Request message:

message PriceHistoryRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  int32  timeframe = 2;   // MQL5 ENUM_TIMEFRAMES value (PERIOD_M1=1, PERIOD_H1=16385, PERIOD_D1=16408)
  int64  from_time = 3;   // Unix seconds; both 0 = newest max_bars bars
  int64  to_time = 4;     // Unix seconds
  int32  max_bars = 5;    // upper bound (defaults to 500); terminal has its own ceiling
}

Reply payload:

message PriceHistoryData { repeated PriceBar bars = 1; }

message PriceBar {
  int64  time = 1;         // Unix seconds, bar open
  double open = 2;
  double high = 3;
  double low = 4;
  double close = 5;
  int64  tick_volume = 6;
  int32  spread = 7;
  int64  real_volume = 8;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol name (selected & synchronized). timeframe i32 MQL5 ENUM_TIMEFRAMES value — see table below. from_time i64 Range start, Unix seconds. 0 + to_time 0 → newest bars. to_time i64 Range end, Unix seconds. max_bars i32 Cap on returned bars (default 500); don't request a decade of M1.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — PriceHistoryData.bars: Vec<PriceBar>
docs.text: Field Rust type Description time i64 Bar open time, Unix seconds. open / high / low / close f64 OHLC prices. tick_volume i64 Number of ticks in the bar. spread i32 Spread at bar close, points. real_volume i64 Exchange volume (0 for pure FX).

docs.title: ⏱️ Common timeframe values (MQL5 ENUM_TIMEFRAMES)
docs.text: Constant Value Constant Value M1 1 H1 16385 M5 5 H4 16388 M15 15 D1 16408 M30 30 W1 32769 MN1 49153

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Newest bars shortcut. Leave from_time and to_time at 0 to get the newest max_bars bars — what opening a chart does.
  • Respect the ceiling. The terminal caps bar counts (ERR_HISTORY_BARS_LIMIT); page by narrowing the time range if you need more.
  • Select + sync first. Call symbol_select and wait for symbol_is_synchronized to avoid empty/partial history.
  • Times are Unix seconds — convert to DateTime for display.

docs.title: 1) Last 100 H1 bars
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let data = account.price_history(pb::PriceHistoryRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    timeframe: 16385, // H1
    from_time: 0, to_time: 0,
    max_bars: 100,
}).await?;
println!("{} bars", data.bars.len());
if let Some(b) = data.bars.last() {
    println!("latest close {:.5} @ {}", b.close, b.time);
}

docs.title: 2) A specific date range of D1 bars
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let from = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp() - 30 * 86_400; // 30 days ago
let data = account.price_history(pb::PriceHistoryRequest {
    symbol: "XAUUSD".into(),
    timeframe: 16408, // D1
    from_time: from, to_time: chrono::Utc::now().timestamp(),
    max_bars: 500,
}).await?;
for b in &data.bars {
    println!("{}  O{:.2} H{:.2} L{:.2} C{:.2}", b.time, b.open, b.high, b.low, b.close);
}

docs.title: 3) Simple SMA(close, 20)
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let bars = account.price_history(pb::PriceHistoryRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(), timeframe: 16385, from_time: 0, to_time: 0, max_bars: 50,
}).await?.bars;
let n = 20.min(bars.len());
if n > 0 {
    let sma: f64 = bars.iter().rev().take(n).map(|b| b.close).sum::<f64>() / n as f64;
    println!("SMA({n}) = {sma:.5}");
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Empty bars. Symbol not selected/synchronized, or the range falls outside available history.
  • Asking for too much. A wide range on a small timeframe hits the bar-count ceiling — narrow it or raise granularity.
  • Timeframe is a raw i32. Use the MQL5 constant values above, not an ordinal.
  • Bar order. Iterate by time; don't assume a particular ordering — sort if you depend on it.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Count cap. With max_bars: 100, bars.len() <= 100.
  • OHLC sanity. For each bar low <= open,close <= high.
  • Latest vs tick. The last D1 close is near the current symbol_info_tick bid/ask.

docs.title: Symbol Exist
docs.text:
Does a symbol name exist on this server — and is it a custom (synthetic) symbol?

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_exist(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolExist(SymbolExistRequest) -> SymbolExistReply
  • Payload: SymbolExistData → exists: bool, is_custom: bool

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A name check against the broker's standard and custom symbols.
  • Why you need it. Validate user input before you try to select, quote, or trade a symbol.
  • When to use. First step of "can I trade X?" — then symbol_select → symbol_info_tick.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_exist(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolExistRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolExistData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolExistRequest { string name = 1; }
message SymbolExistData {
  bool exists = 1;     // found among standard or custom symbols
  bool is_custom = 2;  // the found symbol is custom (synthetic)
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description name String Exact symbol name to check (case-sensitive on most servers).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolExistData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description exists bool true if the symbol exists (standard or custom). is_custom bool true if the existing symbol is a custom/synthetic one.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Existence ≠ visibility. A symbol can exist but not be in Market Watch — call symbol_select before quoting it.
  • Names are broker-specific. EURUSD on one server may be EURUSD.m or EURUSD-5 on another; check first.

docs.title: 1) Validate before trading
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let e = account.symbol_exist(pb::SymbolExistRequest { name: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
if !e.exists {
    println!("no such symbol — check the broker's naming");
    return Ok(());
}
println!("exists{}", if e.is_custom { " (custom)" } else { "" });

docs.title: 2) Resolve a preferred name with fallbacks
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

async fn pick(account: &metarpc_mt5::MT5Account, names: &[&str]) -> Option<String> {
    for n in names {
        if account.symbol_exist(pb::SymbolExistRequest { name: (*n).into() }).await.ok()?.exists {
            return Some((*n).to_string());
        }
    }
    None
}
let sym = pick(&account, &["EURUSD", "EURUSD.m", "EURUSD-5"]).await;
println!("using {sym:?}");

docs.title: 3) Flag custom symbols
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let e = account.symbol_exist(pb::SymbolExistRequest { name: "MyIndex".into() }).await?;
if e.exists && e.is_custom { println!("MyIndex is synthetic — prices may be derived"); }

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Case & suffix sensitivity. eurusd may not match EURUSD; brokers add suffixes.
  • exists == false is not an error. It's a valid answer — don't treat it as a failure to retry.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Known-good. A symbol you can see in the terminal returns exists == true.
  • Nonsense name. "NOPE123" returns exists == false, is_custom == false.

docs.title: Symbol Info — Double
docs.text:
Read one floating-point symbol property (point size, bid/ask, tick value/size, volume limits, swaps, margins).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_info_double(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolInfoDouble(SymbolInfoDoubleRequest) -> SymbolInfoDoubleReply
  • Payload: SymbolInfoDoubleData → value: f64

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolInfoDouble(symbol, property) — one double property.
  • Why you need it. point, tick_value, tick_size, volume_min/step are the constants pip math and lot rounding depend on.
  • When to use. Sizing and price rounding. For many properties at once, use symbol_params_many.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_info_double(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolInfoDoubleData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolInfoDoubleRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  SymbolInfoDoubleProperty type = 2;   // Rust field: r#type (i32)
}
message SymbolInfoDoubleData { double value = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol name. r#type i32 (SymbolInfoDoubleProperty) Which property. Pass Prop::X as i32. Note the raw-ident r#type.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoDoubleData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description value f64 The property value.

docs.title: 🧱 SymbolInfoDoubleProperty — common values (from proto)
docs.text:
Variant Value Meaning SymbolBid 0 Current bid SymbolAsk 3 Current ask SymbolLast 6 Last deal price SymbolPoint 13 Point size (smallest price step) SymbolTradeTickValue 14 Tick value (profit) in deposit currency SymbolTradeTickValueProfit 15 Tick value for a winning position SymbolTradeTickValueLoss 16 Tick value for a losing position SymbolTradeTickSize 17 Minimal price change SymbolTradeContractSize 18 Contract size (e.g. 100000 for FX) SymbolVolumeMin 22 Minimal lot SymbolVolumeMax 23 Maximal lot SymbolVolumeStep 24 Lot step SymbolVolumeLimit 25 Max aggregate volume per direction SymbolSwapLong 26 Long swap SymbolSwapShort 27 Short swap SymbolMarginInitial 35 Initial margin per lot SymbolMarginMaintenance 36 Maintenance margin per lot

This enum has ~40 variants (session open/close, day highs/lows, swaps per weekday, option strike, …). The full set lives in the proto SymbolInfoDoubleProperty and the ENUMs reference.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Pip math needs SymbolPoint + digits. A "pip" is usually 10 × point on 5-digit FX; read SYMBOL_DIGITS via symbol_info_integer.
  • Lot rounding uses VolumeMin/VolumeStep/VolumeMax. Round computed lots to the step and clamp to [min, max].
  • TickValue for P/L. Money-per-tick-per-lot; the P/L-focused tick_value_with_size bundles value + size.

docs.title: 1) Point size
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoDoubleProperty as D;

let point = account
    .symbol_info_double(pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), r#type: D::SymbolPoint as i32 })
    .await?.value;
println!("point = {point}");  // e.g. 0.00001

docs.title: 2) Volume constraints for lot rounding
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoDoubleProperty as D;

async fn vol(account: &metarpc_mt5::MT5Account, sym: &str, p: D) -> f64 {
    account.symbol_info_double(pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest { symbol: sym.into(), r#type: p as i32 })
        .await.map(|d| d.value).unwrap_or(0.0)
}
let (min, step, max) = (
    vol(&account, "EURUSD", D::SymbolVolumeMin).await,
    vol(&account, "EURUSD", D::SymbolVolumeStep).await,
    vol(&account, "EURUSD", D::SymbolVolumeMax).await,
);
let raw = 0.137;
let lots = ((raw / step).round() * step).clamp(min, max);
println!("rounded lots: {lots:.2}");

docs.title: 3) Contract size & tick value
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoDoubleProperty as D;

let cs = account.symbol_info_double(pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), r#type: D::SymbolTradeContractSize as i32 }).await?.value;
let tv = account.symbol_info_double(pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), r#type: D::SymbolTradeTickValue as i32 }).await?.value;
println!("contract {cs}, tick value {tv}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• The field is r#type. It's a Rust keyword; use the raw identifier r#type: in the struct literal.
  • Pass the enum as i32 (D::SymbolPoint as i32).
  • Point ≠ pip. On 5-digit quotes a pip is 10 points — don't conflate them.
  • One property per call. Many properties → symbol_params_many.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Point sanity. EURUSD SymbolPoint is 0.00001 (5-digit) or 0.0001 (4-digit).
  • Bid parity. SymbolBid ≈ symbol_info_tick().bid.
  • Volume rule. VolumeMin <= VolumeStep × k <= VolumeMax.
