docs.title: Symbol Info — Integer
docs.text:
Read one integer symbol property (digits, spread, trade mode, stops level, flags, times).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_info_integer(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolInfoInteger(SymbolInfoIntegerRequest) -> SymbolInfoIntegerReply
  • Payload: SymbolInfoIntegerData → value: i64

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolInfoInteger(symbol, property) — one integer property.
  • Why you need it. SYMBOL_DIGITS scales every price you print; SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL is the minimum SL/TP distance the broker enforces.
  • When to use. Price formatting, SL/TP validation, checking whether a symbol is tradable.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_info_integer(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolInfoIntegerRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolInfoIntegerData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolInfoIntegerRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  SymbolInfoIntegerProperty type = 2;   // Rust field: r#type (i32)
}
message SymbolInfoIntegerData { int64 value = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol name. r#type i32 (SymbolInfoIntegerProperty) Which property. Pass Prop::X as i32.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoIntegerData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description value i64 The property value (booleans as 1/0, enums as their number, times as Unix seconds).

docs.title: 🧱 SymbolInfoIntegerProperty — common values (from proto)
docs.text:
Variant Value Meaning SymbolSelect 7 Is selected in Market Watch (bool) SymbolVisible 8 Is visible in Market Watch (bool) SymbolTime 15 Time of last quote (Unix seconds) SymbolTimeMsc 16 Time of last quote (ms) SymbolDigits 17 Decimal places in the price SymbolSpreadFloat 18 Floating spread? (bool) SymbolSpread 19 Current spread, points SymbolTradeCalcMode 21 Contract price calc mode (enum) SymbolTradeMode 22 Trade permission mode (enum) SymbolStartTime 23 Trading start date (futures) SymbolExpirationTime 24 Trading end date (futures) SymbolTradeStopsLevel 25 Min SL/TP distance from price, points SymbolTradeFreezeLevel 26 Freeze distance, points SymbolTradeExemode 27 Deal execution mode (enum) SymbolFillingMode 32 Allowed fill modes (bit flags) SymbolOrderMode 33 Allowed order types (bit flags)

~37 variants total (sector/industry, session counts, swap mode, option fields, …). Full set in the proto SymbolInfoIntegerProperty / the ENUMs reference.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• SymbolDigits formats prices. Use it as the precision when printing bid/ask ({:.*} with digits as usize).
  • SymbolTradeStopsLevel gates SL/TP. Stops closer than this many points are rejected — validate before order_send.
  • Booleans are 1/0. SymbolSelect, SymbolVisible, SymbolSpreadFloat → compare == 1.
  • Enum properties return the number. Decode SymbolTradeMode against the matching proto enum.

docs.title: 1) Format prices with the symbol's digits
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoIntegerProperty as I;

let digits = account
    .symbol_info_integer(pb::SymbolInfoIntegerRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), r#type: I::SymbolDigits as i32 })
    .await?.value as usize;
let bid = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?.bid;
println!("bid {bid:.*}", digits);

docs.title: 2) Validate an SL distance against stops level
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoIntegerProperty as I;

let stops = account
    .symbol_info_integer(pb::SymbolInfoIntegerRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), r#type: I::SymbolTradeStopsLevel as i32 })
    .await?.value;
let my_sl_points = 8;
if (my_sl_points as i64) < stops { println!("SL too tight: min {stops} points"); }

docs.title: 3) Current spread in points
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoIntegerProperty as I;

let spread = account
    .symbol_info_integer(pb::SymbolInfoIntegerRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), r#type: I::SymbolSpread as i32 })
    .await?.value;
println!("spread: {spread} points");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• The field is r#type (raw identifier).
  • Pass the enum as i32.
  • Times are Unix seconds (SymbolTime, SymbolStartTime) — convert before display.
  • Ignoring stops/freeze level. The commonest cause of "invalid stops" order rejections.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Digits. EURUSD returns 5 (or 4); JPY pairs return 3 (or 2).
  • Spread ≥ 0. And roughly (ask − bid) / point.
  • Selected flag. After symbol_select(sym, true), SymbolSelect == 1.

docs.title: Symbol Info — Margin Rate
docs.text:
The initial and maintenance margin rates for a symbol and order type — multipliers on the base margin.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_info_margin_rate(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolInfoMarginRate(SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest) -> SymbolInfoMarginRateReply
  • Payload: SymbolInfoMarginRateData → maintenance_margin_rate, initial_margin_rate

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolInfoMarginRate(symbol, order_type, initial, maintenance) — the rate pair.
  • Why you need it. Margin can differ by direction (buy vs sell) and order type; these rates scale the reserved amount.
  • When to use. Pre-trade margin estimates. For the actual currency amount, prefer order_calc_margin.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_info_margin_rate(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolInfoMarginRateData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  EnumOrderType order_type = 2;   // Rust field: order_type (i32)
}
message SymbolInfoMarginRateData {
  double maintenance_margin_rate = 1;
  double initial_margin_rate = 2;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol name. order_type i32 (EnumOrderType) Order type (e.g. buy/sell). Pass EnumOrderType::X as i32.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoMarginRateData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description initial_margin_rate f64 Multiplier on the initial margin (deposit to open 1 lot). maintenance_margin_rate f64 Multiplier on the maintenance margin (min to keep 1 lot open).

docs.title: 🧱 EnumOrderType (field order_type)
docs.text: Variant Value Variant Value OrderTypeBuy 0 OrderTypeSellStop 5 OrderTypeSell 1 OrderTypeBuyStopLimit 6 OrderTypeBuyLimit 2 OrderTypeSellStopLimit 7 OrderTypeSellLimit 3 OrderTypeCloseBy 8 OrderTypeBuyStop 4

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Rates, not amounts. Multiply by the symbol's base margin (SYMBOL_MARGIN_INITIAL / SYMBOL_MARGIN_MAINTENANCE from symbol_info_double) to get currency.
  • Direction-dependent. Buy and sell can carry different rates — query the type you'll actually trade.
  • Want the real number? order_calc_margin returns the margin in account currency for a concrete volume and price.

docs.title: 1) Rates for a buy
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::EnumOrderType as OT;

let r = account
    .symbol_info_margin_rate(pb::SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest {
        symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
        order_type: OT::OrderTypeBuy as i32,
    })
    .await?;
println!("initial rate {}, maintenance rate {}", r.initial_margin_rate, r.maintenance_margin_rate);

docs.title: 2) Compare buy vs sell
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::EnumOrderType as OT;

async fn rate(account: &metarpc_mt5::MT5Account, sym: &str, t: OT) -> f64 {
    account.symbol_info_margin_rate(pb::SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest { symbol: sym.into(), order_type: t as i32 })
        .await.map(|d| d.initial_margin_rate).unwrap_or(0.0)
}
let buy = rate(&account, "EURUSD", OT::OrderTypeBuy).await;
let sell = rate(&account, "EURUSD", OT::OrderTypeSell).await;
println!("initial: buy {buy}, sell {sell}");

docs.title: 3) Estimate initial margin (rate × base)
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::{EnumOrderType as OT, SymbolInfoDoubleProperty as D};

let rate = account.symbol_info_margin_rate(pb::SymbolInfoMarginRateRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), order_type: OT::OrderTypeBuy as i32 }).await?.initial_margin_rate;
let base = account.symbol_info_double(pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), r#type: D::SymbolMarginInitial as i32 }).await?.value;
println!("≈ initial margin per lot: {:.2}", rate * base);  // prefer order_calc_margin for the exact figure

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Rate ≠ money. A rate of 1.0 doesn't mean "1 unit of currency" — multiply by the base margin, or use order_calc_margin.
  • Pass order_type as i32.
  • Zero rates. Some symbols/types return 0.0 where the broker uses the base margin as-is.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• FX majors. Initial rate is typically 1.0 (full base margin).
  • Direction symmetry. For plain FX, buy and sell rates usually match.

docs.text:
• order_calc_margin · symbol_info_double
  • Back to: Symbol Information — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Symbol Info — Session Quote
docs.text:
The quote-session window (open → close) for a symbol on a given weekday and session index.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_info_session_quote(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolInfoSessionQuote(SymbolInfoSessionQuoteRequest) -> SymbolInfoSessionQuoteReply
  • Payload: SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData → from, to

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolInfoSessionQuote(symbol, day, session, from, to) — when quotes are provided.
  • Why you need it. Know when prices update for a symbol on each weekday (distinct from when you can trade).
  • When to use. Building a session calendar / "is the market quoting now?" display. For trade hours use symbol_info_session_trade.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_info_session_quote(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolInfoSessionQuoteRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolInfoSessionQuoteRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  DayOfWeek day_of_week = 2;   // Rust field: day_of_week (i32)
  uint32 session_index = 3;    // 0-based
}
message SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData {
  google.protobuf.Timestamp from = 1;   // seconds since 00:00 (ignore the date part)
  google.protobuf.Timestamp to = 2;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol name. day_of_week i32 (DayOfWeek) Weekday. Pass DayOfWeek::X as i32. session_index u32 Session number for that day, starting at 0.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description from Option<Timestamp> Session start — time of day (ignore the date). to Option<Timestamp> Session end — time of day.

docs.title: 🧱 DayOfWeek (from proto)
docs.text: Variant Value Sunday 0 Monday 1 Tuesday 2 Wednesday 3 Thursday 4 Friday 5 Saturday 6

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Date is meaningless. Only the time-of-day part of from/to matters — take seconds-since-midnight.
  • Multiple sessions per day. Increment session_index from 0; an error/empty means no more sessions.
  • Quote ≠ trade. A symbol may quote outside tradable hours — compare with symbol_info_session_trade.

docs.title: 1) Monday's first quote session
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::DayOfWeek as Dow;

let s = account.symbol_info_session_quote(pb::SymbolInfoSessionQuoteRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    day_of_week: Dow::Monday as i32,
    session_index: 0,
}).await?;
if let (Some(f), Some(t)) = (s.from, s.to) {
    println!("quote session: {}..{} (secs of day)", f.seconds % 86_400, t.seconds % 86_400);
}

docs.title: 2) Enumerate all sessions for a day
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::DayOfWeek as Dow;

for idx in 0..8u32 {
    match account.symbol_info_session_quote(pb::SymbolInfoSessionQuoteRequest {
        symbol: "EURUSD".into(), day_of_week: Dow::Tuesday as i32, session_index: idx,
    }).await {
        Ok(s) if s.from.is_some() => println!("session {idx}: ok"),
        _ => break,
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Format as HH:MM
docs.text:
let secs = 3_600 * 8 + 60 * 30; // example
println!("{:02}:{:02}", secs / 3600, (secs % 3600) / 60);

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Treating the date as real. Use seconds % 86_400 for time-of-day.
  • Pass day_of_week as i32.
  • Assuming one session. FX often has a single long session; exchanges may have several.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Weekday present. Monday, index 0 returns a from/to pair on a liquid FX symbol.
  • Weekend empty. Saturday/Sunday sessions may be absent — your loop stops at index 0.

docs.title: Symbol Info — Session Trade
docs.text:
The trade-session window (open → close) for a symbol on a given weekday and session index.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_info_session_trade(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolInfoSessionTrade(SymbolInfoSessionTradeRequest) -> SymbolInfoSessionTradeReply
  • Payload: SymbolInfoSessionTradeData → from, to

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolInfoSessionTrade(...) — when you can actually trade.
  • Why you need it. Avoid sending orders when the market is closed; schedule entries around session boundaries.
  • When to use. "Is X tradable right now?" and session calendars. For quote hours use symbol_info_session_quote.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_info_session_trade(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolInfoSessionTradeRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolInfoSessionTradeData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolInfoSessionTradeRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  DayOfWeek day_of_week = 2;   // Rust field: day_of_week (i32)
  uint32 session_index = 3;    // 0-based
}
message SymbolInfoSessionTradeData {
  google.protobuf.Timestamp from = 1;   // time of day; ignore the date
  google.protobuf.Timestamp to = 2;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol name. day_of_week i32 (DayOfWeek) Weekday (Sunday=0 … Saturday=6). session_index u32 Session number for that day, starting at 0.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoSessionTradeData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description from Option<Timestamp> Trade-session start — time of day. to Option<Timestamp> Trade-session end — time of day.

docs.title: 🧱 DayOfWeek (field day_of_week)
docs.text: Variant Value Variant Value Sunday 0 Thursday 4 Monday 1 Friday 5 Tuesday 2 Saturday 6 Wednesday 3

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• This gates orders. Outside trade sessions, order_send will be rejected — check here first if a symbol "won't trade".
  • Same shape as the quote session, different meaning: trade hours are usually a subset of quote hours.
  • Time-of-day only. Use seconds % 86_400.

docs.title: 1) Is EURUSD tradable now (rough check)?
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::DayOfWeek as Dow;
use chrono::{Datelike, Timelike, Utc};

let now = Utc::now();
let dow = match now.weekday().num_days_from_sunday() { // 0=Sun..6=Sat
    0 => Dow::Sunday, 1 => Dow::Monday, 2 => Dow::Tuesday, 3 => Dow::Wednesday,
    4 => Dow::Thursday, 5 => Dow::Friday, _ => Dow::Saturday,
};
let s = account.symbol_info_session_trade(pb::SymbolInfoSessionTradeRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(), day_of_week: dow as i32, session_index: 0,
}).await?;
if let (Some(f), Some(t)) = (s.from, s.to) {
    let now_secs = (now.hour() * 3600 + now.minute() * 60 + now.second()) as i64;
    let open = (f.seconds % 86_400..=t.seconds % 86_400).contains(&now_secs);
    println!("tradable now: {open}");
}

docs.title: 2) All trade sessions for Friday
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::DayOfWeek as Dow;

for idx in 0..8u32 {
    match account.symbol_info_session_trade(pb::SymbolInfoSessionTradeRequest {
        symbol: "XAUUSD".into(), day_of_week: Dow::Friday as i32, session_index: idx,
    }).await {
        Ok(s) if s.from.is_some() => println!("Fri session {idx}"),
        _ => break,
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Pre-trade guard
docs.text: // Combine with symbol_info_session_trade before order_send to skip closed markets.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Confusing with quote sessions. Quotes can tick while trading is closed.
  • Date part. Ignore it; use time-of-day.
  • Pass day_of_week as i32.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Weekday open. EURUSD Monday, 0 returns a valid window.
  • Weekend closed. Saturday typically has no trade session (index 0 empty/err).

docs.title: Symbol Info — String
docs.text:
Read one string symbol property (base/profit/margin currency, description, path, ISIN, …).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_info_string(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolInfoString(SymbolInfoStringRequest) -> SymbolInfoStringReply
  • Payload: SymbolInfoStringData → value: String

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolInfoString(symbol, property) — one text property.
  • Why you need it. Currencies for P/L conversion, a human description for UI, the Market-Watch path for grouping.
  • When to use. Labelling instruments and figuring out which currency a symbol's profit is in.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_info_string(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolInfoStringRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolInfoStringData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolInfoStringRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  SymbolInfoStringProperty type = 2;   // Rust field: r#type (i32)
}
message SymbolInfoStringData { string value = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol name. r#type i32 (SymbolInfoStringProperty) Which property. Pass Prop::X as i32.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolInfoStringData

docs.title: 🧱 SymbolInfoStringProperty (from proto — full set)
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning SymbolBasis 0 Underlying asset of a derivative SymbolCategory 1 Category/sector name SymbolCountry 2 Country SymbolSectorName 3 Economic sector SymbolIndustryName 4 Industry branch SymbolCurrencyBase 5 Base currency SymbolCurrencyProfit 6 Profit currency SymbolCurrencyMargin 7 Margin currency SymbolBank 8 Quote feeder SymbolDescription 9 Human-readable description SymbolExchange 10 Exchange name SymbolFormula 11 Custom-symbol pricing formula SymbolIsin 12 ISIN code SymbolPage 13 Info web page SymbolPath 14 Path in the symbol tree

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Profit currency matters for P/L. If SymbolCurrencyProfit differs from your account currency, P/L needs conversion.
  • SymbolDescription for UI. Friendlier than the raw symbol code.
  • SymbolPath for grouping. E.g. Forex\Majors\EURUSD — split on \ to build a tree.
  • Fields can be empty. Not every broker fills every property.

docs.title: 1) Currencies of a symbol
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoStringProperty as S;

async fn str_prop(account: &metarpc_mt5::MT5Account, sym: &str, p: S) -> String {
    account.symbol_info_string(pb::SymbolInfoStringRequest { symbol: sym.into(), r#type: p as i32 })
        .await.map(|d| d.value).unwrap_or_default()
}
let base   = str_prop(&account, "EURUSD", S::SymbolCurrencyBase).await;
let profit = str_prop(&account, "EURUSD", S::SymbolCurrencyProfit).await;
println!("base {base}, profit {profit}");

docs.title: 2) Description for a label
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoStringProperty as S;

let desc = account
    .symbol_info_string(pb::SymbolInfoStringRequest { symbol: "XAUUSD".into(), r#type: S::SymbolDescription as i32 })
    .await?.value;
println!("XAUUSD — {desc}");

docs.title: 3) Does profit currency match the account?
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoStringProperty as S;

let prof = account.symbol_info_string(pb::SymbolInfoStringRequest { symbol: "USDJPY".into(), r#type: S::SymbolCurrencyProfit as i32 }).await?.value;
let acct = account.account_summary().await?.account_currency;
if prof != acct { println!("P/L in {prof}, account in {acct} — conversion applies"); }

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• The field is r#type (raw identifier).
  • Pass the enum as i32.
  • Empty strings are valid. Guard before using as a label.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• EURUSD. SymbolCurrencyBase == "EUR", SymbolCurrencyProfit == "USD".
  • Description present. Major symbols return a non-empty SymbolDescription.

docs.title: Symbol Info Tick (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
The latest tick for a symbol: bid, ask, last, volume and timestamps — the quote you trade against.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_info_tick(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolInfoTick(SymbolInfoTickRequest) -> SymbolInfoTickReply
  • Payload: MrpcMqlTick

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolInfoTick(symbol, tick) — one fresh quote.
  • Why you need it. Current bid/ask drives every price decision: spread, entry, SL/TP distances, P/L.
  • When to use. Right before sizing or sending an order; for a one-off price. For a live feed use on_symbol_tick.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• Current bid / ask (and spread = ask − bid)
  • Last deal price and its volume (exchange instruments)
  • Precise update time (time_msc, milliseconds)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_info_tick(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest,
) -> Result<pb::MrpcMqlTick, MT5Error>

Request message:

message SymbolInfoTickRequest { string symbol = 1; }

Reply payload — MrpcMqlTick:

message MrpcMqlTick {
  int64  time = 1;         // Unix seconds, last update
  double bid = 2;
  double ask = 3;
  double last = 4;         // last deal price
  uint64 volume = 5;       // volume for the last price
  int64  time_msc = 6;     // last update, milliseconds
  uint32 flags = 7;        // tick flags
  double volume_real = 8;  // higher-accuracy volume
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol name (must be selected in Market Watch).

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — MrpcMqlTick
docs.text: Field Rust type Description time i64 Last update, Unix seconds. bid f64 Best sell price. ask f64 Best buy price. last f64 Last deal price (0 for pure FX with no exchange last). volume u64 Volume for the last price. time_msc i64 Last update, Unix milliseconds. flags u32 Bitmask of what changed (bid/ask/last/volume). volume_real f64 Volume with greater accuracy.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Spread = ask − bid, in price units; divide by point (from symbol_info_double) for spread in points.
  • FX last is often 0. Use bid/ask; last/volume matter mainly for exchange instruments.
  • Two timestamps. time is seconds, time_msc is milliseconds — use time_msc to order ticks precisely.
  • Select first. On many servers you must symbol_select the symbol before the tick is populated.

docs.title: 1) Bid / ask / spread
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let t = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
println!("bid {:.5}  ask {:.5}  spread {:.5}", t.bid, t.ask, t.ask - t.bid);

docs.title: 2) Spread in points
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::SymbolInfoDoubleProperty as D;

let t = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
let point = account
    .symbol_info_double(pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), r#type: D::SymbolPoint as i32 })
    .await?.value;
println!("spread: {:.1} points", (t.ask - t.bid) / point);

docs.title: 3) Freshness check
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let t = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
let age_ms = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp_millis() - t.time_msc;
if age_ms > 5_000 { println!("[WARN] quote is {age_ms} ms old — market may be closed"); }

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Empty tick (all zeros). Usually means the symbol isn't selected or isn't synchronized yet.
  • Dividing by point you didn't fetch. Get point/digits from symbol_info_double/integer for the right scale.
  • Snapshot, not a stream. Each call is one quote; for continuous updates subscribe with on_symbol_tick.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• During market hours. bid > 0, ask >= bid, time_msc close to now.
  • Weekend / closed. Values present but time/time_msc stale — your freshness check fires.

docs.title: Symbol Is Synchronized
docs.text:
Is the symbol's data in sync with the trade server? Check before trusting prices or history.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_is_synchronized(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolIsSynchronized(SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest) -> SymbolIsSynchronizedReply
  • Payload: SymbolIsSynchronizedData → synchronized: bool

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolIsSynchronized(symbol) — a readiness flag.
  • Why you need it. Just-selected symbols may not have their specs/history loaded yet; acting too early gives stale or empty data.
  • When to use. After symbol_select, poll this until true before reading history or trading.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_is_synchronized(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolIsSynchronizedData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest { string symbol = 1; }
message SymbolIsSynchronizedData    { bool synchronized = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol name.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolIsSynchronizedData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description synchronized bool true once the symbol's data matches the server.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Select first. This is meaningful only after the symbol is in Market Watch.
  • Poll with a timeout. Sync usually completes in well under a second; loop with a short sleep and a deadline rather than forever.

docs.title: 1) Wait for sync after selecting
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

account.symbol_select(pb::SymbolSelectRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), select: true }).await?;

let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5);
loop {
    let s = account
        .symbol_is_synchronized(pb::SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() })
        .await?.synchronized;
    if s { break; }
    if Instant::now() >= deadline { println!("[WARN] not synchronized in time"); break; }
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(200)).await;
}

docs.title: 2) Guard a history read
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

if account.symbol_is_synchronized(pb::SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?.synchronized {
    // safe to call price_history now
}

docs.title: 3) Quick boolean helper
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

async fn synced(account: &metarpc_mt5::MT5Account, sym: &str) -> bool {
    account.symbol_is_synchronized(pb::SymbolIsSynchronizedRequest { symbol: sym.into() })
        .await.map(|d| d.synchronized).unwrap_or(false)
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Polling forever. Always bound the wait with a deadline.
  • Reading history before sync. You may get empty or partial bars — check this first.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• After select. On a live demo, synchronized becomes true within a second or two.
  • Unselected symbol. May report false (or error) — select it first.

docs.title: Symbol List
docs.text:
The full list of symbol names in one call — no index walking.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_list(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolList(SymbolListRequest) -> SymbolListReply
  • Payload: SymbolListData → symbols: Vec<String>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. All symbol names at once.
  • Why you need it. One round-trip instead of symbols_total + N × symbol_name.
  • When to use. Populating a picker, searching names, or snapshotting the universe.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_list(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolListRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolListData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolListRequest {}                       // no fields
message SymbolListData { repeated string symbols = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: None — SymbolListRequest is empty. Pass pb::SymbolListRequest {}.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolListData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description symbols Vec<String> Every symbol name known to the terminal.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One call beats the loop. Prefer this over symbols_total + symbol_name when you want the whole list.
  • Client-side filtering. Filter/sort the returned Vec in Rust (.iter().filter(..)).
  • Can be large. Thousands of entries on some brokers — don't print them all to a UI unfiltered.

docs.title: 1) Get and count
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let list = account.symbol_list(pb::SymbolListRequest {}).await?.symbols;
println!("{} symbols", list.len());

docs.title: 2) Filter FX majors
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let list = account.symbol_list(pb::SymbolListRequest {}).await?.symbols;
let majors: Vec<_> = list.into_iter()
    .filter(|s| ["EURUSD", "GBPUSD", "USDJPY", "USDCHF"].iter().any(|m| s.starts_with(m)))
    .collect();
println!("{majors:?}");

docs.title: 3) Does a name exist (client-side)?
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let list = account.symbol_list(pb::SymbolListRequest {}).await?.symbols;
let has = list.iter().any(|s| s == "XAUUSD");
println!("XAUUSD present: {has}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Existence vs visibility. The list includes symbols not in Market Watch — still symbol_select before quoting.
  • Memory. The Vec can be big; filter early.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Length vs total. symbol_list().symbols.len() ≈ symbols_total(false).total.
  • Membership. A name from the list passes symbol_exist.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• symbols_total · symbol_name · symbol_params_many
  • Back to: Symbol Information — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Symbol Name
docs.text:
The symbol name at a given index — the companion to symbols_total for enumerating symbols.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_name(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolName(SymbolNameRequest) -> SymbolNameReply
  • Payload: SymbolNameData → name: String

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolName(index, selected) — name by position.
  • Why you need it. To iterate the symbol list without fetching every property.
  • When to use. Building a symbol picker; usually prefer symbol_list for the whole list in one call.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_name(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolNameRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolNameData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolNameRequest {
  int32 index = 1;     // ordinal position
  bool  selected = 2;  // true = index into Market Watch list; false = full list
}
message SymbolNameData { string name = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description index i32 Zero-based position in the chosen list. selected bool true → Market Watch list; false → full symbol list.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolNameData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description name String The symbol name at that index.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Bound it with symbols_total. Valid index range is 0..symbols_total(selected).total.
  • Keep selected consistent. The index means different things for the Market-Watch list vs the full list.
  • One call per index. For the whole set, symbol_list is a single round-trip.

docs.title: 1) Name at an index
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let name = account.symbol_name(pb::SymbolNameRequest { index: 0, selected: true }).await?.name;
println!("first Market-Watch symbol: {name}");

docs.title: 2) Full enumeration
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let total = account.symbols_total(pb::SymbolsTotalRequest { mode: false }).await?.total;
for i in 0..total {
    let name = account.symbol_name(pb::SymbolNameRequest { index: i, selected: false }).await?.name;
    if name.starts_with("EUR") { println!("{name}"); }
}

docs.title: 3) Index → name map for the Market Watch
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use std::collections::BTreeMap;

let n = account.symbols_total(pb::SymbolsTotalRequest { mode: true }).await?.total;
let mut map = BTreeMap::new();
for i in 0..n {
    let name = account.symbol_name(pb::SymbolNameRequest { index: i, selected: true }).await?.name;
    map.insert(i, name);
}
println!("{map:#?}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Out-of-range index. index >= total is an error — always bound with symbols_total first.
  • selected mismatch. Indexing the full list while reading counts for Market Watch gives the wrong names.
  • N calls = N round-trips. For the full list prefer symbol_list.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Round-trip. symbol_name(0, true) returns a name that symbol_exist confirms exists.
  • Range. symbol_name(total-1, false) succeeds; symbol_name(total, false) errors.

docs.title: Symbol Params Many (RECOMMENDED for bulk)
docs.text:
Full parameter sets for many symbols (or one) in a single, paged call — every property without a call per field.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_params_many(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: SymbolParamsMany(SymbolParamsManyRequest) -> SymbolParamsManyReply
  • Payload: SymbolParamsManyData → symbol_infos: Vec<SymbolParameters>, paging fields

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A bulk fetch of the whole SymbolParameters record for each symbol.
  • Why you need it. One round-trip replaces dozens of symbol_info_double/integer/string calls.
  • When to use. Caching symbol specs at startup, or reading one symbol's complete spec at once.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_params_many(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolParamsManyRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolParamsManyData, MT5Error>

Request message:

message SymbolParamsManyRequest {
  optional string symbol_name = 1;                 // one symbol; omit for all
  optional AhSymbolParamsManySortType sort_type = 2;
  optional int32 page_number = 3;                  // 0-based
  optional int32 items_per_page = 4;
}
message SymbolParamsManyData {
  repeated SymbolParameters symbol_infos = 1;
  int32 symbols_total = 2;
  optional int32 page_number = 3;
  optional int32 items_per_page = 4;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input (all optional)
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol_name Option<String> A single symbol; None → all symbols. sort_type Option<i32> (AhSymbolParamsManySortType) Sort order (see enum). page_number Option<i32> 0-based page index for paging. items_per_page Option<i32> Page size.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolParamsManyData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description symbol_infos Vec<SymbolParameters> One full record per symbol on this page. symbols_total i32 Total matching symbols (across all pages). page_number Option<i32> Echoed page index. items_per_page Option<i32> Echoed page size.

docs.title: SymbolParameters — a flat record of the symbol's spec
docs.text:
It carries the full property set in one struct (same values as the symbol_info_* calls). Commonly used fields:

Field Rust type Description name String Symbol name bid / ask / last f64 Current prices point f64 Point size volume_real f64 Last volume … plus digits, spread, contract size, volume min/max/step, swaps, margins, currencies, description, path and more

The struct mirrors MQL5's symbol properties; read the field you need directly instead of issuing a symbol_info_* call per property.

docs.title: 🧱 AhSymbolParamsManySortType (from proto)
docs.text: Variant Value Order AhParamsManySortTypeSymbolNameAsc 0 By name, ascending AhParamsManySortTypeSymbolNameDesc 1 By name, descending AhParamsManySortTypeMqlIndexAsc 2 By MQL index, ascending AhParamsManySortTypeMqlIndexDesc 3 By MQL index, descending

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One symbol, full spec. Pass symbol_name: Some("EURUSD") to get a single complete record — far cheaper than many single-property calls.
  • Page large universes. With None, set items_per_page and loop page_number until you've read symbols_total.
  • Cache it. Specs change rarely; read once at startup and keep the records.

docs.title: 1) One symbol's complete spec
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let data = account.symbol_params_many(pb::SymbolParamsManyRequest {
    symbol_name: Some("EURUSD".into()),
    sort_type: None, page_number: None, items_per_page: None,
}).await?;
if let Some(p) = data.symbol_infos.first() {
    println!("{}: bid {:.5} ask {:.5} point {}", p.name, p.bid, p.ask, p.point);
}

docs.title: 2) First page, sorted by name
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::AhSymbolParamsManySortType as Sort;

let data = account.symbol_params_many(pb::SymbolParamsManyRequest {
    symbol_name: None,
    sort_type: Some(Sort::AhParamsManySortTypeSymbolNameAsc as i32),
    page_number: Some(0),
    items_per_page: Some(50),
}).await?;
println!("{} of {} total", data.symbol_infos.len(), data.symbols_total);
for p in data.symbol_infos.iter().take(5) { println!("{}", p.name); }

docs.title: 3) Page through everything
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let page_size = 100;
let mut page = 0;
let mut seen = 0;
loop {
    let d = account.symbol_params_many(pb::SymbolParamsManyRequest {
        symbol_name: None, sort_type: None,
        page_number: Some(page), items_per_page: Some(page_size),
    }).await?;
    seen += d.symbol_infos.len() as i32;
    if d.symbol_infos.is_empty() || seen >= d.symbols_total { break; }
    page += 1;
}
println!("read {seen} symbol records");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Options are Option<..>. Wrap values (Some(..)), use None to omit.
  • Forgetting to page. With None and no page size you may get only the first page — check symbols_total.
  • Over-fetching. Pulling every record each tick is wasteful; cache.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Single-symbol parity. symbol_infos[0].point equals symbol_info_double(SymbolPoint).
  • Paging completeness. Summed page lengths reach symbols_total.

docs.text:
• symbol_info_double · symbol_info_integer · symbol_list

docs.title: Symbol Select
docs.text:
Add a symbol to Market Watch (or remove it) — the switch that makes quotes and history available.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbol_select(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolSelect(SymbolSelectRequest) -> SymbolSelectReply
  • Payload: SymbolSelectData → success: bool

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolSelect(symbol, select) — the only write in this group.
  • Why you need it. Many quote/history calls require the symbol to be in Market Watch first.
  • When to use. Right after confirming the symbol exists, before symbol_info_tick / price_history.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_select(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolSelectRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolSelectData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolSelectRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  bool   select = 2;   // true = add to Market Watch, false = remove
}
message SymbolSelectData { bool success = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol name. select bool true → add/select; false → remove from Market Watch.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolSelectData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description success bool false on failure (e.g. removing a symbol with an open position/chart).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Select before you quote. On many servers symbol_info_tick / price_history only work for selected symbols.
  • Removal can refuse. A symbol can't be removed while its chart is open or it has open positions — success comes back false.
  • Idempotent-ish. Selecting an already-selected symbol just returns success == true.

docs.title: 1) Ensure a symbol is ready to quote
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let ok = account
    .symbol_select(pb::SymbolSelectRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), select: true })
    .await?.success;
if !ok { println!("could not add EURUSD to Market Watch"); }
let tick = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
println!("bid {:.5}", tick.bid);

docs.title: 2) Exists → select → quote pipeline
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let sym = "GBPUSD";
if account.symbol_exist(pb::SymbolExistRequest { name: sym.into() }).await?.exists {
    account.symbol_select(pb::SymbolSelectRequest { symbol: sym.into(), select: true }).await?;
    let t = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: sym.into() }).await?;
    println!("{sym} {:.5}/{:.5}", t.bid, t.ask);
}

docs.title: 3) Tidy up — remove a symbol
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let ok = account
    .symbol_select(pb::SymbolSelectRequest { symbol: "GBPUSD".into(), select: false })
    .await?.success;
println!("removed: {ok}");  // false if a chart/position still holds it

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Ignoring success. A false means the change didn't happen — check it, don't assume.
  • Removing a busy symbol. Open positions or charts block removal.
  • Forgetting to select. The commonest cause of "empty tick" / "no history" errors.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Add then count. symbol_select(sym, true) → symbols_total(true) grows by 1 (if it wasn't selected).
  • Blocked removal. With an open position on sym, symbol_select(sym, false).success == false.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• symbol_exist · symbol_info_tick · price_history
  • Back to: Symbol Information — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Symbols Total
docs.text:
How many symbols the terminal knows — all of them, or only those in Market Watch.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::symbols_total(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolsTotal(SymbolsTotalRequest) -> SymbolsTotalReply
  • Payload: SymbolsTotalData → total: i32

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 SymbolsTotal(selected) — a count.
  • Why you need it. The upper bound for walking symbols by index with symbol_name.
  • When to use. Enumerating the symbol universe, or showing "N symbols in Market Watch".

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbols_total(
    &self,
    request: pb::SymbolsTotalRequest,
) -> Result<pb::SymbolsTotalData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolsTotalRequest { bool mode = 1; }   // true = only Market Watch
message SymbolsTotalData    { int32 total = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description mode bool true → count only symbols selected in Market Watch; false → count all symbols.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolsTotalData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description total i32 Number of symbols.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Pairs with symbol_name. Loop index in 0..total and call symbol_name with the same selected/mode meaning.
  • mode selects the universe. Market-Watch count is usually far smaller than the full broker list.

docs.title: 1) Count both universes
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let all = account.symbols_total(pb::SymbolsTotalRequest { mode: false }).await?.total;
let watch = account.symbols_total(pb::SymbolsTotalRequest { mode: true }).await?.total;
println!("{all} symbols total, {watch} in Market Watch");

docs.title: 2) Walk every Market-Watch symbol
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let n = account.symbols_total(pb::SymbolsTotalRequest { mode: true }).await?.total;
for i in 0..n {
    let name = account
        .symbol_name(pb::SymbolNameRequest { index: i, selected: true })
        .await?.name;
    println!("[{i}] {name}");
}

docs.title: 3) Guard a later index lookup
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let n = account.symbols_total(pb::SymbolsTotalRequest { mode: false }).await?.total;
let idx = 5.min(n - 1).max(0);
let name = account.symbol_name(pb::SymbolNameRequest { index: idx, selected: false }).await?.name;
println!("symbol #{idx} = {name}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• selected must match. Use the same universe here and in symbol_name — mixing them indexes a different list.
  • total can be large. The full broker list may be thousands; prefer mode: true for UI.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Market Watch ≤ all. symbols_total(true).total <= symbols_total(false).total.
  • After symbol_select. Selecting a new symbol increments the Market-Watch count by 1.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• symbol_name · symbol_list · symbol_select
  • Back to: Symbol Information — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: 3. Positions & Orders — Overview
docs.text:
What you hold now (open positions), what's resting (pending orders), their ticket lists, the closed history, and a P/L helper.

In MT5, positions and orders are distinct: an order is an instruction (market or pending); a position is the resulting open exposure. Deals are the fills recorded in history. These methods are read-only.

docs.title: Current state
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner positions_total() PositionsTotalData How many positions are open right now. opened_orders(req) OpenedOrdersData Open positions and active pending orders, with full detail. opened_orders_tickets(req) OpenedOrdersTicketsData Just the ticket numbers of open orders and positions.

docs.title: History
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner order_history(req) OrdersHistoryData Historical orders and deals in a time range (paged). positions_history(req) PositionsHistoryData Closed positions in a time range (paged).

docs.title: P/L helper
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner tick_value_with_size(req) TickValueWithSizeData Tick value/size and contract size for symbols — the inputs for money-per-point P/L.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text:
• "How many positions do I have?" → positions_total() (a single count).
  • "Show me everything open, with prices and P/L" → opened_orders() — returns both position_infos and opened_orders (pendings).
  • "I just need the tickets to iterate" → opened_orders_tickets() (lighter payload).
  • "What happened last week?" → order_history() (orders + deals) or positions_history() (closed positions).
  • "How much is a point worth per lot?" → tick_value_with_size().

opened_orders() is the workhorse: its position_infos carry live profit, price_current, SL/TP, swap and more. MT5Sugar builds its position helpers on top of it.

docs.title: ⚠️ Reply-shape note
docs.text:
Most methods here use the standard oneof { data, error } reply. tick_value_with_size is different — its reply carries flat data / error fields (handled internally by a separate unwrap). You still just get Result<TickValueWithSizeData, MT5Error>.

Back to: MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Opened Orders (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
Everything currently live: open positions (with P/L, SL/TP, prices) and active pending orders, in one call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::opened_orders(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • RPC: OpenedOrders(OpenedOrdersRequest) -> OpenedOrdersReply
  • Payload: OpenedOrdersData → opened_orders: Vec<OpenedOrderInfo>, position_infos: Vec<PositionInfo>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A full snapshot of your live book: positions and pendings.
  • Why you need it. position_infos carry live profit, price_current, SL/TP, swap — everything to manage trades.
  • When to use. Any position/pending dashboard or management loop. This is the method MT5Sugar's position helpers wrap.

docs.title: 🎯 Purpose
docs.text:
• List open positions with live P/L and current price
  • List active pending orders (limits/stops) awaiting fill
  • Read SL/TP, volumes, magic numbers, comments per entry

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn opened_orders(
    &self,
    request: pb::OpenedOrdersRequest,
) -> Result<pb::OpenedOrdersData, MT5Error>

Request message:

message OpenedOrdersRequest {
  Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType input_sort_mode = 1;   // Rust field: input_sort_mode (i32)
}

Reply payload:

message OpenedOrdersData {
  repeated OpenedOrderInfo opened_orders = 1;  // pending orders
  repeated PositionInfo    position_infos = 2; // open positions
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description input_sort_mode i32 (Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType) Sort order (see enum). Pass Sort::X as i32.

docs.title: Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType
docs.text: Variant Value Order Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOpenTimeAsc 0 Open time ↑ Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOpenTimeDesc 1 Open time ↓ Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOrderTicketIdAsc 2 Ticket ↑ Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOrderTicketIdDesc 3 Ticket ↓

docs.title: position_infos: Vec<PositionInfo> (open positions)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description ticket u64 Position ticket symbol String Symbol volume f64 Lots price_open f64 Entry price price_current f64 Current price stop_loss / take_profit f64 SL / TP (0 if unset) swap f64 Accrued swap profit f64 Live floating P/L r#type i32 (Bmt5EnumPositionType) 0 = Buy, 1 = Sell magic_number i64 EA magic comment String Comment open_time / last_update_time Option<Timestamp> Times position_commission f64 Commission identifier i64 Position id

docs.title: opened_orders: Vec<OpenedOrderInfo> (pending orders)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description ticket u64 Order ticket symbol String Symbol price_open f64 Trigger price stop_limit f64 Stop-limit price (for stop-limit orders) stop_loss / take_profit f64 SL / TP volume_initial / volume_current f64 Requested / remaining lots r#type i32 (Bmt5EnumOrderType) Order type (buy/sell limit/stop…) state i32 (Bmt5EnumOrderState) Order state type_filling / type_time i32 Filling / time policy time_setup / time_expiration Option<Timestamp> Placed / expiry magic_number i64 EA magic comment String Comment

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Two lists, different meanings. position_infos = exposure you hold; opened_orders = instructions not yet filled.
  • r#type is a raw identifier on both structs — Rust keyword.
  • Position side. PositionInfo.r#type: 0 Buy, 1 Sell (Bmt5EnumPositionType).
  • Sum profit across position_infos for total floating P/L.

docs.title: 1) Print open positions with P/L
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType as Sort;

let data = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest {
    input_sort_mode: Sort::Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOpenTimeAsc as i32,
}).await?;
for p in &data.position_infos {
    let side = if p.r#type == 0 { "BUY" } else { "SELL" };
    println!("#{} {side} {} {:.2} lot  P/L {:+.2}", p.ticket, p.symbol, p.volume, p.profit);
}

docs.title: 2) Total floating P/L
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType as Sort;

let data = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest { input_sort_mode: Sort::Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOpenTimeAsc as i32 }).await?;
let total: f64 = data.position_infos.iter().map(|p| p.profit + p.swap).sum();
println!("floating P/L (incl. swap): {total:+.2}");

docs.title: 3) List pending orders
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType as Sort;

let data = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest { input_sort_mode: Sort::Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOrderTicketIdAsc as i32 }).await?;
for o in &data.opened_orders {
    println!("pending #{} {} @ {:.5} ({} lot)", o.ticket, o.symbol, o.price_open, o.volume_current);
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Mixing the two lists. Closing a pending (opened_orders) deletes the order; closing a position (position_infos) flattens exposure — different operations.
  • input_sort_mode is required. Pass a valid enum as i32.
  • Snapshot. P/L is as-of the call; re-query for fresh numbers or stream with on_position_profit.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Flat. Both vectors empty; position_infos.len() == positions_total().total_positions == 0.
  • One market buy. position_infos.len() == 1, r#type == 0, profit changes with price.
  • One pending. Appears in opened_orders, not position_infos.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• positions_total · opened_orders_tickets · on_position_profit
  • Back to: Positions & Orders — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Opened Orders Tickets
docs.text:
Just the ticket numbers of open pending orders and open positions — a lightweight list.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::opened_orders_tickets(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • RPC: OpenedOrdersTickets(OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest) -> OpenedOrdersTicketsReply
  • Payload: OpenedOrdersTicketsData → opened_orders_tickets, opened_position_tickets

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The ticket ids only — no prices, no P/L.
  • Why you need it. Cheap iteration or diffing "what's open now vs before" without the full payload.
  • When to use. When you only need ids (e.g. to modify/close by ticket). For details use opened_orders.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn opened_orders_tickets(
    &self,
    request: pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest,
) -> Result<pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {}   // no fields
message OpenedOrdersTicketsData {
  repeated int64 opened_orders_tickets = 1;    // pending order tickets
  repeated int64 opened_position_tickets = 2;  // open position tickets
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: None — pass pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {}.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OpenedOrdersTicketsData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description opened_orders_tickets Vec<i64> Tickets of active pending orders. opened_position_tickets Vec<i64> Tickets of open positions.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Two lists, like opened_orders. Pendings vs positions, but ids only.
  • Pair with detail calls. Use a ticket with order_modify / order_close, or match against opened_orders entries.
  • Great for diffs. Store the sets and compare across polls to detect fills/closes.

docs.title: 1) Count open vs pending
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let t = account.opened_orders_tickets(pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {}).await?;
println!("{} positions, {} pendings", t.opened_position_tickets.len(), t.opened_orders_tickets.len());

docs.title: 2) Iterate position tickets
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let t = account.opened_orders_tickets(pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {}).await?;
for ticket in t.opened_position_tickets {
    println!("position ticket {ticket}");
}

docs.title: 3) Detect new fills across two polls
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use std::collections::HashSet;

let before: HashSet<i64> = account.opened_orders_tickets(pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {}).await?
    .opened_position_tickets.into_iter().collect();
// ... later ...
let after: HashSet<i64> = account.opened_orders_tickets(pb::OpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {}).await?
    .opened_position_tickets.into_iter().collect();
for t in after.difference(&before) { println!("newly opened position {t}"); }

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Ids are i64 here. The detail structs use u64 for ticket; cast when matching (ticket as i64).
  • No details. If you need symbol/volume/P/L, call opened_orders.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Length parity. opened_position_tickets.len() == positions_total().total_positions.
  • Cross-check. Every id appears as a ticket in opened_orders's matching list.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• opened_orders · positions_total · order_modify
  • Back to: Positions & Orders — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Order History
docs.text:
Historical orders and their deals within a time range — paged.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::order_history(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: OrderHistory(OrderHistoryRequest) -> OrderHistoryReply
  • Payload: OrdersHistoryData → paging + history_data: Vec<HistoryData>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 history of orders and deals in [from, to].
  • Why you need it. Audit what happened: fills, closes, commissions, realized profit.
  • When to use. Statements, trade journals, realized-P/L reports. For closed positions specifically, positions_history is often simpler.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_history(
    &self,
    request: pb::OrderHistoryRequest,
) -> Result<pb::OrdersHistoryData, MT5Error>

Request message:

message OrderHistoryRequest {
  google.protobuf.Timestamp input_from = 1;   // required (server time)
  google.protobuf.Timestamp input_to = 2;     // required (server time)
  Bmt5EnumOrderHistorySortType input_sort_mode = 3;
  int32 page_number = 4;       // default 0
  int32 items_per_page = 5;    // default 0 (server default)
}

Reply payload:

message OrdersHistoryData {
  int32 array_total = 1;       // total matching rows
  int32 page_number = 2;
  int32 items_per_page = 3;
  repeated HistoryData history_data = 4;
}

message HistoryData {
  uint32 index = 1;
  OrderHistoryData history_order = 2;  // optional
  DealHistoryData  history_deal = 3;   // optional
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description input_from Option<Timestamp> Range start (server time). Required. input_to Option<Timestamp> Range end (server time). Required. input_sort_mode i32 (Bmt5EnumOrderHistorySortType) Sort order (see enum). page_number i32 0-based page. items_per_page i32 Page size (0 = server default).

docs.title: Bmt5EnumOrderHistorySortType
docs.text: Variant Value Bmt5SortByOpenTimeAsc / ...Desc 0 / 1 Bmt5SortByCloseTimeAsc / ...Desc 2 / 3 Bmt5SortByOrderTicketIdAsc / ...Desc 4 / 5

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrdersHistoryData
docs.text: array_total is the total matching rows (for paging); each HistoryData holds an optional order and/or deal.

docs.title: OrderHistoryData (key fields)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description ticket u64 Order ticket symbol String Symbol state i32 (Bmt5EnumOrderState) Final order state r#type i32 (Bmt5EnumOrderType) Order type price_open / price_current f64 Prices stop_loss / take_profit f64 SL / TP volume_initial / volume_current f64 Lots setup_time / done_time Option<Timestamp> Placed / finished position_id u64 Owning position magic_number i64 EA magic

docs.title: DealHistoryData (key fields)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description ticket u64 Deal ticket symbol String Symbol profit f64 Realized profit commission / fee / swap f64 Costs price f64 Fill price volume f64 Lots entry_type i32 (Bmt5EnumDealEntryType) In / out / inout r#type i32 (Bmt5EnumDealType) Deal type time Option<Timestamp> Fill time position_id u64 Owning position

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Orders vs deals. An order is the instruction; a deal is the execution that realized money. Realized P/L lives on deals (DealHistoryData.profit).
  • Both optional per row. Check history_order.is_some() / history_deal.is_some() before unwrapping.
  • Server time. from/to are server time — mind the broker's UTC offset (account_summary().utc_timezone_server_time_shift_minutes).
  • Page with array_total. Loop pages until you've read array_total rows.

docs.title: 1) Last 7 days, first page
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Bmt5EnumOrderHistorySortType as Sort;

fn ts(secs: i64) -> prost_types::Timestamp { prost_types::Timestamp { seconds: secs, nanos: 0 } }

let now = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp();
let data = account.order_history(pb::OrderHistoryRequest {
    input_from: Some(ts(now - 7 * 86_400)),
    input_to: Some(ts(now)),
    input_sort_mode: Sort::Bmt5SortByCloseTimeDesc as i32,
    page_number: 0,
    items_per_page: 50,
}).await?;
println!("{} total rows", data.array_total);

docs.title: 2) Realized P/L from deals
docs.text:
let realized: f64 = data.history_data.iter()
    .filter_map(|h| h.history_deal.as_ref())
    .map(|d| d.profit + d.commission + d.swap + d.fee)
    .sum();
println!("realized (net): {realized:+.2}");

docs.title: 3) Page through everything
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Bmt5EnumOrderHistorySortType as Sort;

let (from, to) = (ts(now - 30 * 86_400), ts(now));
let mut page = 0; let mut seen = 0;
loop {
    let d = account.order_history(pb::OrderHistoryRequest {
        input_from: Some(from.clone()), input_to: Some(to.clone()),
        input_sort_mode: Sort::Bmt5SortByOpenTimeAsc as i32,
        page_number: page, items_per_page: 100,
    }).await?;
    seen += d.history_data.len() as i32;
    if d.history_data.is_empty() || seen >= d.array_total { break; }
    page += 1;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Missing from/to. Both are required; None yields nothing useful.
  • Unwrapping the wrong half. A row may carry only an order or only a deal.
  • Server vs local time. Off-by-offset ranges silently miss rows.
  • Profit on orders. Orders don't carry realized P/L — read it from deals.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Known trade. After closing a position, its deal appears with the expected profit.
  • Paging completeness. Summed page lengths reach array_total.

docs.title: Positions History
docs.text:
Closed positions within a time range — one tidy record per position, paged.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::positions_history(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: PositionsHistory(PositionsHistoryRequest) -> PositionsHistoryReply
  • Payload: PositionsHistoryData → history_positions: Vec<PositionHistoryInfo>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Closed positions with entry/exit prices and realized P/L — already aggregated per position.
  • Why you need it. Cleaner than reconstructing positions from order_history's orders+deals.
  • When to use. Trade journals and realized-P/L reports per position.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn positions_history(
    &self,
    request: pb::PositionsHistoryRequest,
) -> Result<pb::PositionsHistoryData, MT5Error>

Request message:

message PositionsHistoryRequest {
  AhEnumPositionsHistorySortType sort_type = 1;        // Rust field: sort_type (i32)
  google.protobuf.Timestamp position_open_time_from = 2;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp position_open_time_to = 3;
  optional int32 page_number = 4;
  optional int32 items_per_page = 5;
}

Reply payload:

message PositionsHistoryData {
  repeated PositionHistoryInfo history_positions = 1;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description sort_type i32 (AhEnumPositionsHistorySortType) Sort order (see enum). position_open_time_from Option<Timestamp> Range start (by position open time). position_open_time_to Option<Timestamp> Range end. page_number Option<i32> 0-based page. items_per_page Option<i32> Page size.

docs.title: AhEnumPositionsHistorySortType
docs.text: Variant Value Order AhPositionOpenTimeAsc 0 Open time ↑ AhPositionOpenTimeDesc 1 Open time ↓ AhPositionTicketAsc 2 Ticket ↑ AhPositionTicketDesc 3 Ticket ↓

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — PositionHistoryInfo (per position)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description position_ticket u64 Position ticket symbol String Symbol order_type i32 (AhEnumPositionsHistoryOrderType) Direction/type (0 Buy, 1 Sell, …) volume f64 Lots open_price / close_price f64 Entry / exit open_time / close_time Option<Timestamp> Opened / closed stop_loss / take_profit f64 SL / TP profit f64 Realized profit swap f64 Swap commission / fee f64 Costs market_value f64 Position value comment String Comment magic i64 EA magic

docs.title: 🧱 AhEnumPositionsHistoryOrderType (field order_type)
docs.text: Variant Value Variant Value AhOrderTypeBuy 0 AhOrderTypeSellStop 5 AhOrderTypeSell 1 AhOrderTypeBuyStopLimit 6 AhOrderTypeBuyLimit 2 AhOrderTypeSellStopLimit 7 AhOrderTypeSellLimit 3 AhOrderTypeCloseBy 8 AhOrderTypeBuyStop 4

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One row per closed position — no order/deal split to reconcile.
  • Net result = profit + swap + commission + fee.
  • Range is by open time. Positions opened in the window; a long-held trade opened earlier won't appear even if closed in the window.
  • Page via items_per_page. With None you may get only the first page.

docs.title: 1) Closed positions, last 30 days
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::AhEnumPositionsHistorySortType as Sort;

fn ts(s: i64) -> prost_types::Timestamp { prost_types::Timestamp { seconds: s, nanos: 0 } }
let now = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp();

let data = account.positions_history(pb::PositionsHistoryRequest {
    sort_type: Sort::AhPositionOpenTimeDesc as i32,
    position_open_time_from: Some(ts(now - 30 * 86_400)),
    position_open_time_to: Some(ts(now)),
    page_number: Some(0),
    items_per_page: Some(100),
}).await?;
for p in &data.history_positions {
    let side = if p.order_type == 0 { "BUY" } else { "SELL" };
    println!("#{} {side} {} {:.2} lot  {:.5}->{:.5}  P/L {:+.2}",
        p.position_ticket, p.symbol, p.volume, p.open_price, p.close_price, p.profit);
}

docs.title: 2) Net realized over the window
docs.text:
let net: f64 = data.history_positions.iter()
    .map(|p| p.profit + p.swap + p.commission + p.fee)
    .sum();
println!("net realized: {net:+.2}");

docs.title: 3) Win rate
docs.text:
let (wins, total) = data.history_positions.iter()
    .fold((0usize, 0usize), |(w, t), p| (w + (p.profit > 0.0) as usize, t + 1));
if total > 0 { println!("win rate: {:.1}%", wins as f64 / total as f64 * 100.0); }

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Options are Option<..>. Wrap times and paging in Some(..).
  • Range semantics. Filtered by open time, not close time.
  • order_type as i32 when comparing to the enum.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Recently closed trade. Appears with matching open_price/close_price and expected profit sign.
  • Empty window. A quiet range returns an empty history_positions.

docs.title: Positions Total
docs.text:
How many positions are open right now — a single integer.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::positions_total() (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • RPC: PositionsTotal(PositionsTotalRequest) -> PositionsTotalReply
  • Payload: PositionsTotalData → total_positions: i32

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 PositionsTotal() — the count of open positions.
  • Why you need it. A cheap "do I have exposure?" check before heavier calls.
  • When to use. Guards and dashboards. For details use opened_orders.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn positions_total(&self) -> Result<pb::PositionsTotalData, MT5Error>

Takes no argument — the underlying request is the unit (), so there's no …Request struct to build.

Reply payload:

message PositionsTotalData { int32 total_positions = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: None.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — PositionsTotalData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description total_positions i32 Number of currently open positions.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Positions, not orders. Pending orders are not counted here — see opened_orders().opened_orders for those.
  • Cheapest exposure check. Prefer this over fetching all positions just to test for zero.

docs.title: 1) Quick guard
docs.text:
let n = account.positions_total().await?.total_positions;
if n == 0 { println!("flat — no open positions"); }
else { println!("{n} open position(s)"); }

docs.title: 2) Gate a "close all" routine
docs.text:
if account.positions_total().await?.total_positions > 0 {
    // ... fetch opened_orders and close them
}

docs.title: 3) Poll exposure
docs.text:
use std::time::Duration;
for _ in 0..5 {
    println!("positions: {}", account.positions_total().await?.total_positions);
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Don't pass a request. This method takes no args; there is no PositionsTotalRequest to construct.
  • Count ≠ volume. Two positions could net to zero exposure; the count doesn't tell you direction or size.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Flat account. Returns 0.
  • After opening one position. Returns 1; matches opened_orders().position_infos.len().

docs.title: Tick Value With Size
docs.text:
Tick value, tick size and contract size for one or more symbols — the inputs for money-per-point P/L math.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::tick_value_with_size(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: TickValueWithSize(TickValueWithSizeRequest) -> TickValueWithSizeReply
  • Payload: TickValueWithSizeData → symbol_tick_size_infos: Vec<TickSizeSymbol>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Per-symbol tick economics: how much money one tick is worth per lot, and the price step.
  • Why you need it. To convert a price move (points) into account-currency P/L and to size positions by risk.
  • When to use. Risk sizing and P/L estimation across several symbols at once.

⚠️ Reply shape B. Unlike most methods, this reply uses flat data / error fields (not the usual oneof). The SDK unwraps it the same way — you still get Result<TickValueWithSizeData, MT5Error>.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn tick_value_with_size(
    &self,
    request: pb::TickValueWithSizeRequest,
) -> Result<pb::TickValueWithSizeData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message TickValueWithSizeRequest {
  repeated string symbol_names = 1;   // one or many
}
message TickValueWithSizeReply {
  TickValueWithSizeData data = 1;     // flat (shape B)
  Error error = 2;
}
message TickValueWithSizeData {
  repeated TickSizeSymbol symbol_tick_size_infos = 1;
}
message TickSizeSymbol {
  int32  index = 1;
  string name = 2;
  double trade_tick_value = 3;
  double trade_tick_value_profit = 4;
  double trade_tick_value_loss = 5;
  double trade_tick_size = 6;
  double trade_contract_size = 7;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol_names Vec<String> One or more symbols to query in a single call.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — TickSizeSymbol (per symbol)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description index i32 Row index name String Symbol name trade_tick_value f64 Money per tick per lot (deposit currency) trade_tick_value_profit f64 Tick value for a winning position trade_tick_value_loss f64 Tick value for a losing position trade_tick_size f64 Minimal price change trade_contract_size f64 Contract size (e.g. 100000 for FX)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Money per point. value_per_point = trade_tick_value × (point / trade_tick_size). When tick size equals point, it's just trade_tick_value per point per lot.
  • Risk sizing. lots ≈ risk_money / (stop_points × value_per_point), then round to the symbol's volume step.
  • Batch it. Pass several names at once — one round-trip for your whole watchlist.
  • Profit vs loss tick value can differ for some instruments; use the relevant one for conservative sizing.

docs.title: 1) Tick value for a few symbols
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let data = account.tick_value_with_size(pb::TickValueWithSizeRequest {
    symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into(), "GBPUSD".into(), "XAUUSD".into()],
}).await?;
for s in &data.symbol_tick_size_infos {
    println!("{}: tick value {:.5}, tick size {:.5}, contract {}",
        s.name, s.trade_tick_value, s.trade_tick_size, s.trade_contract_size);
}

docs.title: 2) Risk-based lot sizing
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let s = account.tick_value_with_size(pb::TickValueWithSizeRequest { symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into()] })
    .await?.symbol_tick_size_infos.into_iter().next().unwrap();

let point = account.symbol_info_double(pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    r#type: pb::SymbolInfoDoubleProperty::SymbolPoint as i32,
}).await?.value;

let value_per_point = s.trade_tick_value * (point / s.trade_tick_size);
let risk_money = 50.0;      // risk $50
let stop_points = 200.0;    // 20 pips on a 5-digit symbol
let raw_lots = risk_money / (stop_points * value_per_point);
println!("raw lots ≈ {raw_lots:.2} (round to volume step before trading)");

docs.title: 3) Estimate P/L of a move
docs.text:
// A 30-point move on 0.10 lot:
let value_per_point = /* as above */ 1.0_f64;
let pl = 30.0 * value_per_point * 0.10;
println!("≈ P/L for 30 points @ 0.10 lot: {pl:+.2}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Tick size vs point. They're not always equal — scale by point / trade_tick_size, don't assume 1.
  • Unknown symbol. A name the server doesn't know may be omitted from the result — match by name, don't assume positional order.
  • Round lots. Always round the computed size to the symbol's volume step and clamp to min/max.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• FX major. EURUSD trade_contract_size == 100000; trade_tick_value > 0.
  • Batch parity. Requesting three names returns three symbol_tick_size_infos (for known symbols).
  • Sizing sanity. Doubling stop_points halves the computed lots.

docs.title: 4. Market Depth (DOM) — Overview
docs.text:
Level-II order book: the queue of buy/sell orders at each price. Subscribe, read snapshots, release.

The Depth of Market (DOM) is a subscription, not a one-shot read. The lifecycle is:

  1. market_book_add — subscribe to a symbol's book.
  2. market_book_get — read the current book snapshot (repeat as needed).
  3. market_book_release — unsubscribe when done.

docs.title: Methods in this group
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner market_book_add(req) MarketBookAddData Subscribe to a symbol's order book (opened_successfully). market_book_get(req) MarketBookGetData Current book: a vector of price levels with side & volume. market_book_release(req) MarketBookReleaseData Unsubscribe (closed_successfully).

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text:
• Starting out → market_book_add(symbol) once, check opened_successfully.
  • Each refresh → market_book_get(symbol) → iterate mql_book_infos.
  • Cleanup → market_book_release(symbol) to stop the feed.

DOM is only meaningful for instruments the broker provides depth for (typically exchange-traded). Many retail FX feeds return an empty or shallow book.

Back to: MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Market Book Add
docs.text:
Subscribe to a symbol's Depth of Market — the first step before reading the order book.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::market_book_add(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: MarketBookAdd(MarketBookAddRequest) -> MarketBookAddReply
  • Payload: MarketBookAddData → opened_successfully: bool

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 MarketBookAdd(symbol) — opens the DOM feed for a symbol.
  • Why you need it. market_book_get only returns data after a successful add.
  • When to use. Once, at the start of a DOM session; pair with market_book_release.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn market_book_add(
    &self,
    request: pb::MarketBookAddRequest,
) -> Result<pb::MarketBookAddData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message MarketBookAddRequest { string symbol = 1; }
message MarketBookAddData    { bool opened_successfully = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol whose DOM to subscribe to.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — MarketBookAddData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description opened_successfully bool true if the subscription opened.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Select first. Ensure the symbol is in Market Watch (symbol_select) before subscribing.
  • One add per symbol. Re-adding an already-subscribed symbol is harmless but unnecessary.
  • Always release. Balance every successful add with a market_book_release to free the feed.

docs.title: 1) Subscribe and check
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let ok = account.market_book_add(pb::MarketBookAddRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() })
    .await?.opened_successfully;
if !ok { println!("DOM not available for this symbol"); }

docs.title: 2) Full lifecycle
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

account.market_book_add(pb::MarketBookAddRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
let book = account.market_book_get(pb::MarketBookGetRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
println!("{} levels", book.mql_book_infos.len());
account.market_book_release(pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;

docs.title: 3) Guard before polling
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

if account.market_book_add(pb::MarketBookAddRequest { symbol: "XAUUSD".into() }).await?.opened_successfully {
    // safe to loop market_book_get now
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Reading before adding. market_book_get without a successful add yields nothing.
  • Leaking subscriptions. Forgetting market_book_release keeps the feed open.
  • FX may have no DOM. opened_successfully can be false on feeds without depth.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Supported symbol. opened_successfully == true, then market_book_get returns levels.
  • Idempotent-ish. Adding twice still returns true.
