docs.title: Market Book Get
docs.text:
A snapshot of the current order book: price levels with side and volume.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::market_book_get(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: MarketBookGet(MarketBookGetRequest) -> MarketBookGetReply
  • Payload: MarketBookGetData → mql_book_infos: Vec<MrpcMqlBookInfo>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 MarketBookGet(symbol, book[]) — the current depth levels.
  • Why you need it. See resting liquidity above and below the market — bids vs offers and their sizes.
  • When to use. After a successful market_book_add; call repeatedly to refresh.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn market_book_get(
    &self,
    request: pb::MarketBookGetRequest,
) -> Result<pb::MarketBookGetData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message MarketBookGetRequest { string symbol = 1; }
message MarketBookGetData { repeated MrpcMqlBookInfo mql_book_infos = 1; }

message MrpcMqlBookInfo {
  BookType type = 1;        // Rust field: r#type (i32)
  double price = 2;
  int64  volume = 3;
  double volume_real = 4;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Subscribed symbol.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — MrpcMqlBookInfo (per level)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description r#type i32 (BookType) Side/kind of the level (see enum). price f64 Price of the level. volume i64 Volume at the level. volume_real f64 Higher-accuracy volume.

docs.title: BookType
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning Sell 0 Sell order (offer / ask side) Buy 1 Buy order (bid side) SellMarket 2 Sell at market BuyMarket 3 Buy at market

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Two sides in one vector. Filter by r#type to split bids (Buy) from offers (Sell).
  • Best bid / best ask. Highest Buy price and lowest Sell price; their gap is the book spread.
  • Snapshot. Each call is a point-in-time copy; poll to refresh.
  • r#type is a raw identifier (Rust keyword).

docs.title: 1) Print the book
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::BookType;

let book = account.market_book_get(pb::MarketBookGetRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
for lvl in &book.mql_book_infos {
    let side = match BookType::try_from(lvl.r#type) {
        Ok(BookType::Buy) | Ok(BookType::BuyMarket) => "BID",
        _ => "ASK",
    };
    println!("{side} {:.5} x {}", lvl.price, lvl.volume);
}

docs.title: 2) Best bid / best ask
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::BookType;

let book = account.market_book_get(pb::MarketBookGetRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
let best_bid = book.mql_book_infos.iter()
    .filter(|l| matches!(BookType::try_from(l.r#type), Ok(BookType::Buy)))
    .map(|l| l.price).fold(f64::MIN, f64::max);
let best_ask = book.mql_book_infos.iter()
    .filter(|l| matches!(BookType::try_from(l.r#type), Ok(BookType::Sell)))
    .map(|l| l.price).fold(f64::MAX, f64::min);
println!("book spread: {:.5}", best_ask - best_bid);

docs.title: 3) Total depth per side
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::BookType;

let book = account.market_book_get(pb::MarketBookGetRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
let (bid_vol, ask_vol) = book.mql_book_infos.iter().fold((0i64, 0i64), |(b, a), l| {
    match BookType::try_from(l.r#type) {
        Ok(BookType::Buy) => (b + l.volume, a),
        Ok(BookType::Sell) => (b, a + l.volume),
        _ => (b, a),
    }
});
println!("bid depth {bid_vol}, ask depth {ask_vol}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Empty book. Means no DOM for this symbol or you didn't market_book_add first.
  • r#type as i32 / try_from. Decode the side with BookType::try_from(l.r#type).
  • Assuming order. Don't assume levels are pre-sorted — sort by price if you need rank.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Subscribed exchange symbol. Returns multiple levels; best ask ≥ best bid.
  • Unsubscribed. Empty vector — add first.

docs.text:

docs.title: Market Book Release
docs.text:
Unsubscribe from a symbol's Depth of Market — the cleanup step.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::market_book_release(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: MarketBookRelease(MarketBookReleaseRequest) -> MarketBookReleaseReply
  • Payload: MarketBookReleaseData → closed_successfully: bool

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 MarketBookRelease(symbol) — closes the DOM feed.
  • Why you need it. Frees server/terminal resources once you're done reading the book.
  • When to use. At the end of a DOM session — one release per market_book_add.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn market_book_release(
    &self,
    request: pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest,
) -> Result<pb::MarketBookReleaseData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message MarketBookReleaseRequest { string symbol = 1; }
message MarketBookReleaseData    { bool closed_successfully = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol to unsubscribe.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — MarketBookReleaseData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description closed_successfully bool true if the subscription closed.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Pair with add. Every successful market_book_add should get a matching release.
  • Idempotent-ish. Releasing a symbol that isn't subscribed typically returns false — safe to ignore.
  • Do it in cleanup paths. Release on error paths too, so a failed read doesn't leak the feed.

docs.title: 1) Release when done
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let ok = account.market_book_release(pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() })
    .await?.closed_successfully;
println!("released: {ok}");

docs.title: 2) RAII-style guard
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

account.market_book_add(pb::MarketBookAddRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
let result = (|| async {
    let book = account.market_book_get(pb::MarketBookGetRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
    Ok::<_, metarpc_mt5::MT5Error>(book.mql_book_infos.len())
})().await;
// always release, even if the read failed
let _ = account.market_book_release(pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await;
println!("levels: {result:?}");

docs.title: 3) Release several symbols
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

for sym in ["EURUSD", "GBPUSD"] {
    let _ = account.market_book_release(pb::MarketBookReleaseRequest { symbol: sym.into() }).await;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Forgetting to release. Leaves the DOM feed open on the terminal.
  • Releasing without adding. Returns false; not harmful, just a no-op.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• After add. closed_successfully == true.
  • Double release. Second call returns false.

docs.title: 5. Trading Operations — Overview
docs.text:
The write path: send, modify and close orders — plus pre-trade calculators (check, margin, profit).

These are the only methods in MT5Account that change account state (order_send, order_modify, order_close). The three calculators (order_check, order_calc_margin, order_calc_profit) are read-only "what-if" helpers.

The low-level calls take the raw protobuf requests (MT5's trade request has many fields). For friendlier argument shapes — buy/sell by symbol, pip-based SL/TP, risk sizing — use MT5Service and MT5Sugar, which build on these.

docs.title: Execution (state-changing)
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner order_send(req) OrderSendData Place a market or pending order (with optional SL/TP). order_modify(req) OrderModifyData Change SL/TP/price/expiry of an order or position. order_close(req) OrderCloseData Close (or partially close) by ticket.

docs.title: Calculators (read-only)
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner order_check(req) OrderCheckData Validate a trade request and preview margin/balance impact. order_calc_margin(req) OrderCalcMarginData Margin required for a hypothetical order. order_calc_profit(req) OrderCalcProfitData Profit for a hypothetical open→close move.

docs.title: Return codes
docs.text: Execution methods return a returned_code (u32) — the MT5 trade server retcode. 10009 = TRADE_RETCODE_DONE (success). Anything else is a rejection/partial; returned_code_description explains it. See the Return Codes reference.

docs.title: A safe trading flow
docs.text:
1. Calculate — order_calc_margin / order_calc_profit to size and sanity-check.
  2. Check — order_check to validate against the live account (margin, stops level, filling mode).
  3. Send — order_send; confirm returned_code == 10009.
  4. Manage — order_modify (move SL to breakeven, trail) as the trade runs.
  5. Close — order_close by ticket.

This is exactly what the MT5Sugar strategy orchestrators automate.

Back to: MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Order Calc Margin
docs.text:
How much margin a hypothetical order would require — before you place it.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::order_calc_margin(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • RPC: OrderCalcMargin(OrderCalcMarginRequest) -> OrderCalcMarginReply
  • Payload: OrderCalcMarginData → margin: f64

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 OrderCalcMargin — margin in account currency for a would-be order.
  • Why you need it. Size positions to your free margin; avoid "no money" rejections.
  • When to use. During sizing, before order_send. More precise than multiplying margin rates yourself.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_calc_margin(
    &self,
    request: pb::OrderCalcMarginRequest,
) -> Result<pb::OrderCalcMarginData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message OrderCalcMarginRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  EnumOrderTypeTf order_type = 2;   // Rust field: order_type (i32)
  double volume = 3;                // lots
  double open_price = 4;            // hypothetical entry
}
message OrderCalcMarginData { double margin = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol. order_type i32 (EnumOrderTypeTf) Order type. Pass EnumOrderTypeTf::X as i32. volume f64 Lots. open_price f64 Entry price to assume.

docs.title: EnumOrderTypeTf (common)
docs.text: Variant Value OrderTypeTfBuy 0 OrderTypeTfSell 1 OrderTypeTfBuyLimit 2 OrderTypeTfSellLimit 3

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCalcMarginData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description margin f64 Required margin in the account's deposit currency.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Account currency. The result is in your deposit currency, ready to compare with free_margin.
  • Assumes a clean account. The calc ignores your existing positions/orders (hedging nets may make the real requirement lower).
  • Sizing loop. Try a volume, compare margin to free margin, adjust; or divide a target margin budget by the per-lot margin.

docs.title: 1) Margin for 1 lot EURUSD
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::EnumOrderTypeTf as TF;

let price = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?.ask;
let m = account.order_calc_margin(pb::OrderCalcMarginRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    order_type: TF::OrderTypeTfBuy as i32,
    volume: 1.0,
    open_price: price,
}).await?.margin;
println!("margin for 1.0 lot: {m:.2}");

docs.title: 2) Largest size that fits free margin
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::{EnumOrderTypeTf as TF, AccountInfoDoublePropertyType as P};

let price = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?.ask;
let per_lot = account.order_calc_margin(pb::OrderCalcMarginRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(), order_type: TF::OrderTypeTfBuy as i32, volume: 1.0, open_price: price,
}).await?.margin;
let free = account.account_info_double(pb::AccountInfoDoubleRequest { property_id: P::AccountMarginFree as i32 }).await?.requested_value;
let max_lots = if per_lot > 0.0 { (free * 0.9) / per_lot } else { 0.0 };  // keep 10% buffer
println!("max ≈ {max_lots:.2} lot (round to volume step)");

docs.title: 3) Margin for a sell
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::EnumOrderTypeTf as TF;

let m = account.order_calc_margin(pb::OrderCalcMarginRequest {
    symbol: "XAUUSD".into(), order_type: TF::OrderTypeTfSell as i32, volume: 0.10, open_price: 2400.0,
}).await?.margin;
println!("margin: {m:.2}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Enum as i32 (TF::OrderTypeTfBuy as i32).
  • Ignoring the buffer. Sizing to 100% of free margin leaves no room — keep a cushion.
  • Hedging accounts. The real requirement may be lower than this clean-account estimate.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Scales with volume. margin(2.0) ≈ 2 × margin(1.0).
  • Leverage effect. Higher account leverage → lower margin for the same volume.

docs.text:
• order_calc_profit · order_check · symbol_info_margin_rate

docs.title: Order Calc Profit
docs.text:
The profit a hypothetical open→close move would produce — in account currency.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::order_calc_profit(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • RPC: OrderCalcProfit(OrderCalcProfitRequest) -> OrderCalcProfitReply
  • Payload: OrderCalcProfitData → profit: f64

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 OrderCalcProfit — profit for volume moving from open_price to close_price.
  • Why you need it. Turn a target/stop distance into money; evaluate risk:reward before trading.
  • When to use. Planning TP/SL, backtest-style what-ifs. Handles cross-currency conversion for you.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_calc_profit(
    &self,
    request: pb::OrderCalcProfitRequest,
) -> Result<pb::OrderCalcProfitData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message OrderCalcProfitRequest {
  EnumOrderTypeTf order_type = 1;   // Rust field: order_type (i32)
  string symbol = 2;
  double volume = 3;                // lots
  double open_price = 4;
  double close_price = 5;
}
message OrderCalcProfitData { double profit = 1; }

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description order_type i32 (EnumOrderTypeTf) Buy or Sell (direction matters for the sign). symbol String Symbol. volume f64 Lots. open_price f64 Assumed entry. close_price f64 Assumed exit.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCalcProfitData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description profit f64 Profit (negative = loss) in the deposit currency.

docs.title: 🧱 EnumOrderTypeTf (field order_type)
docs.text:
Variant Value Variant Value OrderTypeTfBuy 0 OrderTypeTfSellStop 5 OrderTypeTfSell 1 OrderTypeTfBuyStopLimit 6 OrderTypeTfBuyLimit 2 OrderTypeTfSellStopLimit 7 OrderTypeTfSellLimit 3 OrderTypeTfCloseBy 8 OrderTypeTfBuyStop 4

For a profit estimate you'll almost always use OrderTypeTfBuy / OrderTypeTfSell — the direction sets the sign.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Direction sets the sign. For Buy, close > open is profit; for Sell, it's the opposite — use the correct order_type.
  • Cross-currency handled. The server converts to account currency, so you don't need the symbol's profit-currency rate.
  • Risk:reward. Compute profit at your TP and the (negative) profit at your SL; the ratio is your R:R.

docs.title: 1) Profit of a 50-pip buy move
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::EnumOrderTypeTf as TF;

let open = 1.08500;
let p = account.order_calc_profit(pb::OrderCalcProfitRequest {
    order_type: TF::OrderTypeTfBuy as i32,
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    volume: 0.10,
    open_price: open,
    close_price: open + 0.0050,   // +50 pips
}).await?.profit;
println!("profit: {p:+.2}");

docs.title: 2) Risk:reward from SL/TP
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::EnumOrderTypeTf as TF;

let (entry, sl, tp) = (1.08500, 1.08300, 1.09000);
let calc = |close: f64| {
    let acc = &account;
    async move {
        acc.order_calc_profit(pb::OrderCalcProfitRequest {
            order_type: TF::OrderTypeTfBuy as i32, symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
            volume: 0.10, open_price: entry, close_price: close,
        }).await.map(|d| d.profit)
    }
};
let reward = calc(tp).await?;
let risk = calc(sl).await?;          // negative
println!("R:R ≈ {:.2}", reward / risk.abs());

docs.title: 3) Profit of a sell
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::EnumOrderTypeTf as TF;

let p = account.order_calc_profit(pb::OrderCalcProfitRequest {
    order_type: TF::OrderTypeTfSell as i32, symbol: "USDJPY".into(),
    volume: 0.10, open_price: 156.00, close_price: 155.50,   // price fell → sell profits
}).await?.profit;
println!("sell profit: {p:+.2}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Wrong order_type. Using Buy for a short flips the sign.
  • Enum as i32.
  • Spread/commission not included. This is gross price-move profit, not net of costs — subtract commission/swap separately (see tick_value_with_size / history).

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Sign check. Buy with close > open → positive; close < open → negative.
  • Scales with volume. Double the lots → double the profit.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• order_calc_margin · tick_value_with_size · order_send
  • Back to: Trading Operations — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Order Check
docs.text:
Validate a trade request against the live account before sending it — margin, balance, equity and free margin after the hypothetical deal.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::order_check(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • RPC: OrderCheck(OrderCheckRequest) -> OrderCheckReply
  • Payload: OrderCheckData → mql_trade_check_result: Option<MrpcMqlTradeCheckResult>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 OrderCheck — a dry run of order_send.
  • Why you need it. Catch "not enough money" / "invalid stops" before committing.
  • When to use. Right before order_send, especially for larger sizes.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_check(
    &self,
    request: pb::OrderCheckRequest,
) -> Result<pb::OrderCheckData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message OrderCheckRequest {
  MrpcMqlTradeRequest mql_trade_request = 1;   // the trade to validate
}
message OrderCheckData {
  MrpcMqlTradeCheckResult mql_trade_check_result = 1;
}

MrpcMqlTradeRequest (key fields):

message MrpcMqlTradeRequest {
  MrpcEnumTradeRequestActions action = 1;
  uint64 expert_advisor_magic_number = 2;
  uint64 order = 3;
  string symbol = 4;
  double volume = 5;
  double price = 6;
  double stop_limit = 7;
  double stop_loss = 8;
  // … take_profit, deviation, type, type_filling, type_time, expiration, comment …
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description mql_trade_request Option<MrpcMqlTradeRequest> The hypothetical trade (Some(..)). Fill symbol, volume, price, stop_loss, take_profit, order type, etc.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — MrpcMqlTradeCheckResult
docs.text: Field Rust type Description returned_code u32 Validation retcode (10009 = would succeed). balance_after_deal f64 Projected balance. equity_after_deal f64 Projected equity. profit f64 Projected floating profit. margin f64 Margin the deal needs. free_margin f64 Projected free margin. margin_level f64 Projected margin level (%). comment String Description / error.

docs.title: 🧱 MrpcEnumTradeRequestActions (field action)
docs.text:
Variant Value Meaning TradeActionDeal 0 Market deal (open/close at market) TradeActionPending 1 Place a pending order TradeActionSltp 2 Modify a position's SL/TP TradeActionModify 3 Modify a pending order TradeActionRemove 4 Delete a pending order TradeActionCloseBy 5 Close a position by an opposite one

The request also carries order_type (EnumOrderTypeTf), type_filling and type_time enums — set the ones your check needs; ..Default::default() leaves the rest zeroed.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Preview, not execution. Nothing is placed; it only validates and projects.
  • Check margin headroom. If free_margin would go negative or margin_level too low, don't send.
  • returned_code here mirrors send codes. 10009 means the real order_send would be accepted (market conditions permitting).
  • Result is Option. Unwrap mql_trade_check_result before reading.

docs.title: 1) Validate before sending
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let req = pb::MrpcMqlTradeRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    volume: 0.50,
    price: 1.08500,
    stop_loss: 1.08300,
    take_profit: 1.09000,
    ..Default::default()
};
let out = account.order_check(pb::OrderCheckRequest { mql_trade_request: Some(req) }).await?;
if let Some(r) = out.mql_trade_check_result {
    if r.returned_code == 10009 {
        println!("OK — needs margin {:.2}, free after {:.2}", r.margin, r.free_margin);
    } else {
        println!("would fail: {} ({})", r.returned_code, r.comment);
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Guard a send with a margin-level floor
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let out = account.order_check(pb::OrderCheckRequest {
    mql_trade_request: Some(pb::MrpcMqlTradeRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), volume: 1.0, price: 1.085, ..Default::default() }),
}).await?;
let ok = out.mql_trade_check_result
    .map(|r| r.returned_code == 10009 && r.margin_level > 200.0)
    .unwrap_or(false);
println!("safe to send: {ok}");

docs.title: 3) Projected equity impact
docs.text:
if let Some(r) = out.mql_trade_check_result {
    println!("equity now→after: {:.2}", r.equity_after_deal);
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Forgetting Some(..). mql_trade_request is an Option.
  • Treating it as a send. It never opens anything.
  • Not unwrapping the result option.
  • ..Default::default() leaves other fields zeroed — set the ones that matter for your check.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Oversized order. A huge volume yields a non-10009 code and negative free margin.
  • Reasonable order. returned_code == 10009, margin > 0.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• order_send · order_calc_margin · Return Codes
  • Back to: Trading Operations — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Order Close
docs.text:
Close a position (fully or partially) by ticket.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::order_close(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • RPC: OrderClose(OrderCloseRequest) -> OrderCloseReply
  • Payload: OrderCloseData → returned_code: u32, close_mode, …

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Close by ticket — full or partial.
  • Why you need it. Exit a trade or scale out part of it.
  • When to use. Taking profit, cutting losses, flattening. For "close all", loop over opened_orders.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_close(
    &self,
    request: pb::OrderCloseRequest,
) -> Result<pb::OrderCloseData, MT5Error>

Request / Reply:

message OrderCloseRequest {
  uint64 ticket = 1;
  double volume = 2;     // lots to close (full volume = full close)
  int32  slippage = 5;
}
message OrderCloseData {
  uint32 returned_code = 1;             // 10009 = success
  string returned_string_code = 2;
  string returned_code_description = 3;
  MrpcOrderCloseMode close_mode = 4;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description ticket u64 Position ticket to close. volume f64 Lots to close. Pass the position's full volume to close completely; less for a partial. slippage i32 Max price deviation, points.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description returned_code u32 10009 = success. returned_code_description String Human-readable retcode. close_mode i32 (MrpcOrderCloseMode) How it was closed.

docs.title: 🧱 MrpcOrderCloseMode (reply field close_mode)
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning MrpcMarketOrderClose 0 Full market close of a position MrpcMarketOrderPartialClose 1 Partial market close MrpcPendingOrderRemove 2 A pending order was removed

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Full vs partial. volume equal to the position's size → full close; smaller → partial (the remainder stays open).
  • Get the volume first. Read it from opened_orders().position_infos[..].volume.
  • Pendings. To cancel a resting pending order, close it by its ticket the same way (the gateway deletes it).
  • Check returned_code.

docs.title: 1) Full close by ticket
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

// find the position's volume
let pos = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest {
    input_sort_mode: pb::Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType::Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOpenTimeAsc as i32,
}).await?;
if let Some(p) = pos.position_infos.iter().find(|p| p.ticket == 123456) {
    let res = account.order_close(pb::OrderCloseRequest { ticket: p.ticket, volume: p.volume, slippage: 20 }).await?;
    println!("close code {}", res.returned_code);
}

docs.title: 2) Partial close (scale out half)
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let res = account.order_close(pb::OrderCloseRequest {
    ticket: 123456,
    volume: 0.05,   // half of a 0.10 lot position
    slippage: 20,
}).await?;
println!("partial close code {}", res.returned_code);

docs.title: 3) Close all positions
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let data = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest {
    input_sort_mode: pb::Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType::Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOpenTimeAsc as i32,
}).await?;
for p in &data.position_infos {
    let r = account.order_close(pb::OrderCloseRequest { ticket: p.ticket, volume: p.volume, slippage: 30 }).await?;
    println!("#{} -> {}", p.ticket, r.returned_code);
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Wrong volume. More than the position holds → rejection; use the actual volume.
  • Partial leaves a remainder. Don't assume the ticket is gone after a partial close.
  • Ignoring returned_code.
  • Slippage too small in fast markets → requote/rejection.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Full close. After opening 0.10 lot, close 0.10 → 10009; position disappears from opened_orders.
  • Partial. Close 0.05 of 0.10 → remaining 0.05 still listed.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• order_send · order_modify · opened_orders
  • Back to: Trading Operations — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Order Modify
docs.text:
Change SL/TP of a position, or price/SL/TP/expiry of a pending order — by ticket.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::order_modify(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • RPC: OrderModify(OrderModifyRequest) -> OrderModifyReply
  • Payload: OrderModifyData → returned_code: u32, …

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 OrderModify/PositionModify — adjust an existing order/position.
  • Why you need it. Move SL to breakeven, trail stops, re-price a pending.
  • When to use. Managing a live trade. The MT5Sugar orchestrators call this to trail.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_modify(
    &self,
    request: pb::OrderModifyRequest,
) -> Result<pb::OrderModifyData, MT5Error>

Request message:

message OrderModifyRequest {
  uint64 ticket = 1;                       // position or pending order
  optional double stop_loss = 2;           // new SL
  optional double take_profit = 3;         // new TP
  optional double price = 4;               // new price — pendings only
  optional Tmt5EnumOrderTypeTime expiration_time_type = 5;  // pendings only
  optional google.protobuf.Timestamp expiration_time = 6;
  optional double stop_limit = 8;          // pendings only
}

Reply payload OrderModifyData (key fields): returned_code: u32, deal, order, volume, price, bid, ask, comment, returned_code_description.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description ticket u64 Order/position ticket (required). stop_loss Option<f64> New SL (absolute price). take_profit Option<f64> New TP (absolute price). price Option<f64> New trigger price — pending orders only. expiration_time_type Option<i32> Expiry policy — pendings only. expiration_time Option<Timestamp> Expiry time — pendings only. stop_limit Option<f64> New stop-limit price — pendings only.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderModifyData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description returned_code u32 10009 = success. price f64 Confirmed price. bid / ask f64 Prices at the operation. returned_code_description String Human-readable retcode.

docs.title: 🧱 Tmt5EnumOrderTypeTime (field expiration_time_type, pending orders)
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning Tmt5OrderTimeGtc 0 Good-till-cancelled (default) Tmt5OrderTimeDay 1 Valid for the current trading day Tmt5OrderTimeSpecified 2 Valid until expiration_time Tmt5OrderTimeSpecifiedDay 3 Valid until the end of expiration_time's day

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Only set what you change. Leave untouched fields as None — but note some servers want the SL/TP you intend to keep re-sent; when in doubt, send both stop_loss and take_profit.
  • price is for pendings. Modifying an open position's entry price is not possible — only SL/TP.
  • Absolute prices. SL/TP/price are price levels, not distances.
  • Respect stops level. New SL/TP must sit beyond SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL from the market.

docs.title: 1) Move SL to breakeven
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let entry = 1.08500;  // the position's open price
let res = account.order_modify(pb::OrderModifyRequest {
    ticket: 123456,
    stop_loss: Some(entry),       // breakeven
    take_profit: None,
    price: None, expiration_time_type: None, expiration_time: None, stop_limit: None,
}).await?;
println!("modify code {}", res.returned_code);

docs.title: 2) Set both SL and TP
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let res = account.order_modify(pb::OrderModifyRequest {
    ticket: 123456,
    stop_loss: Some(1.08300),
    take_profit: Some(1.09000),
    price: None, expiration_time_type: None, expiration_time: None, stop_limit: None,
}).await?;
if res.returned_code != 10009 { println!("rejected: {}", res.returned_code_description); }

docs.title: 3) Re-price a pending order
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let res = account.order_modify(pb::OrderModifyRequest {
    ticket: 123457,
    stop_loss: None, take_profit: None,
    price: Some(1.08000),   // new trigger
    expiration_time_type: None, expiration_time: None, stop_limit: None,
}).await?;
println!("re-price code {}", res.returned_code);

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Modifying a position's price. Not allowed — only SL/TP on open positions.
  • Clearing SL/TP unintentionally. If a server treats None as "clear", pass the value you want to keep.
  • Too-tight new stops. Rejected per stops level.
  • Ignoring returned_code.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Breakeven move. After a profitable open, set SL to entry → 10009; verify via opened_orders.
  • Invalid ticket. A non-existent ticket → rejection code.

docs.title: Order Send (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
Place a market or pending order, optionally with SL/TP, slippage, comment and magic number.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::order_send(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.TradeFunctions
  • RPC: OrderSend(OrderSendRequest) -> OrderSendReply
  • Payload: OrderSendData → returned_code: u32, deal, order, …

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL5 OrderSend — the one call that opens trades.
  • Why you need it. Market entries and pending orders, with SL/TP in one shot.
  • When to use. Entering a trade. For friendlier buy/sell-by-pips, use MT5Sugar.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_send(
    &self,
    request: pb::OrderSendRequest,
) -> Result<pb::OrderSendData, MT5Error>

Request message (key fields):

message OrderSendRequest {
  string symbol = 1;                     // REQUIRED
  Tmt5EnumOrderType operation = 2;       // Rust field: operation (i32)
  double volume = 3;                     // lots
  optional double price = 4;             // required for pendings; market uses current
  optional uint64 slippage = 5;          // max deviation, points
  optional double stop_loss = 6;
  optional double take_profit = 7;
  optional string comment = 8;
  optional uint64 expert_id = 9;         // magic number
  optional double stop_limit_price = 10;
  optional Tmt5EnumOrderTypeTime expiration_time_type = 11;
  optional google.protobuf.Timestamp expiration_time = 12;
  optional int32 quotes_wait_ms = 13;    // wait for first quote (default 5000, max 60000)
}

Reply payload OrderSendData (key fields): returned_code: u32, deal: u64, order: u64, volume: f64, price: f64, bid: f64, ask: f64, comment: String, returned_string_code, returned_code_description.

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol String Symbol (required). operation i32 (Tmt5EnumOrderType) Order type — see enum. volume f64 Lots. price Option<f64> Required for pendings; omit (None) for market. slippage Option<u64> Max price deviation, points. stop_loss / take_profit Option<f64> Absolute price levels. comment Option<String> Free text. expert_id Option<u64> Magic number. stop_limit_price Option<f64> For stop-limit orders. expiration_time_type / expiration_time Option<..> Pending expiry policy. quotes_wait_ms Option<i32> How long to wait for the first quote.

docs.title: Tmt5EnumOrderType
docs.text: Variant Value Variant Value Tmt5OrderTypeBuy 0 Tmt5OrderTypeSellLimit 3 Tmt5OrderTypeSell 1 Tmt5OrderTypeBuyStop 4 Tmt5OrderTypeBuyLimit 2 Tmt5OrderTypeSellStop 5 Tmt5OrderTypeBuyStopLimit 6 Tmt5OrderTypeSellStopLimit 7

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderSendData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description returned_code u32 10009 = success (TRADE_RETCODE_DONE). deal u64 Deal ticket (if executed). order u64 Order ticket (if placed). volume f64 Filled volume. price f64 Fill price. bid / ask f64 Prices at execution. comment String Broker comment. returned_code_description String Human-readable retcode.

docs.title: 🧱 Tmt5EnumOrderTypeTime (field expiration_time_type, pending orders)
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning Tmt5OrderTimeGtc 0 Good-till-cancelled (default) Tmt5OrderTimeDay 1 Valid for the current trading day Tmt5OrderTimeSpecified 2 Valid until expiration_time Tmt5OrderTimeSpecifiedDay 3 Valid until the end of expiration_time's day

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Check returned_code == 10009. Don't assume success — read the code every time.
  • Market vs pending. Market: operation Buy/Sell, price: None. Pending: a limit/stop type and a price.
  • SL/TP are absolute prices, not distances — compute them from the entry and point.
  • Respect stops level. SL/TP closer than SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL are rejected (see symbol_info_integer).

docs.title: 1) Market buy with SL/TP
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Tmt5EnumOrderType as OT;

let tick = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
let point = account.symbol_info_double(pb::SymbolInfoDoubleRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(), r#type: pb::SymbolInfoDoubleProperty::SymbolPoint as i32,
}).await?.value;

let res = account.order_send(pb::OrderSendRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    operation: OT::Tmt5OrderTypeBuy as i32,
    volume: 0.10,
    price: None,                                    // market
    slippage: Some(20),
    stop_loss: Some(tick.ask - 200.0 * point),      // 20 pips
    take_profit: Some(tick.ask + 400.0 * point),    // 40 pips
    comment: Some("demo entry".into()),
    expert_id: Some(12345),
    stop_limit_price: None, expiration_time_type: None, expiration_time: None, quotes_wait_ms: None,
}).await?;

if res.returned_code == 10009 { println!("opened, order #{}", res.order); }
else { println!("rejected: {} ({})", res.returned_code, res.returned_code_description); }

docs.title: 2) Buy limit (pending)
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Tmt5EnumOrderType as OT;

let bid = account.symbol_info_tick(pb::SymbolInfoTickRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?.bid;
let res = account.order_send(pb::OrderSendRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    operation: OT::Tmt5OrderTypeBuyLimit as i32,
    volume: 0.10,
    price: Some(bid - 0.0010),   // 10 pips below market
    slippage: None, stop_loss: None, take_profit: None,
    comment: Some("limit".into()), expert_id: Some(12345),
    stop_limit_price: None, expiration_time_type: None, expiration_time: None, quotes_wait_ms: None,
}).await?;
println!("pending #{} code {}", res.order, res.returned_code);

docs.title: 3) Minimal market sell
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Tmt5EnumOrderType as OT;

let res = account.order_send(pb::OrderSendRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(), operation: OT::Tmt5OrderTypeSell as i32, volume: 0.01,
    price: None, slippage: Some(30), stop_loss: None, take_profit: None,
    comment: None, expert_id: None, stop_limit_price: None,
    expiration_time_type: None, expiration_time: None, quotes_wait_ms: None,
}).await?;
println!("code {}", res.returned_code);

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Ignoring returned_code. A non-10009 code means it didn't open as asked.
  • Pending without price. Limits/stops require price: Some(..).
  • SL/TP as distances. They're absolute prices.
  • Invalid stops. Too-tight SL/TP → rejection; check the stops level first.
  • Enum as i32. operation: OT::Tmt5OrderTypeBuy as i32.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Demo market buy. returned_code == 10009, order > 0; then it shows up in opened_orders.
  • Bad volume. Below VolumeMin → rejection with a descriptive code.
  • Too-tight SL. Rejected per stops level.

docs.title: 6. Streaming Methods — Overview
docs.text:
Real-time server-push streams: ticks, trade events, live position profit, ticket lists, and raw trade transactions.

Unlike every other group, these return a stream, not a single value. Each method yields:

Result<impl tokio_stream::Stream<Item = Result<…Data, MT5Error>>, MT5Error>

The outer Result reports whether the subscription opened; then you iterate the stream, and each item is either a data frame or an MT5Error. Under the hood they use the gateway's SubscriptionService and carry the usual apikey + terminal id metadata.

docs.title: Methods in this group
docs.text: Method Item type One-liner on_symbol_tick(req) OnSymbolTickData Live ticks for one or more symbols. on_trade(req) OnTradeData Trade events (orders/positions/deals change) + account snapshot. on_position_profit(req) OnPositionProfitData Per-position floating P/L on a timer (new/updated/deleted). on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(req) OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData Open-position & pending-order ticket lists on a timer. on_trade_transaction(req) OnTradeTransactionData The raw MT5 OnTradeTransaction feed (transaction + request + result).

docs.title: Consuming a stream (pattern)
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;  // brings `.next()` into scope
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut stream = account
    .on_symbol_tick(pb::OnSymbolTickRequest { symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into()] })
    .await?;                       // subscription opened

while let Some(item) = stream.next().await {
    match item {
        Ok(data) => { /* handle frame */ }
        Err(e)   => { eprintln!("stream error: {e}"); break; }
    }
}
  • Timer-based streams (on_position_profit, on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets) push every timer_period_milliseconds.
  • Event-based streams (on_trade, on_trade_transaction) push when something actually changes.
  • on_symbol_tick pushes on every new tick for the subscribed symbols.
  • Dropping the stream unsubscribes.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text:
• Live prices → on_symbol_tick (vs polling symbol_info_tick).
  • React to fills/closes → on_trade or the lower-level on_trade_transaction.
  • Live P/L dashboard → on_position_profit.
  • Track what's open without re-fetching details → on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets.

Back to: MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: On Position Profit (stream)
docs.text:
Per-position floating P/L, pushed on a timer — new, updated and closed positions each call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::on_position_profit(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnPositionProfit(OnPositionProfitRequest) -> stream OnPositionProfitReply
  • Item payload: OnPositionProfitData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A timer-driven stream of each open position's live profit.
  • Why you need it. A live P/L dashboard without hammering opened_orders.
  • When to use. Monitoring floating P/L; driving trailing/breakeven logic off real-time profit.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn on_position_profit(
    &self,
    request: pb::OnPositionProfitRequest,
) -> Result<impl tokio_stream::Stream<Item = Result<pb::OnPositionProfitData, MT5Error>>, MT5Error>

Request / item:

message OnPositionProfitRequest {
  int32 timer_period_milliseconds = 1;
  bool  ignore_empty_data = 2;
}

message OnPositionProfitData {
  Mt5SubEnumEventGroupType type = 1;                       // Rust field: r#type
  repeated OnPositionProfitPositionInfo new_positions = 2;
  repeated OnPositionProfitPositionInfo updated_positions = 3;
  repeated OnPositionProfitPositionInfo deleted_positions = 4;
  // + server_time
}

message OnPositionProfitPositionInfo {
  int32  index = 1;
  int64  ticket = 2;
  double profit = 3;
  string position_symbol = 4;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description timer_period_milliseconds i32 How often to push (e.g. 1000 = every second). ignore_empty_data bool true → skip frames with no changes (less noise).

docs.title: ⬆️ Item — OnPositionProfitData
docs.text:
Field Rust type Description r#type i32 (Mt5SubEnumEventGroupType) Event group. new_positions Vec<OnPositionProfitPositionInfo> Positions that appeared since last frame. updated_positions Vec<OnPositionProfitPositionInfo> Positions with changed profit. deleted_positions Vec<OnPositionProfitPositionInfo> Positions closed since last frame.

Each OnPositionProfitPositionInfo: ticket: i64, profit: f64, position_symbol: String.

docs.title: 🧱 Mt5SubEnumEventGroupType (field r#type)
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning OrderProfit 0 Position-profit group update OrderUpdate 1 Order / position change group

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Three deltas per frame. Merge new + updated into your map, remove deleted.
  • ignore_empty_data: true keeps the stream quiet when nothing changed.
  • Pick a sane period. 500–1000 ms is plenty for a dashboard; smaller means more frames.
  • ticket is i64 here (the detail structs use u64).

docs.title: 1) Live total floating P/L
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use std::collections::HashMap;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_position_profit(pb::OnPositionProfitRequest {
    timer_period_milliseconds: 1000,
    ignore_empty_data: true,
}).await?;

let mut book: HashMap<i64, f64> = HashMap::new();
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    for p in d.new_positions.iter().chain(d.updated_positions.iter()) {
        book.insert(p.ticket, p.profit);
    }
    for p in &d.deleted_positions { book.remove(&p.ticket); }
    let total: f64 = book.values().sum();
    println!("floating P/L: {total:+.2} ({} positions)", book.len());
}

docs.title: 2) Alert when a position crosses a profit target
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_position_profit(pb::OnPositionProfitRequest { timer_period_milliseconds: 500, ignore_empty_data: true }).await?;
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    for p in d.updated_positions {
        if p.profit >= 100.0 { println!("#{} ({}) hit +{:.2}", p.ticket, p.position_symbol, p.profit); }
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Detect closes
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_position_profit(pb::OnPositionProfitRequest { timer_period_milliseconds: 1000, ignore_empty_data: false }).await?;
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    for p in d.deleted_positions { println!("closed #{} ({})", p.ticket, p.position_symbol); }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Reading only one list. You must merge new/updated and honor deleted to keep an accurate book.
  • Tiny timer period. Floods you with frames; 500–1000 ms is usually enough.
  • Ticket type. i64 here vs u64 elsewhere — cast when cross-referencing.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• With an open position. updated_positions carries its ticket; profit moves with price.
  • Close it. It appears once in deleted_positions, then no more.
  • Flat + ignore_empty_data. Stream stays quiet.

docs.title: 📚 See also
docs.text:
• opened_orders · on_trade · on_symbol_tick
  • Back to: Streaming Methods — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: On Positions And Pending Orders Tickets (stream)
docs.text:
Open-position and pending-order ticket lists, pushed on a timer — a lightweight "what's open now" feed.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTickets(...) -> stream
  • Item payload: OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A timer stream of just the ticket ids for open positions and pendings.
  • Why you need it. Cheap way to notice opens/closes without pulling full details each time.
  • When to use. Keeping a live set of active tickets; diffing to detect fills/cancellations.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(
    &self,
    request: pb::OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsRequest,
) -> Result<impl tokio_stream::Stream<Item = Result<pb::OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData, MT5Error>>, MT5Error>

Request / item:

message OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsRequest {
  int32 timer_period_milliseconds = 1;
}

message OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData {
  repeated uint64 position_tickets = 1;
  repeated uint64 pending_order_tickets = 2;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp server_time = 3;
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 4;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description timer_period_milliseconds i32 Push interval (e.g. 1000).

docs.title: ⬆️ Item — OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData
docs.text:
Field Rust type Description position_tickets Vec<u64> Current open-position tickets. pending_order_tickets Vec<u64> Current pending-order tickets. server_time Option<Timestamp> Server time of the snapshot. terminal_instance_guid_id String Originating terminal session.

Note: tickets are u64 here (vs i64 in the non-streaming opened_orders_tickets).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Full snapshot each frame. Every push is the complete current set — diff against your last set to find adds/removes.
  • Lighter than on_trade + fetch. Ids only; fetch details only when the set changes.
  • Pick a modest period. 1000 ms is fine for most monitors.

docs.title: 1) Detect opens and closes by diffing
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use std::collections::HashSet;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(
    pb::OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsRequest { timer_period_milliseconds: 1000 },
).await?;

let mut prev: HashSet<u64> = HashSet::new();
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    let now: HashSet<u64> = d.position_tickets.iter().copied().collect();
    for t in now.difference(&prev) { println!("opened position {t}"); }
    for t in prev.difference(&now) { println!("closed position {t}"); }
    prev = now;
}

docs.title: 2) Keep live counts
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(
    pb::OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsRequest { timer_period_milliseconds: 2000 },
).await?;
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    println!("{} positions, {} pendings", d.position_tickets.len(), d.pending_order_tickets.len());
}

docs.title: 3) Fetch details only on change
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(
    pb::OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsRequest { timer_period_milliseconds: 1000 },
).await?;
let mut last_len = usize::MAX;
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    if d.position_tickets.len() != last_len {
        last_len = d.position_tickets.len();
        // set changed — pull full detail once
        let _ = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest {
            input_sort_mode: pb::Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType::Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOpenTimeAsc as i32,
        }).await?;
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Treating a frame as a delta. It's a full snapshot — diff it yourself.
  • Ticket type. u64 here; cast if comparing with i64 sources.
  • Count-only change detection misses swaps. A close + open between frames can keep the count equal — diff the sets, not just lengths, when correctness matters.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Open a trade. Its ticket appears in position_tickets on the next frame.
  • Place a pending. It shows in pending_order_tickets; on fill it moves to position_tickets.

docs.text:
• opened_orders_tickets · on_trade
  • Back to: Streaming Methods — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview

docs.title: On Symbol Tick (stream)
docs.text:
Live tick updates for one or more symbols — the push alternative to polling symbol_info_tick.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::on_symbol_tick(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnSymbolTick(OnSymbolTickRequest) -> stream OnSymbolTickReply
  • Item payload: OnSymbolTickData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A server-push stream of ticks for the symbols you subscribe to.
  • Why you need it. React to every price change without a polling loop.
  • When to use. Live dashboards, tick-driven strategies. For a one-off quote use symbol_info_tick.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn on_symbol_tick(
    &self,
    request: pb::OnSymbolTickRequest,
) -> Result<impl tokio_stream::Stream<Item = Result<pb::OnSymbolTickData, MT5Error>>, MT5Error>

Request / item:

message OnSymbolTickRequest { repeated string symbol_names = 1; }

message OnSymbolTickData {
  MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick symbol_tick = 1;   // optional
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 2;
}

message MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick {
  google.protobuf.Timestamp time = 1;
  double bid = 2; double ask = 3; double last = 4;
  uint64 volume = 5; int64 time_msc = 6; uint32 flags = 7;
  double volume_real = 8; string symbol = 9;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: Param Rust type Description symbol_names Vec<String> One or more symbols to stream.

docs.title: ⬆️ Item — OnSymbolTickData
docs.text:
Field Rust type Description symbol_tick Option<MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick> The tick (bid/ask/last/volume/time + symbol). terminal_instance_guid_id String Originating terminal session.

MrpcSubscriptionMqlTick mirrors MrpcMqlTick but time is a Timestamp and it adds the symbol field (handy when streaming many).

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Select the symbols first so the feed is live.
  • symbol_tick is Option. Guard before using.
  • symbol disambiguates. With multiple subscriptions, route by symbol_tick.symbol.
  • Drop to unsubscribe. Ending the loop / dropping the stream stops the feed.

docs.title: 1) Stream EURUSD ticks
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_symbol_tick(pb::OnSymbolTickRequest { symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into()] }).await?;
while let Some(item) = s.next().await {
    match item {
        Ok(d) => if let Some(t) = d.symbol_tick {
            println!("{} {:.5}/{:.5}", t.symbol, t.bid, t.ask);
        },
        Err(e) => { eprintln!("stream error: {e}"); break; }
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Several symbols, routed by name
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_symbol_tick(pb::OnSymbolTickRequest {
    symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into(), "GBPUSD".into()],
}).await?;
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    if let Some(t) = d.symbol_tick {
        println!("[{}] mid {:.5}", t.symbol, (t.bid + t.ask) / 2.0);
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Stop after N ticks
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_symbol_tick(pb::OnSymbolTickRequest { symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into()] }).await?;
let mut n = 0;
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    if d.symbol_tick.is_some() { n += 1; }
    if n >= 10 { break; }   // dropping `s` unsubscribes
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Forgetting use tokio_stream::StreamExt;. .next() won't resolve otherwise.
  • Unwrapping symbol_tick. It's an Option.
  • Blocking the runtime. Do heavy work off the stream task (e.g. tokio::spawn).

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• During market hours. Frames arrive steadily; bid/ask populated.
  • Closed market. Few/no frames — your loop just waits.

docs.text:
• symbol_info_tick · on_position_profit

docs.title: On Trade (stream)
docs.text:
Trade events — whenever orders, positions or deals change — with an account snapshot attached.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::on_trade(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnTrade(OnTradeRequest) -> stream OnTradeReply
  • Item payload: OnTradeData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The MT5 OnTrade event feed — pushes when your trading state changes.
  • Why you need it. React to fills, closes and modifications without polling opened_orders.
  • When to use. Event-driven bots and live blotters. For the raw transaction detail, see on_trade_transaction.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn on_trade(
    &self,
    request: pb::OnTradeRequest,
) -> Result<impl tokio_stream::Stream<Item = Result<pb::OnTradeData, MT5Error>>, MT5Error>

Request / item:

message OnTradeRequest {}   // no fields

message OnTradeData {
  Mt5SubEnumEventGroupType type = 1;          // Rust field: r#type (i32)
  OnTadeEventData event_data = 2;             // optional
  OnEventAccountInfo account_info = 3;        // optional
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 4;
}

message OnEventAccountInfo {
  double balance = 1; double credit = 2; double equity = 3;
  double margin = 4; double free_margin = 5; double profit = 6;
  double margin_level = 7; int64 login = 8;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: None — pass pb::OnTradeRequest {}.

docs.title: ⬆️ Item — OnTradeData
docs.text:
Field Rust type Description r#type i32 (Mt5SubEnumEventGroupType) Which event group changed. event_data Option<OnTadeEventData> Details of the change. account_info Option<OnEventAccountInfo> Balance/equity/margin snapshot at the event. terminal_instance_guid_id String Originating terminal session.

OnEventAccountInfo gives live balance, equity, margin, free_margin, profit, margin_level — a cheap way to keep an account header fresh on every trade event.

docs.title: 🧱 Mt5SubEnumEventGroupType (field r#type)
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning OrderProfit 0 Position-profit group update OrderUpdate 1 Order / position change group

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Event-driven. Frames arrive only when something changes — quiet periods are silent.
  • Both sub-messages are Option. Guard before use.
  • r#type is a raw identifier (Rust keyword).
  • Snapshot included. Use account_info to update equity/margin without a separate account_summary call.

docs.title: 1) Log trade events with equity
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_trade(pb::OnTradeRequest {}).await?;
while let Some(item) = s.next().await {
    match item {
        Ok(d) => {
            if let Some(a) = d.account_info {
                println!("event type {} | equity {:.2} free {:.2}", d.r#type, a.equity, a.free_margin);
            }
        }
        Err(e) => { eprintln!("stream error: {e}"); break; }
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Trigger a re-sync on any event
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_trade(pb::OnTradeRequest {}).await?;
while let Some(Ok(_)) = s.next().await {
    // something changed — refresh the full picture
    let data = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest {
        input_sort_mode: pb::Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType::Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOpenTimeAsc as i32,
    }).await?;
    println!("now {} open position(s)", data.position_infos.len());
}

docs.title: 3) Watch margin level drop
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_trade(pb::OnTradeRequest {}).await?;
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    if let Some(a) = d.account_info {
        if a.margin_level != 0.0 && a.margin_level < 150.0 {
            println!("[ALERT] margin level {:.0}%", a.margin_level);
        }
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Expecting periodic frames. This is event-driven, not a timer — use on_position_profit for steady P/L ticks.
  • Unwrapping Option fields.
  • Heavy work inline. Offload to a spawned task to keep consuming promptly.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Open a trade. A frame arrives soon after order_send; account_info.margin rises.
  • Close it. Another frame; free_margin recovers.

docs.title: On Trade Transaction (stream)
docs.text:
The raw MT5 OnTradeTransaction feed — each transaction with its originating request and result.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT5Account::on_trade_transaction(request) (defined in src/mt5/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt5_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnTradeTransaction(OnTradeTransactionRequest) -> stream
  • Item payload: OnTradeTransactionData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The lowest-level trade feed: MT5's MqlTradeTransaction plus the MqlTradeRequest and MqlTradeResult that produced it.
  • Why you need it. Precise, step-by-step audit of order lifecycle (add/update/delete/deal-add) that on_trade summarizes.
  • When to use. Detailed execution tracking, reconciliation, debugging order flow.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn on_trade_transaction(
    &self,
    request: pb::OnTradeTransactionRequest,
) -> Result<impl tokio_stream::Stream<Item = Result<pb::OnTradeTransactionData, MT5Error>>, MT5Error>

Request / item:

message OnTradeTransactionRequest {}   // no fields

message OnTradeTransactionData {
  Mt5SubEnumEventGroupType type = 1;         // Rust field: r#type
  MqlTradeTransaction trade_transaction = 2; // optional — the transaction
  MqlTradeRequest     trade_request = 3;     // optional — the request behind it
  MqlTradeResult      trade_result = 4;      // optional — the result
  string …guid… = 5;
}

docs.title: 🔽 Input
docs.text: None — pass pb::OnTradeTransactionRequest {}.

docs.title: ⬆️ Item — OnTradeTransactionData
docs.text:
Field Rust type Description r#type i32 (Mt5SubEnumEventGroupType) Event group. trade_transaction Option<MqlTradeTransaction> The transaction (type: order add/update/delete, deal add, …). trade_request Option<MqlTradeRequest> The request that caused it (when applicable). trade_result Option<MqlTradeResult> The server result (retcode etc.).

Transaction kinds come from SubEnumTradeTransactionType — e.g. OrderAdd (0), OrderUpdate (1), OrderDelete (2), DealAdd (3), DealUpdate (4), …

docs.title: 🧱 Enums
docs.text:
Mt5SubEnumEventGroupType (field r#type): OrderProfit = 0, OrderUpdate = 1.

SubEnumTradeTransactionType — the transaction kind inside trade_transaction:

Variant Value Variant Value SubTradeTransactionOrderAdd 0 SubTradeTransactionDealDelete 5 SubTradeTransactionOrderUpdate 1 SubTradeTransactionHistoryAdd 6 SubTradeTransactionOrderDelete 2 SubTradeTransactionHistoryUpdate 7 SubTradeTransactionDealAdd 3 SubTradeTransactionHistoryDelete 8 SubTradeTransactionDealUpdate 4 SubTradeTransactionPosition 9 SubTradeTransactionRequest 10

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• More granular than on_trade. You see each sub-step (order placed → partially filled → deal added), not just "something changed".
  • All three sub-messages are Option. Many transactions carry only the transaction; request/result appear for operations you initiated.
  • r#type is a raw identifier.
  • Prefer on_trade if you only need "refresh my view" — this feed is noisier.

docs.title: 1) Log every transaction
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_trade_transaction(pb::OnTradeTransactionRequest {}).await?;
while let Some(item) = s.next().await {
    match item {
        Ok(d) => {
            if let Some(tx) = &d.trade_transaction { let _ = tx; println!("transaction (group {})", d.r#type); }
            if let Some(r)  = &d.trade_result      { let _ = r;  println!("  result attached"); }
        }
        Err(e) => { eprintln!("stream error: {e}"); break; }
    }
}

docs.title: 2) React only to deal additions
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_trade_transaction(pb::OnTradeTransactionRequest {}).await?;
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    if d.trade_transaction.is_some() {
        // inspect the transaction's own type field (SubEnumTradeTransactionType) to filter DealAdd
        println!("tx event, group {}", d.r#type);
    }
}

docs.title: 3) Capture results of your own requests
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_trade_transaction(pb::OnTradeTransactionRequest {}).await?;
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    if let (Some(_req), Some(_res)) = (&d.trade_request, &d.trade_result) {
        println!("request → result pair received");
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Noise. This feed is detailed; filter by transaction type rather than reacting to everything.
  • Unwrapping Options. Each sub-message may be absent.
  • Not a snapshot. It reports transitions; keep your own state if you need current totals.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Send an order. You see an order-add transaction, then a deal-add on fill.
  • Modify SL/TP. An order-update transaction arrives.

docs.text:

docs.title: MT5Service — 1. Account Information
docs.text:
Account snapshot + single typed properties, returned as clean scalars (f64/i64/String) instead of protobuf …Data.

Layer: MID — friendly wrappers over MT5Account. Defined in src/mt5/service.rs.

docs.title: The 4 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Tier Delegates to account_summary() AccountSummaryData ⚪ pass-through account.account_summary() account_double(property_id) f64 🟢 clean account.account_info_double(..).requested_value account_integer(property_id) i64 🟢 clean account.account_info_integer(..).requested_value account_string(property_id) String 🟢 clean account.account_info_string(..).requested_value

Where the value is: the three account_* getters take a typed property enum and hand back the bare value — no …Request to build, no .requested_value to pull out. account_summary() is a straight pass-through (returns the same AccountSummaryData as the low-level call).

Unlike the Python facade, this account_summary() does not fan out extra RPCs for margin/free-margin — read those with account_double(AccountMargin…). See the low-level account_summary for the exact AccountSummaryData fields.

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:
pub async fn account_summary(&self) -> Result<pb::AccountSummaryData, MT5Error>

pub async fn account_double(&self, property_id: pb::AccountInfoDoublePropertyType) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>
pub async fn account_integer(&self, property_id: pb::AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType) -> Result<i64, MT5Error>
pub async fn account_string(&self, property_id: pb::AccountInfoStringPropertyType) -> Result<String, MT5Error>

Note the argument is the typed enum (e.g. AccountInfoDoublePropertyType::AccountBalance), not an i32 — the Service does the cast.

docs.title: Property enums (common values)
docs.text:
AccountInfoDoublePropertyType: AccountBalance=0, AccountCredit=1, AccountProfit=2, AccountEquity=3, AccountMargin=4, AccountMarginFree=5, AccountMarginLevel=6, … (see account_info_double for the full 14).

AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType: AccountLogin=0, AccountTradeMode=1, AccountLeverage=2, AccountTradeAllowed=5, AccountTradeExpert=6, … (11 total).

AccountInfoStringPropertyType: AccountName=0, AccountServer=1, AccountCurrency=2, AccountCompany=3.

docs.title: 1) Read single properties as scalars
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::{AccountInfoDoublePropertyType as D, AccountInfoIntegerPropertyType as I, AccountInfoStringPropertyType as S};

let balance  = service.account_double(D::AccountBalance).await?;      // f64
let free     = service.account_double(D::AccountMarginFree).await?;   // f64
let leverage = service.account_integer(I::AccountLeverage).await?;    // i64
let currency = service.account_string(S::AccountCurrency).await?;     // String

println!("{balance:.2} {currency}  free {free:.2}  1:{leverage}");

docs.title: 2) Account banner from the summary
docs.text:
let s = service.account_summary().await?;
println!("#{}  {}  equity {:.2} {}", s.account_login, s.account_company_name, s.account_equity, s.account_currency);

docs.title: 3) Margin picture (fields not in the summary)
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::AccountInfoDoublePropertyType as D;

let margin = service.account_double(D::AccountMargin).await?;
let level  = service.account_double(D::AccountMarginLevel).await?;  // percent
println!("margin {margin:.2}, level {level:.1}%");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Typed enum, not i32. Pass D::AccountBalance, not 0 — the Service casts internally.
  • No margin in the summary. Use account_double(AccountMargin/…MarginFree/…MarginLevel).
  • Margin level is a percent.

docs.title: MT5Service — 2. Symbol Information
docs.text:
Discovery, quotes, properties, sessions and bulk params — with &str symbols, typed property enums, and scalar returns where it makes sense.

Layer: MID over MT5Account Symbol Information. Defined in src/mt5/service.rs.

docs.title: The 13 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Tier Delegates to symbols_total(selected_only) i32 🟢 clean symbols_total(..).total symbol_exist(name) SymbolExistData ⚪ pass-through symbol_exist(..) symbol_name(index, selected_only) String 🟢 clean symbol_name(..).name symbol_select(symbol, select) bool 🟢 clean symbol_select(..).success symbol_is_synchronized(symbol) bool 🟢 clean symbol_is_synchronized(..).synchronized symbol_double(symbol, property) f64 🟢 clean symbol_info_double(..).value symbol_integer(symbol, property) i64 🟢 clean symbol_info_integer(..).value symbol_string(symbol, property) String 🟢 clean symbol_info_string(..).value symbol_margin_rate(symbol, order_type) SymbolInfoMarginRateData 🔵 friendly args symbol_info_margin_rate(..) symbol_tick(symbol) MrpcMqlTick 🔵 friendly args symbol_info_tick(..) symbol_session_quote(symbol, day, session_index) SymbolInfoSessionQuoteData 🔵 friendly args symbol_info_session_quote(..) symbol_session_trade(symbol, day, session_index) SymbolInfoSessionTradeData 🔵 friendly args symbol_info_session_trade(..) symbol_params_many(symbol_name, page_number, items_per_page) SymbolParamsManyData 🔵 friendly args symbol_params_many(..) (sort = None)

Where the value is: the getters unwrap to a scalar (i32/String/bool/f64/i64), and every method takes a &str symbol + typed property/DayOfWeek/EnumOrderType enum so you never build a …Request or cast to i32.

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:

pub async fn symbol_integer(&self, symbol: &str, property: pb::SymbolInfoIntegerProperty) -> Result<i64, MT5Error>

symbol_params_many always passes sort_type: None to the low layer. If you need sorting, call MT5Account::symbol_params_many directly via service.account().

Property enums come straight from the low-level pages — symbol_info_double, integer, string. DayOfWeek: Sunday=0 … Saturday=6.

docs.title: 1) Exists → select → quote
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;

if service.symbol_exist("EURUSD").await?.exists {
    service.symbol_select("EURUSD", true).await?;           // bool
    let t = service.symbol_tick("EURUSD").await?;            // MrpcMqlTick
    println!("bid/ask {:.5}/{:.5}", t.bid, t.ask);
}

docs.title: 2) Properties as scalars
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::{SymbolInfoDoubleProperty as D, SymbolInfoIntegerProperty as I};

let point  = service.symbol_double("EURUSD", D::SymbolPoint).await?;   // f64
let digits = service.symbol_integer("EURUSD", I::SymbolDigits).await?; // i64
println!("point {point}, digits {digits}");

docs.title: 3) Full spec of one symbol
docs.text:
let data = service.symbol_params_many(Some("EURUSD".into()), None, None).await?;
if let Some(p) = data.symbol_infos.first() {
    println!("{}: contract {}, bid {:.5}", p.name, p.point, p.bid);
}

docs.title: 4) Is the market open today?
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::DayOfWeek as Dow;

let s = service.symbol_session_trade("EURUSD", Dow::Monday, 0).await?;
println!("trade session present: {}", s.from.is_some());

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Typed enums, &str symbols — no manual …Request or as i32.
  • symbol_params_many has no sort here — use the low layer if you need it.
  • Select before quoting/history — same rule as the low level.
  • symbol_exist is a pass-through — returns SymbolExistData (.exists, .is_custom), not a bare bool.

docs.title: MT5Service — 3. Positions & Orders
docs.text:
Open book, ticket lists and history — with typed sort enums and a scalar positions_total.

Layer: MID over MT5Account Positions & Orders. Defined in src/mt5/service.rs.

docs.title: The 5 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Tier Delegates to positions_total() i32 🟢 clean positions_total().total_positions opened_orders(sort_mode) OpenedOrdersData 🔵 friendly args opened_orders(..) opened_orders_tickets() OpenedOrdersTicketsData ⚪ pass-through opened_orders_tickets(default) order_history(sort_mode, from, to, page, per_page) OrdersHistoryData 🔵 friendly args order_history(..) positions_history(sort_type, from, to, page, per_page) PositionsHistoryData 🔵 friendly args positions_history(..)

docs.title: Sort enums
docs.text:
• Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType: ...SortByOpenTimeAsc=0, ...Desc=1, ...SortByOrderTicketIdAsc=2, ...Desc=3.
  • Bmt5EnumOrderHistorySortType: open/close/ticket × asc/desc (0–5).
  • AhEnumPositionsHistorySortType: AhPositionOpenTimeAsc=0, ...Desc=1, AhPositionTicketAsc=2, ...Desc=3.

Field tables for OpenedOrdersData (position_infos + opened_orders), OrdersHistoryData and PositionsHistoryData live in the low-level opened_orders, order_history and positions_history pages.

docs.title: 1) Count + list open positions
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Bmt5EnumOpenedOrderSortType as Sort;

if service.positions_total().await? > 0 {
    let data = service.opened_orders(Sort::Bmt5OpenedOrderSortByOpenTimeAsc).await?;
    for p in &data.position_infos {
        println!("#{} {} {:.2} lot  P/L {:+.2}", p.ticket, p.symbol, p.volume, p.profit);
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Last 7 days of order history
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Bmt5EnumOrderHistorySortType as Sort;

fn ts(s: i64) -> prost_types::Timestamp { prost_types::Timestamp { seconds: s, nanos: 0 } }
let now = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp();

let h = service.order_history(Sort::Bmt5SortByCloseTimeDesc, Some(ts(now - 7*86_400)), Some(ts(now)), 0, 50).await?;
println!("{} rows", h.array_total);

docs.title: 3) Closed positions, net realized
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::AhEnumPositionsHistorySortType as Sort;

fn ts(s: i64) -> prost_types::Timestamp { prost_types::Timestamp { seconds: s, nanos: 0 } }
let now = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp();

let data = service.positions_history(Sort::AhPositionOpenTimeDesc, Some(ts(now - 30*86_400)), Some(ts(now)), Some(0), Some(100)).await?;
let net: f64 = data.history_positions.iter().map(|p| p.profit + p.swap + p.commission + p.fee).sum();
println!("net realized (30d): {net:+.2}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• order_history paging is required i32 (page_number, items_per_page); positions_history uses Option<i32>.
  • Ranges are Option<Timestamp> — build prost_types::Timestamp { seconds, nanos }.
  • opened_orders_tickets tickets are i64 (see the low-level note); the streaming variant uses u64.

docs.title: MT5Service — 4. Market Depth (DOM)
docs.text:
Subscribe → read → release the order book, each by a plain &str symbol.

Layer: MID over MT5Account Market Depth. Defined in src/mt5/service.rs.

docs.title: The 3 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Tier Delegates to subscribe_market_depth(symbol) MarketBookAddData 🔵 friendly args market_book_add(..) market_depth(symbol) MarketBookGetData 🔵 friendly args market_book_get(..) unsubscribe_market_depth(symbol) MarketBookReleaseData 🔵 friendly args market_book_release(..)

Where the value is: friendlier names (subscribe/unsubscribe) and a &str symbol instead of building each MarketBook*Request. The lifecycle is the same as the low level: subscribe once → read repeatedly → release.

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:
pub async fn subscribe_market_depth(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<pb::MarketBookAddData, MT5Error>
pub async fn market_depth(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<pb::MarketBookGetData, MT5Error>
pub async fn unsubscribe_market_depth(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<pb::MarketBookReleaseData, MT5Error>
  • MarketBookAddData.opened_successfully: bool
  • MarketBookReleaseData.closed_successfully: bool
  • MarketBookGetData.mql_book_infos: Vec<MrpcMqlBookInfo> — each level has r#type (BookType: Sell=0, Buy=1, SellMarket=2, BuyMarket=3), price, volume, volume_real. Full detail: low-level market_book_get.

docs.title: 1) Full lifecycle
docs.text:
let ok = service.subscribe_market_depth("EURUSD").await?.opened_successfully;
if ok {
    let book = service.market_depth("EURUSD").await?;
    println!("{} levels", book.mql_book_infos.len());
    service.unsubscribe_market_depth("EURUSD").await?;
}

docs.title: 2) Best bid / best ask
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::BookType;

service.subscribe_market_depth("EURUSD").await?;
let book = service.market_depth("EURUSD").await?;
let best_bid = book.mql_book_infos.iter()
    .filter(|l| matches!(BookType::try_from(l.r#type), Ok(BookType::Buy)))
    .map(|l| l.price).fold(f64::MIN, f64::max);
let best_ask = book.mql_book_infos.iter()
    .filter(|l| matches!(BookType::try_from(l.r#type), Ok(BookType::Sell)))
    .map(|l| l.price).fold(f64::MAX, f64::min);
println!("book spread {:.5}", best_ask - best_bid);
service.unsubscribe_market_depth("EURUSD").await?;

docs.title: 3) Depth per side
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::BookType;

let book = service.market_depth("EURUSD").await?;
let (bid, ask) = book.mql_book_infos.iter().fold((0i64, 0i64), |(b, a), l| match BookType::try_from(l.r#type) {
    Ok(BookType::Buy) => (b + l.volume, a),
    Ok(BookType::Sell) => (b, a + l.volume),
    _ => (b, a),
});
println!("bid depth {bid}, ask depth {ask}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Subscribe first. market_depth returns nothing useful without a prior subscribe_market_depth.
  • Always release. Balance every subscribe with an unsubscribe.
  • FX often has no DOM — opened_successfully may be false.
