docs.title: MT5Service — 5. Trading Operations
docs.text:
Send/modify/close/check orders (raw requests) + margin/profit calculators (friendly args).

Layer: MID over MT5Account Trading Operations. Defined in src/mt5/service.rs.

docs.title: The 6 methods
docs.text:
Method Returns Tier Delegates to place_order(request) OrderSendData ⚪ pass-through order_send(..) modify_order(request) OrderModifyData ⚪ pass-through order_modify(..) close_order(request) OrderCloseData ⚪ pass-through order_close(..) check_order(request) OrderCheckData ⚪ pass-through order_check(..) calculate_margin(symbol, order_type, volume, open_price) OrderCalcMarginData 🔵 friendly args order_calc_margin(..) calculate_profit(symbol, order_type, volume, open_price, close_price) OrderCalcProfitData 🔵 friendly args order_calc_profit(..)

Design note: order construction (symbol/side/volume → OrderSendRequest, pip-based SL/TP, risk sizing) is deliberately not here — that's MT5Sugar's job. At this layer place_order/modify_order/close_order/check_order take the protobuf request directly (mirroring the Python facade), so they're pass-throughs. The two calculators do add friendly args: &str symbol + typed EnumOrderTypeTf, returning the …Data.

docs.title: Signatures
docs.text:
pub async fn place_order(&self, request: pb::OrderSendRequest) -> Result<pb::OrderSendData, MT5Error>
pub async fn modify_order(&self, request: pb::OrderModifyRequest) -> Result<pb::OrderModifyData, MT5Error>
pub async fn close_order(&self, request: pb::OrderCloseRequest) -> Result<pb::OrderCloseData, MT5Error>
pub async fn check_order(&self, request: pb::OrderCheckRequest) -> Result<pb::OrderCheckData, MT5Error>

pub async fn calculate_margin(
    &self, symbol: &str, order_type: pb::EnumOrderTypeTf, volume: f64, open_price: f64,
) -> Result<pb::OrderCalcMarginData, MT5Error>

pub async fn calculate_profit(
    &self, symbol: &str, order_type: pb::EnumOrderTypeTf, volume: f64, open_price: f64, close_price: f64,
) -> Result<pb::OrderCalcProfitData, MT5Error>
  • Return code: OrderSendData.returned_code / OrderCloseData.returned_code — 10009 = success. See Return Codes.
  • EnumOrderTypeTf: OrderTypeTfBuy=0, OrderTypeTfSell=1, OrderTypeTfBuyLimit=2, …
  • Request/field tables: low-level order_send, order_modify, order_close, order_check.

docs.title: 1) Check → place (the safe flow)
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use pb::Tmt5EnumOrderType as OT;

// validate
let check = service.check_order(pb::OrderCheckRequest {
    mql_trade_request: Some(pb::MrpcMqlTradeRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into(), volume: 0.10, price: 1.085, ..Default::default() }),
}).await?;
let ok = check.mql_trade_check_result.map(|r| r.returned_code == 10009).unwrap_or(false);

if ok {
    let res = service.place_order(pb::OrderSendRequest {
        symbol: "EURUSD".into(), operation: OT::Tmt5OrderTypeBuy as i32, volume: 0.10,
        price: None, slippage: Some(20), stop_loss: None, take_profit: None,
        comment: Some("svc".into()), expert_id: Some(1), stop_limit_price: None,
        expiration_time_type: None, expiration_time: None, quotes_wait_ms: None,
    }).await?;
    println!("send code {}", res.returned_code);
}

docs.title: 2) Margin for a would-be order
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::EnumOrderTypeTf as TF;

let price = service.symbol_tick("EURUSD").await?.ask;
let m = service.calculate_margin("EURUSD", TF::OrderTypeTfBuy, 1.0, price).await?.margin;
println!("margin for 1.0 lot: {m:.2}");

docs.title: 3) Profit of a 50-pip move
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::EnumOrderTypeTf as TF;

let open = 1.08500;
let p = service.calculate_profit("EURUSD", TF::OrderTypeTfBuy, 0.10, open, open + 0.0050).await?.profit;
println!("profit: {p:+.2}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Execution methods take raw requests. Build the OrderSendRequest/etc. yourself here, or step up to MT5Sugar for symbol/side/pip helpers.
  • Check returned_code == 10009.
  • Calculators use EnumOrderTypeTf (the …Tf enum), not EnumOrderType.

docs.title: MT5Service — 6. Streaming Methods
docs.text:
Real-time streams with friendlier arguments (Vec<String> symbols, plain timer/flag params). Same item payloads as the low level.

Layer: MID over MT5Account Streaming. Defined in src/mt5/service.rs.

docs.title: The 5 streams
docs.text:
Method Item Tier Delegates to stream_ticks(symbols) OnSymbolTickData 🔵 friendly args on_symbol_tick(..) stream_trade_updates() OnTradeData ⚪ pass-through on_trade(default) stream_position_profits(timer_period_ms, ignore_empty) OnPositionProfitData 🔵 friendly args on_position_profit(..) stream_opened_tickets(timer_period_ms) OnPositionsAndPendingOrdersTicketsData 🔵 friendly args on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets(..) stream_transactions() OnTradeTransactionData ⚪ pass-through on_trade_transaction(default)

Where the value is: you pass a Vec<String> / a timer in ms / a bool flag instead of constructing the On*Request. Each returns the same Result<impl Stream<Item = Result<…Data, MT5Error>>, MT5Error> as the low level — the outer Result is "subscription opened", then you iterate.

    -> Result<impl tokio_stream::Stream<Item = Result<pb::OnTradeData, MT5Error>>, MT5Error>

Item field tables are on the low-level pages: on_symbol_tick, on_trade, on_position_profit, on_positions_and_pending_orders_tickets, on_trade_transaction.

docs.title: 1) Live ticks
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;

let mut s = service.stream_ticks(vec!["EURUSD".into(), "GBPUSD".into()]).await?;
while let Some(item) = s.next().await {
    match item {
        Ok(d) => if let Some(t) = d.symbol_tick { println!("{} {:.5}/{:.5}", t.symbol, t.bid, t.ask); },
        Err(e) => { eprintln!("stream error: {e}"); break; }
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Live total floating P/L (every second, quiet when idle)
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;
use std::collections::HashMap;

let mut s = service.stream_position_profits(1000, true).await?;
let mut book: HashMap<i64, f64> = HashMap::new();
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    for p in d.new_positions.iter().chain(d.updated_positions.iter()) { book.insert(p.ticket, p.profit); }
    for p in &d.deleted_positions { book.remove(&p.ticket); }
    println!("floating {:+.2} ({} pos)", book.values().sum::<f64>(), book.len());
}

docs.title: 3) React to trade events
docs.text:
use tokio_stream::StreamExt;

let mut s = service.stream_trade_updates().await?;
while let Some(Ok(d)) = s.next().await {
    if let Some(a) = d.account_info { println!("event {} | equity {:.2}", d.r#type, a.equity); }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• use tokio_stream::StreamExt; to get .next().
  • Two Results: outer = opened, inner (per item) = frame-or-error.
  • Timer streams push on a clock (stream_position_profits, stream_opened_tickets); event streams push on change.
  • Dropping the stream unsubscribes.

docs.title: MT5Service — Mid-Level API Overview
docs.text: The friendly facade over MT5Account: the same operations, but you pass plain arguments (typed enums, &str symbols) and get back clean values (f64/i64/String/bool) instead of protobuf …Data wrappers and hand-built …Request structs.

docs.title: ⚠️ What this layer is (and isn't)
docs.text:
MT5Service is architectural middleware — it sits between MT5Account (raw gRPC/protobuf) and MT5Sugar (business logic).

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ MT5Sugar   — HIGH   order building, pip math,   │
│                      risk sizing, one-liners    │
└───────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                │ uses Service methods
                ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ MT5Service  — MID    ← you are here             │
│   friendly args (typed enums, &str, sides)      │
│   clean values (unwraps …Data → scalar)         │
└───────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                │ calls Account methods
                ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ MT5Account  — LOW    raw gRPC, …Data payloads   │
└───────────────┬─────────────────────────────────┘
                │ gRPC
                ▼              MT5 terminal gateway

Defined in src/mt5/service.rs. It wraps one MT5Account (field acc); borrow it any time with service.account() / service.account_mut().

docs.title: What the value-add actually is (Rust)
docs.text:
Two concrete conveniences, nothing magic:

  1. Friendly arguments — pass a typed enum (SymbolInfoDoubleProperty::SymbolBid) and a &str symbol; the Service builds the …Request and does the as i32 cast for you.
  2. Clean return values — the simple getters return the inner scalar (f64, i64, String, bool, i32) instead of the …Data struct you'd otherwise destructure.

What it does not do (be honest about it): it does not aggregate extra RPC calls into account_summary (that's a pass-through here), and it does not convert protobuf Timestamp into a date type — timestamps stay as prost_types::Timestamp. Richer behavior (order construction, pip/risk math) lives one layer up in MT5Sugar.

docs.title: Method value, at a glance
docs.text:
Tier Meaning Examples 🟢 Clean value Unwraps …Data → a scalar you can use directly account_double, symbols_total, symbol_double, positions_total, symbol_select 🔵 Friendly args Still returns a …Data, but you skip building the request & casting enums symbol_tick, symbol_params_many, opened_orders, order_history, calculate_margin, the streams ⚪ Pass-through Same shape as MT5Account, just a friendlier name/args account_summary, symbol_exist, opened_orders_tickets, place_order/modify_order/close_order/check_order

Rule of thumb: using Sugar? Everything here just works beneath it. Using Service directly? Prefer the 🟢/🔵 methods; for a ⚪ pass-through you can equally call MT5Account via service.account().

docs.title: Usage pattern
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api as pb;
use metarpc_mt5::{MT5Account, MT5Service};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // 1. low-level account
    let account = MT5Account::new(12_345_678, "password", None);

    // 2. wrap in the mid-level service
    let mut service = MT5Service::new(account);

    // 3. connect (delegates to the account)
    service.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;

    // 4. clean values — no …Data to destructure
    let balance = service.account_double(pb::AccountInfoDoublePropertyType::AccountBalance).await?;
    let digits  = service.symbol_integer("EURUSD", pb::SymbolInfoIntegerProperty::SymbolDigits).await?;
    let tick    = service.symbol_tick("EURUSD").await?;
    println!("balance {balance:.2}, digits {digits}, bid {:.5}", tick.bid);

    // 5. need the raw layer? borrow it
    let _acc = service.account();

    // 6. disconnect (the bool mirrors the Python facade; it is ignored here)
    service.disconnect(false).await?;
    Ok(())
}

docs.title: When to use Service vs Account
docs.text:
Use MT5Service when you want ergonomic calls (typed-enum args, scalar returns) or you're building on top via MT5Sugar.

Call MT5Account directly (via service.account()) when the Service method is a ⚪ pass-through and you'd rather not add a layer, or you need a field/variant the Service doesn't surface.

See also: MT5Account — Master Overview · MT5Sugar — Master Overview

docs.title: MT5Sugar — Master Overview
docs.text:
High-level, one-line convenience methods for MetaTrader 5 automation in Rust.

MT5Sugar wraps an MT5Service (composition, not inheritance — field svc) and adds ergonomic business logic:

  • Quick balances & a compact account snapshot
  • Prices by symbol (bid/ask/spread) with an optional default symbol
  • Order construction from symbol / side / volume (market, pending, pip-based SL/TP)
  • Position management (close, partial close, close-all, modify SL/TP)
  • Position queries (by ticket, by symbol, counts, floating profit)
  • History & statistics over predefined periods
  • Risk sizing and pre-trade validation

It is Layer 3 — the top of the stack. Defined in src/mt5/sugar.rs.

MT5Sugar (HIGH)  ← you are here      sugar.buy_market_with_pips(...)
   │ uses
MT5Service (MID)                     svc.place_order(req) / svc.symbol_tick(sym)
   │ uses
MT5Account (LOW)                     gRPC → MT5 terminal gateway

docs.title: Conventions used throughout
docs.text:
• Default symbol. Construct with MT5Sugar::new(svc).with_default_symbol("EURUSD"). Methods taking symbol: Option<&str> fall back to it when you pass None; without a default, None is an InvalidArgument error.
  • Pips. A "pip" is 10 × point (so on a 5-digit FX symbol, 1 pip = 0.0001). Pip→price conversion uses the symbol's SYMBOL_POINT.
  • Success code. Trade calls check TRADE_RETCODE_DONE (10009); a different code becomes an MT5Error::Api { code, message, mql_code }. The boolean-returning helpers map "done" → true.
  • Tickets. Order-entry methods return the order ticket (u64).
  • Async. Every method is async — .await it.

docs.title: Minimal usage
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::{MT5Account, MT5Service, MT5Sugar};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let account = MT5Account::new(12_345_678, "password", None);
    let mut sugar = MT5Sugar::new(MT5Service::new(account)).with_default_symbol("EURUSD");

    sugar.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;

    println!("balance {:.2}, bid {:.5}", sugar.balance().await?, sugar.bid(None).await?);

    // risk 1% over a 20-pip stop, then enter with a pip bracket
    let lots = sugar.calculate_position_size("EURUSD", 1.0, 20.0).await?;
    let ticket = sugar.buy_market_with_pips(None, lots, Some(20.0), Some(40.0), "demo", 1001).await?;
    println!("opened #{ticket}");

    sugar.disconnect(false).await?;
    Ok(())
}

See also: MT5Service — Overview · MT5Account — Master Overview · Strategies

API Information:

    &mut self,
    host: &str,

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description host &str Server address (e.g. "mt5.broker.com"). port u16 Port (often 443). timeout_seconds u32 Connection timeout. Output Type Description () — Unit on success; MT5Error otherwise.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Opens the terminal session to a specific address.
  • Why you need it: For brokers/setups where you connect by host rather than cluster name.
  • Alternative: connect_by_server_name is usually simpler.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.connect_by_host_port()
  → MT5Service.connect_by_host_port()
    → MT5Account.connect_by_host_port()  (ConnectRequest)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• You have an explicit server address (not just a cluster name).
  • Testing against a specific gateway endpoint.

docs.title: 1) Connect by address
docs.text:
let mut sugar = MT5Sugar::new(MT5Service::new(account));
sugar.connect_by_host_port("mt5.broker.com", 443, 30).await?;

docs.title: 2) Then trade
docs.text:
sugar.connect_by_host_port("mt5.broker.com", 443, 30).await?;
let bal = sugar.balance().await?;
println!("balance {bal:.2}");

docs.title: 3) Error handling
docs.text:
if let Err(e) = sugar.connect_by_host_port("bad.host", 443, 10).await {
    eprintln!("connect failed: {e}");
}

docs.title: Related Methods

• connect_by_server_name — by cluster name (recommended)
  • ping · disconnect

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Needs &mut.
  • Wrong host/port → connection error.
  • Prefer the cluster-name connect unless you specifically need an address.

docs.title: Connect By Server Name (connect_by_server_name)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Connect to the terminal gateway by broker cluster name — the recommended way.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.connect_by_server_name(server_name, timeout_seconds)
  • Returns: Result<(), MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar) — delegates straight to MT5Service → MT5Account

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn connect_by_server_name(
    &mut self,
    server_name: &str,
    timeout_seconds: u32,
) -> Result<(), MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description server_name &str Broker server/cluster name (e.g. "MetaQuotes-Demo"). timeout_seconds u32 How long to wait for the connection. Output Type Description () — Unit on success; MT5Error on failure.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Resolves the broker cluster by name and opens the terminal session.
  • Why you need it: It's the first call — every other method needs an open connection.
  • Recommended: Prefer this over host/port unless you have a specific address.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.connect_by_server_name()
  → MT5Service.connect_by_server_name()
    → MT5Account.connect_by_server_name()  (ConnectExRequest → terminal session id)

&mut self — connecting mutates the wrapped service/account (stores the session id).

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• At startup, before any balance/price/trade call.
  • When you know the broker cluster name (most common for demo/live logins).

docs.title: 1) Basic connect
docs.text:
let mut sugar = MT5Sugar::new(MT5Service::new(account));
sugar.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;
println!("connected");

docs.title: 2) With a default symbol set
docs.text:
let mut sugar = MT5Sugar::new(MT5Service::new(account)).with_default_symbol("EURUSD");
sugar.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 60).await?;
println!("bid {:.5}", sugar.bid(None).await?);  // uses the default symbol

docs.title: 3) Handle a connection error
docs.text:
if let Err(e) = sugar.connect_by_server_name("Wrong-Server", 15).await {
    eprintln!("connect failed: {e}");
}

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text:
• connect_by_host_port — connect by explicit address
  • ping — check the connection is alive
  • disconnect — close it

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Needs &mut. The sugar binding must be mut.
  • Wrong cluster name → connection error; names are broker-specific.
  • Too-short timeout on a cold terminal can fail; 30–60 s is safe.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text:
• connect_by_host_port · ping
  • Low-level: MT5Account — Constructor & connection

docs.title: Disconnect (disconnect)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Close the terminal connection.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.disconnect(delete)
  • Returns: Result<(), MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar) — delegates to MT5Service → MT5Account

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn disconnect(&mut self, delete: bool) -> Result<(), MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description delete bool Mirrors the Python facade's flag. Accepted for API parity; the low-level disconnect() takes no argument, so the channel is simply dropped. Output Type Description () — Unit on success.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Ends the session and releases the channel.
  • Why you need it: Clean shutdown at the end of a program/task.
  • Note: delete is kept only for signature parity with the Python Sugar; it does not change behavior here.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.disconnect(delete)
  → MT5Service.disconnect(delete)   // delete ignored
    → MT5Account.disconnect()       // drops the channel

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• On shutdown of a script or worker.
  • Before re-creating a connection from scratch.

docs.title: 1) Clean shutdown
docs.text: sugar.disconnect(false).await?;

docs.title: 2) In a run function
docs.text:
async fn run(sugar: &mut MT5Sugar) -> Result<(), MT5Error> {
    // ... do work ...
    sugar.disconnect(false).await
}

docs.title: 3) Ignore errors on teardown
docs.text: let _ = sugar.disconnect(true).await;  // best-effort cleanup

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text:
• connect_by_server_name · connect_by_host_port
  • ping

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Needs &mut.
  • delete is a no-op here — don't rely on it to delete anything server-side.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • ping · connect_by_server_name

docs.title: Ping (ping)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Liveness check — true if the account responds.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.ping()
  • Returns: bool
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn ping(&self) -> bool

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description bool — true if an account snapshot succeeds, else false.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Tries account_summary(); success → true.
  • Why you need it: Confirm the connection is alive before trading or in a health loop.
  • Note: Returns a plain bool (no Result) — a failed call is reported as false, not an error.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.ping()
  → MT5Service.account_summary().is_ok()
    → MT5Account.account_summary()  (gRPC)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Health checks / watchdog loops.
  • A quick gate before a batch of operations.

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text: if sugar.ping().await { println!("alive"); } else { println!("not connected"); }

docs.title: 2) Guard before work
docs.text:
if !sugar.ping().await {
    sugar.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;
}

docs.title: 3) Periodic check
docs.text:
use std::time::Duration;
loop {
    println!("alive: {}", sugar.ping().await);
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(10)).await;
}

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text:
• connect_by_server_name · disconnect
  • get_account_info

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Swallows the error. ping returns false on any failure — use account_summary() directly if you need the error detail.
  • One round-trip. It's cheap but not free; don't spin it in a tight loop.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • connect_by_server_name · disconnect

docs.title: Calculate Position Size (calculate_position_size)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Lot size that risks risk_percent% of balance over an sl_pips stop — rounded to the volume step and clamped to min/max.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.calculate_position_size(symbol, risk_percent, sl_pips)
  • Returns: Result<f64, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn calculate_position_size(
    &self,
    symbol: &str,
    risk_percent: f64,
    sl_pips: f64,
) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol &str Symbol name. risk_percent f64 Percent of balance to risk (e.g. 1.0 = 1%). sl_pips f64 Stop distance in pips. Output Type Description f64 — Lot size (step-rounded, clamped to [volume_min, volume_max]).

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: The core risk-sizing helper.
  • Formula: risk_amount = balance × risk%/100; pip_value = point × 10 × contract_size; lots = round(risk_amount / (sl_pips × pip_value) / step) × step, clamped to min/max.
  • Guards: if sl_pips ≤ 0 or pip_value ≤ 0, returns volume_min.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.calculate_position_size(symbol, risk_percent, sl_pips)
  → balance()                     // MT5Service.account_double(AccountBalance)
  → get_symbol_info(symbol)       // point, contract_size, volume_min/step/max
  → compute & round lots

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Every risk-based entry — pair with the pip-bracket trading methods.

docs.title: 1) 1% over a 20-pip stop
docs.text:
let lots = sugar.calculate_position_size("EURUSD", 1.0, 20.0).await?;
println!("lots {lots:.2}");

docs.title: 2) Size then enter
docs.text:
let lots = sugar.calculate_position_size("EURUSD", 1.0, 20.0).await?;
sugar.buy_market_with_pips(Some("EURUSD"), lots, Some(20.0), Some(40.0), "sized", 3001).await?;

docs.title: 3) Conservative vs aggressive
docs.text:
let cons = sugar.calculate_position_size("EURUSD", 0.5, 30.0).await?;
let aggr = sugar.calculate_position_size("EURUSD", 2.0, 15.0).await?;
println!("cons {cons:.2}, aggr {aggr:.2}");

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • calculate_required_margin · can_open_position · buy_market_with_pips

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Risk is on balance, not equity.
  • Approximate pip value (point × 10 × contract_size) — for cross-currency instruments the true per-pip value may differ; validate for exotics.
  • Degenerate inputs (sl_pips ≤ 0) fall back to volume_min.
  • Still check margin with calculate_required_margin before sending.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • can_open_position · calculate_sltp

docs.title: Calculate Required Margin (calculate_required_margin)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Margin needed to open volume lots of a symbol (defaults to BUY), at the current price.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.calculate_required_margin(symbol, volume, order_type)
  • Returns: Result<f64, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn calculate_required_margin(
    &self,
    symbol: &str,
    volume: f64,
    order_type: Option<pb::EnumOrderTypeTf>,
) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol &str Symbol name. volume f64 Lots. order_type Option<EnumOrderTypeTf> Direction; None → OrderTypeTfBuy. Output Type Description f64 — Required margin in the deposit currency.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Fetches the current price (ask for buy, bid for sell) and asks the server to compute margin.
  • Why you need it: Confirm a size fits your free_margin before trading.
  • Default side: BUY when order_type is None.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.calculate_required_margin(symbol, volume, order_type)
  → price = symbol_tick(symbol).ask|bid
  → MT5Service.calculate_margin(symbol, order_type, volume, price).margin
    → MT5Account.order_calc_margin(...)  (gRPC)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Pre-trade fit check; sizing to margin.

docs.title: 1) Margin for 1 lot
docs.text:
let m = sugar.calculate_required_margin("EURUSD", 1.0, None).await?;
println!("needs {m:.2}");

docs.title: 2) Fits free margin?
docs.text:
let need = sugar.calculate_required_margin("EURUSD", 0.50, None).await?;
if sugar.free_margin().await? < need { println!("too big"); }

docs.title: 3) Sell-side margin
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::proto::mt5_term_api::EnumOrderTypeTf as TF;
let m = sugar.calculate_required_margin("EURUSD", 0.10, Some(TF::OrderTypeTfSell)).await?;

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • free_margin · calculate_position_size · can_open_position

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Clean-account estimate — ignores existing positions (hedging may make the real figure lower).
  • Keep a buffer vs free margin.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • calculate_position_size · can_open_position

docs.title: Calculate SL/TP (calculate_sltp)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Convert pip SL/TP distances into absolute prices for a given side.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.calculate_sltp(symbol, is_buy, sl_pips, tp_pips)
  • Returns: Result<(Option<f64>, Option<f64>), MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn calculate_sltp(
    &self,
    symbol: &str,
    is_buy: bool,
    sl_pips: Option<f64>,
    tp_pips: Option<f64>,
) -> Result<(Option<f64>, Option<f64>), MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol &str Symbol name. is_buy bool true for long (SL below / TP above), false for short. sl_pips Option<f64> SL distance in pips, or None. tp_pips Option<f64> TP distance in pips, or None. Output Type Description (Option<f64>, Option<f64>) — (sl_price, tp_price) — each None if its pips input was None.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Pip → absolute-price helper that respects side (entry = ask for buy, bid for sell).
  • Why you need it: Feed absolute SL/TP into modify_position_sltp or build order requests.
  • Pip size: point × 10.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.calculate_sltp(symbol, is_buy, sl_pips, tp_pips)
  → tick = symbol_tick(symbol); point = symbol_double(symbol, SymbolPoint)
  → entry = if is_buy { ask } else { bid }
  → buy:  sl = entry - p*point*10,  tp = entry + p*point*10
    sell: sl = entry + p*point*10,  tp = entry - p*point*10

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Before modifying a position's SL/TP from pip distances.
  • Computing bracket levels for display or manual order building.

docs.title: 1) Long bracket prices
docs.text:
let (sl, tp) = sugar.calculate_sltp("EURUSD", true, Some(20.0), Some(40.0)).await?;
println!("SL {sl:?}  TP {tp:?}");

docs.title: 2) Apply to a position
docs.text:
let (sl, tp) = sugar.calculate_sltp("EURUSD", true, Some(20.0), Some(40.0)).await?;
sugar.modify_position_sltp(123456, sl, tp).await?;

docs.title: 3) Short, SL only
docs.text: let (sl, _tp) = sugar.calculate_sltp("EURUSD", false, Some(25.0), None).await?;

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • modify_position_sltp · buy_market_with_pips

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Uses the current tick as entry — for a position already open, the real entry differs; use the entry price when that matters.
  • None in → None out for that side.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • calculate_position_size · modify_position_sltp

docs.title: Can Open Position (can_open_position)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Validate whether a BUY of volume lots could be opened; returns (can_open, reason).

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.can_open_position(symbol, volume)
  • Returns: Result<(bool, String), MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn can_open_position(&self, symbol: &str, volume: f64) -> Result<(bool, String), MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol &str Symbol name. volume f64 Lots to validate. Output Type Description (bool, String) — (true, "OK") if it would be accepted, else (false, reason).

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Builds a market-BUY trade request (IOC fill, GTC time) and runs check_order.
  • Why you need it: Catch "no money" / "invalid volume" / "market closed" before actually sending.
  • Success condition: the check result's returned_code == 0.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.can_open_position(symbol, volume)
  → tick = symbol_tick(symbol)
  → build MrpcMqlTradeRequest { action=Deal, symbol, volume, price=ask,
       order_type=Buy(Tf), type_filling=IOC, type_time=GTC }
  → MT5Service.check_order(...).mql_trade_check_result
    → MT5Account.order_check(...)  (gRPC)
  → code==0 → (true, "OK") else (false, "check failed: code=.. ..")

Note the check uses retcode 0 as the "would succeed" signal for the check (distinct from the send success code 10009).

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Pre-trade gate in front of buy_market/buy_market_with_pips.

docs.title: 1) Gate an entry
docs.text:
let (ok, why) = sugar.can_open_position("EURUSD", 0.50).await?;
if ok {
    sugar.buy_market(Some("EURUSD"), 0.50, "validated", 3002).await?;
} else {
    println!("cannot open: {why}");
}

docs.title: 2) Find the largest size that passes
docs.text:
let mut v = 1.0;
while v >= 0.01 {
    if sugar.can_open_position("EURUSD", v).await?.0 { break; }
    v -= 0.1;
}
println!("max passing size ≈ {v:.2}");

docs.title: 3) Log the reason
docs.text:
let (_ok, why) = sugar.can_open_position("EURUSD", 100.0).await?;
println!("{why}");

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • calculate_required_margin · calculate_position_size · low-level order_check

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• BUY-only check. It validates a buy; a sell's margin can differ slightly.
  • Check code is 0, not 10009 — that's the order-check convention.
  • Validation ≠ execution — market can move between check and send.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • calculate_position_size · calculate_required_margin

docs.title: Get Max Lot Size (get_max_lot_size)
docs.text:
Sugar method: The maximum lot size allowed for a symbol.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.get_max_lot_size(symbol)
  • Returns: Result<f64, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn get_max_lot_size(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol &str Symbol name. Output Type Description f64 — Symbol's volume_max.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood

MT5Sugar.get_max_lot_size(symbol)

docs.title: 1) Read it

let want = 25.0;

docs.title: Balance (balance)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Current account balance (realized P/L only) in one line.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.balance()
  • Returns: Result<f64, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn balance(&self) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description f64 — Balance in the deposit currency.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Money excluding floating P/L of open positions.
  • Why you need it: Risk sizing and "enough funds?" checks.
  • Sanity check: balance ≤ equity when positions are in profit, ≥ when in loss.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.balance()
  → MT5Service.account_double(AccountBalance)
    → MT5Account.account_info_double(...).requested_value

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Before trading — confirm funds.
  • Position sizing — base risk on balance (see calculate_position_size).

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text:
let bal = sugar.balance().await?;
println!("balance {bal:.2}");

docs.title: 2) Risk amount
docs.text:
let risk = sugar.balance().await? * 0.02;  // 2%
println!("risking {risk:.2}");

docs.title: 3) Gate trading
docs.text: if sugar.balance().await? < 1000.0 { println!("insufficient"); return Ok(()); }

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • equity · free_margin · get_account_info

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Balance ≠ equity. Balance ignores open positions; use equity for live account value.
  • Fetching several properties? Prefer get_account_info (one call).

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • equity · get_account_info

docs.title: Equity (equity)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Current equity = balance + floating P/L.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.equity()
  • Returns: Result<f64, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn equity(&self) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description f64 — Equity in the deposit currency.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: The live account value — balance adjusted for open positions' floating P/L.
  • Why you need it: The number that matters for drawdown and margin level.
  • Sanity check: equity − balance equals current floating P/L.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.equity()
  → MT5Service.account_double(AccountEquity)
    → MT5Account.account_info_double(...).requested_value

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Drawdown / performance monitoring.
  • Margin-level math (equity / margin × 100).

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text: println!("equity {:.2}", sugar.equity().await?);

docs.title: 2) Floating P/L
docs.text:
let floating = sugar.equity().await? - sugar.balance().await?;
println!("floating P/L {floating:+.2}");

docs.title: 3) Drawdown alert
docs.text:
let (bal, eq) = (sugar.balance().await?, sugar.equity().await?);
if bal > 0.0 && (bal - eq) / bal > 0.1 { println!("[ALERT] >10% drawdown"); }

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • balance · floating_profit · margin_level

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Snapshot. Equity moves with price — re-read before decisions.
  • For floating P/L specifically, floating_profit is more direct.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • balance · floating_profit · get_account_info

docs.title: Floating Profit (floating_profit)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Current floating P/L of all open positions.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.floating_profit()
  • Returns: Result<f64, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn floating_profit(&self) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description f64 — Floating profit (negative = loss) in the deposit currency.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: The account-level unrealized P/L (ACCOUNT_PROFIT).
  • Why you need it: One number for "how are my open trades doing?".
  • Relation: equals equity − balance.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.floating_profit()
  → MT5Service.account_double(AccountProfit)
    → MT5Account.account_info_double(...).requested_value

Account-level figure. For a per-symbol or per-position breakdown, use get_total_profit / get_profit_by_symbol.

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Live P/L display.
  • Trailing/exit logic keyed on account profit.

docs.title: 1) Basic

docs.title: 2) Take-profit-all trigger
docs.text:
if sugar.floating_profit().await? >= 100.0 {
    sugar.close_all_positions(None).await?;
}

docs.title: 3) Same as equity − balance
docs.text:
let a = sugar.floating_profit().await?;
let b = sugar.equity().await? - sugar.balance().await?;
println!("{a:+.2} ≈ {b:+.2}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text: • Account-wide. This sums everything; for one symbol use the position-info helpers.

docs.title: Free Margin (free_margin)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Margin available for opening new positions.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.free_margin()
  • Returns: Result<f64, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn free_margin(&self) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description f64 — Free margin in the deposit currency (equity − margin).

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: What's left to open new trades.
  • Why you need it: Pre-trade gate — compare with calculate_required_margin.
  • Flat account: equals equity.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.free_margin()
  → MT5Service.account_double(AccountMarginFree)
    → MT5Account.account_info_double(...).requested_value

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Before opening a position — does it fit?
  • Sizing with a safety buffer.

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text: println!("free margin {:.2}", sugar.free_margin().await?);

docs.title: 2) Fit check
docs.text:
let need = sugar.calculate_required_margin("EURUSD", 1.0, None).await?;
if sugar.free_margin().await? < need { println!("not enough free margin"); }

docs.title: 3) Keep a buffer
docs.text:
let usable = sugar.free_margin().await? * 0.9;  // leave 10%
println!("usable {usable:.2}");

docs.text: • margin · margin_level · calculate_required_margin

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text: • Don't size to 100%. Leave headroom for spread/slippage and adverse moves.

docs.title: Get Account Info (get_account_info)

Sugar method: A compact account snapshot (AccountInfo) in one call.

API Information:

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn get_account_info(&self) -> Result<AccountInfo, MT5Error>

docs.title: AccountInfo
docs.text:
pub struct AccountInfo {
    pub login: i64,
    pub name: String,
    pub company: String,
    pub currency: String,
    pub leverage: i64,
    pub balance: f64,
    pub equity: f64,
}

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description AccountInfo struct Login, name, company, currency, leverage, balance, equity.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: The handful of fields you usually want, built from one account_summary().
  • Why you need it: One round-trip instead of several balance()/equity()/… calls.
  • Note: It does not include margin fields — read those with margin/free_margin/margin_level.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.get_account_info()
  → MT5Service.account_summary()  (maps AccountSummaryData → AccountInfo)
    → MT5Account.account_summary()  (gRPC)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Account banner / header.
  • Any time you need more than one of login/name/company/currency/leverage/balance/equity.

docs.title: 1) Banner
docs.text:
let a = sugar.get_account_info().await?;
println!("#{} {} — {:.2} {} (eq {:.2})  1:{}", a.login, a.company, a.balance, a.currency, a.equity, a.leverage);

docs.title: 2) Floating P/L from the snapshot
docs.text:
let a = sugar.get_account_info().await?;
println!("floating {:+.2}", a.equity - a.balance);

docs.title: 3) Owner & currency
docs.text:
let a = sugar.get_account_info().await?;
println!("{} trades in {}", a.name, a.currency);

docs.title: Margin (margin)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Margin currently used by open positions.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.margin()

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn margin(&self) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description f64 — Used margin in the deposit currency.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Funds reserved to hold current open positions.
  • Why you need it: Combine with equity for margin level; see headroom for new trades.
  • Flat account: 0.0.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.margin()
  → MT5Service.account_double(AccountMargin)
    → MT5Account.account_info_double(...).requested_value

docs.text:
• Risk/exposure dashboards.
  • Deciding whether another position fits.

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text: println!("used margin {:.2}", sugar.margin().await?);

docs.title: 2) Margin level by hand
docs.text:
let (eq, m) = (sugar.equity().await?, sugar.margin().await?);
if m > 0.0 { println!("margin level {:.1}%", eq / m * 100.0); }

docs.title: 3) Headroom
docs.text: println!("free vs used: {:.2} / {:.2}", sugar.free_margin().await?, sugar.margin().await?);

docs.title: Margin Level (margin_level)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Margin level as a percentage (equity / margin × 100).

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.margin_level()
  • Returns: Result<f64, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn margin_level(&self) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description f64 — Margin level in percent.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Health gauge — the broker issues margin calls / stop-outs below thresholds.
  • Why you need it: De-risk before you hit stop-out.
  • Flat account: typically 0.0 (no margin used → no division).

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.margin_level()
  → MT5Service.account_double(AccountMarginLevel)
    → MT5Account.account_info_double(...).requested_value

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Risk monitoring / alerts.
  • Deciding to reduce exposure.

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text: println!("margin level {:.1}%", sugar.margin_level().await?);

docs.title: 2) Alert
docs.text:
let lvl = sugar.margin_level().await?;
if lvl != 0.0 && lvl < 200.0 { println!("[ALERT] margin level {lvl:.0}% — de-risk"); }

docs.title: 3) Guard a new trade
docs.text: if sugar.margin_level().await? < 300.0 { println!("skip: margin level too low"); }

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • margin · free_margin · equity

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• It's a percent, not currency.
  • Zero when flat — guard the 0.0 case before alerting.

docs.title: Spread (spread)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Current spread (ask − bid) in price units.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.spread(symbol)

  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn spread(&self, symbol: Option<&str>) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol Option<&str> Symbol, or None for the default symbol. Output Type Description f64 — ask − bid, in price units (not points).

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: The cost of crossing the book right now, in price.
  • Why you need it: Avoid entering when the spread is abnormally wide.
  • Points: divide by the symbol's point for spread in points (see get_symbol_info).

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.spread(symbol)

docs.title: When to Use

• Pre-trade filter — skip wide spreads.
  • Execution-cost estimates.

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text: println!("spread {:.5}", sugar.spread(None).await?);

docs.title: 2) In points
docs.text:
let si = sugar.get_symbol_info("EURUSD").await?;
let pts = sugar.spread(Some("EURUSD")).await? / si.point;
println!("spread {pts:.1} points");

docs.title: 3) Spread gate
docs.text: if sugar.spread(Some("EURUSD")).await? > 0.0003 { println!("spread too wide — skip"); }

docs.title: Buy Limit (buy_limit)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Place a BUY LIMIT pending order at price (below market).

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.buy_limit(symbol, volume, price, comment, magic)
  • Returns: Result<u64, MT5Error> (order ticket)
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn buy_limit(
    &self,
    symbol: Option<&str>,
    volume: f64,
    price: f64,
    comment: &str,
    magic: u64,
) -> Result<u64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol Option<&str> Symbol, or None for default. volume f64 Lots. price f64 Trigger price — below current market. comment &str Comment. magic u64 Magic number. Output Type Description u64 — Pending order ticket.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: "Buy if price drops to price."
  • Why you need it: Enter long on a pullback without watching the screen.
  • Rule: price must be below the current ask (else the server rejects it).

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.buy_limit()
  → send_order(BuyLimit, price=price, sl=None, tp=None)
    → MT5Service.place_order(...) → MT5Account.order_send(...)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Pullback entries, grid levels, scaling in below market.

docs.title: 1) 10 pips below market
docs.text:
let bid = sugar.bid(Some("EURUSD")).await?;
let t = sugar.buy_limit(Some("EURUSD"), 0.10, bid - 0.0010, "dip", 1003).await?;
println!("pending #{t}");

docs.title: 2) Default symbol
docs.text:
let price = sugar.bid(None).await? - 0.0015;
let t = sugar.buy_limit(None, 0.05, price, "", 0).await?;

docs.title: 3) Cancel later
docs.text:
let t = sugar.buy_limit(Some("EURUSD"), 0.1, 1.0800, "x", 1).await?;
sugar.close_position(t).await?;  // deletes the resting pending

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • sell_limit · buy_stop · buy_market

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Price above market for a buy limit → rejection.
  • Pending ≠ position until filled; check with has_open_position.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • sell_limit · buy_stop

docs.title: Buy Market (buy_market)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Open a BUY at market in one line; returns the order ticket.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.buy_market(symbol, volume, comment, magic)
  • Returns: Result<u64, MT5Error> (order ticket)
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn buy_market(
    &self,
    symbol: Option<&str>,
    volume: f64,
    comment: &str,
    magic: u64,
) -> Result<u64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol Option<&str> Symbol, or None for the default symbol. volume f64 Lots. comment &str Order comment ("" for none). magic u64 EA magic number (0 for none). Output Type Description u64 — The opened order ticket.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Market buy at the current ask; no SL/TP.
  • Why you need it: The simplest way to go long.
  • Price: fetched automatically (the ask); slippage defaults to 10 points.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.buy_market()
  → send_order(Buy, price=ask, sl=None, tp=None)
    → MT5Service.place_order(OrderSendRequest)
      → MT5Account.order_send(...)  (gRPC)
  → checks returned_code == 10009, returns res.order

A non-10009 retcode becomes MT5Error::Api { code, message, mql_code }.

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Immediate long entry at market.
  • Building blocks for strategies (add SL/TP via buy_market_with_pips).

docs.title: 1) Default symbol
docs.text:
let ticket = sugar.buy_market(None, 0.10, "entry", 1001).await?;
println!("opened #{ticket}");

docs.title: 2) Explicit symbol, no magic
docs.text: let t = sugar.buy_market(Some("GBPUSD"), 0.05, "", 0).await?;

docs.title: 3) Handle rejection
docs.text:
match sugar.buy_market(None, 0.10, "x", 1).await {
    Ok(t) => println!("ok #{t}"),
    Err(e) => eprintln!("rejected: {e}"),
}

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • sell_market · buy_limit · buy_market_with_pips

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• No SL/TP. Use the SL/TP variants for protection.
  • None without a default → InvalidArgument.
  • Volume rules. Must satisfy the symbol's min/step/max, or the server rejects it.

docs.title: 📚 See Also

docs.title: Sell Stop (sell_stop)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Place a SELL STOP pending order at price (below market).

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.sell_stop(symbol, volume, price, comment, magic)
  • Returns: Result<u64, MT5Error> (order ticket)
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn sell_stop(
    &self,
    symbol: Option<&str>,
    volume: f64,
    price: f64,
    comment: &str,
    magic: u64,
) -> Result<u64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol Option<&str> Symbol, or None for default. volume f64 Lots. price f64 Trigger price — below current market. comment &str Comment. magic u64 Magic number. Output Type Description u64 — Pending order ticket.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: "Sell if price breaks down to price."
  • Why you need it: Downside breakout entries.
  • Rule: price must be below the current bid.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.sell_stop()
  → send_order(SellStop, price=price) → MT5Service.place_order(...) → MT5Account.order_send(...)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Downside breakout entries; stop-entry strategies.

docs.title: 1) 20 pips below market
docs.text:
let bid = sugar.bid(Some("EURUSD")).await?;
let t = sugar.sell_stop(Some("EURUSD"), 0.10, bid - 0.0020, "breakdown", 1006).await?;

docs.title: 2) Default symbol
docs.text:
let price = sugar.bid(None).await? - 0.0020;
let t = sugar.sell_stop(None, 0.05, price, "", 0).await?;

docs.title: 3) Cancel
docs.text: sugar.close_position(t).await?;

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn buy_market_with_pips(
    &self,

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials

  • Why you need it: Cleanest call for "buy with a 20-pip stop and 40-pip target".

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood

docs.title: 1) 20/40 bracket

let lots = sugar.calculate_position_size("EURUSD", 1.0, 20.0).await?;

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls

docs.title: Buy Market with SL/TP (buy_market_with_sltp)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Market BUY with stop-loss / take-profit given as absolute prices and/or pips.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.buy_market_with_sltp(symbol, volume, sl, tp, sl_pips, tp_pips, comment, magic)
  • Returns: Result<u64, MT5Error> (order ticket)
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn buy_market_with_sltp(
    &self,
    symbol: Option<&str>,
    volume: f64,
    sl: Option<f64>,        // absolute price
    tp: Option<f64>,        // absolute price
    sl_pips: Option<f64>,   // distance in pips
    tp_pips: Option<f64>,   // distance in pips
    comment: &str,
    magic: u64,
) -> Result<u64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol Option<&str> Symbol, or None for default. volume f64 Lots. sl / tp Option<f64> Absolute SL / TP price. sl_pips / tp_pips Option<f64> SL / TP distance in pips from entry (1 pip = 10 × point). comment &str Comment. magic u64 Magic number. Output Type Description u64 — Order ticket.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Market buy at the ask, with protection in whichever form you prefer.
  • Why you need it: Enter and protect in a single call.
  • Pips win: if sl_pips/tp_pips are provided, they're converted from the entry and override the absolute sl/tp for that side.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.buy_market_with_sltp()
  → market_with_sltp(Buy):
      entry = ask
      if sl_pips: sl = entry - sl_pips*point*10
      if tp_pips: tp = entry + tp_pips*point*10
  → send_order(Buy, entry, sl, tp) → MT5Service.place_order(...) → MT5Account.order_send(...)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Protected long entries where you think in pips or in exact prices.

docs.title: 1) Pips SL/TP
docs.text: let t = sugar.buy_market_with_sltp(Some("EURUSD"), 0.10, None, None, Some(20.0), Some(40.0), "bracket", 2001).await?;

docs.title: 2) Absolute SL/TP
docs.text: let t = sugar.buy_market_with_sltp(Some("EURUSD"), 0.10, Some(1.08300), Some(1.09000), None, None, "", 0).await?;

docs.title: 3) SL only (let profit run)
docs.text: let t = sugar.buy_market_with_sltp(None, 0.05, None, None, Some(25.0), None, "", 0).await?;

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • sell_market_with_sltp · buy_market_with_pips · calculate_sltp

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Pips override absolute on a given side when both are passed.
  • Too-tight stops (inside the symbol's stops level) → rejection.
  • None without a default → InvalidArgument.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • buy_market_with_pips · sell_market_with_sltp

docs.text:

  • Direction handled: for a short, SL sits above and TP below entry — the method applies the signs.

MT5Sugar.sell_market_with_pips()

    → market_with_sltp(Sell) → send_order(...) → MT5Service.place_order(...)

docs.title: When to Use

docs.title: 1) 20/40 bracket
docs.text: let t = sugar.sell_market_with_pips(Some("EURUSD"), 0.10, Some(20.0), Some(40.0), "short", 2004).await?;

docs.title: 2) Risk-sized

let lots = sugar.calculate_position_size("EURUSD", 1.0, 20.0).await?;
let t = sugar.sell_market_with_pips(Some("EURUSD"), lots, Some(20.0), Some(40.0), "sized", 2004).await?;

docs.title: Sell Market with SL/TP (sell_market_with_sltp)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Market SELL with stop-loss / take-profit given as absolute prices and/or pips.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.sell_market_with_sltp(symbol, volume, sl, tp, sl_pips, tp_pips, comment, magic)
  • Returns: Result<u64, MT5Error> (order ticket)
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn sell_market_with_sltp(
    &self,
    symbol: Option<&str>,
    volume: f64,
    sl: Option<f64>,
    tp: Option<f64>,
    sl_pips: Option<f64>,
    tp_pips: Option<f64>,

) -> Result<u64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol Option<&str> Symbol, or None for default. volume f64 Lots. sl / tp Option<f64> Absolute SL / TP price. sl_pips / tp_pips Option<f64> SL / TP distance in pips from entry. comment &str Comment. magic u64 Magic number. Output Type Description u64 — Order ticket.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Market sell at the bid, with protection.
  • Direction: for a short, SL is above entry and TP is below — the method handles the sign for pips automatically.
  • Pips override absolute on the same side.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.sell_market_with_sltp()

docs.title: 1) Pips SL/TP

docs.title: Close All Positions (close_all_positions)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Close every open position (optionally only on one symbol); returns how many closed.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.close_all_positions(symbol)
  • Returns: Result<usize, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn close_all_positions(&self, symbol: Option<&str>) -> Result<usize, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol Option<&str> Limit to this symbol, or None for all positions. Output Type Description usize — Number of positions successfully closed.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Iterates open positions and closes each (filtered by symbol if given).
  • Why you need it: Panic button / end-of-session flatten.
  • Counting: only positions the server confirmed closed are counted.

Note: here symbol is Option<&str> as a direct filter — it is not the default-symbol fallback. None means "all symbols".

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.close_all_positions(symbol)
  → get_open_positions()                       // MT5Service.opened_orders(...).position_infos
  → for each (optionally matching symbol): close_position(ticket)
  → returns count of successful closes

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• Flatten everything at session end or on a risk trigger.
  • Flatten one symbol before reversing.

docs.title: 1) Close everything
docs.text:
let n = sugar.close_all_positions(None).await?;
println!("closed {n} positions");

docs.title: 2) Close only EURUSD
docs.text: let n = sugar.close_all_positions(Some("EURUSD")).await?;

docs.title: 3) Risk trigger
docs.text:
if sugar.floating_profit().await? <= -200.0 {
    sugar.close_all_positions(None).await?;   // cut the day
}

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • close_position · get_open_positions · count_open_positions

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• None = ALL. Unlike price methods, None is not the default symbol here — it means every position.
  • Partial failures are skipped (not counted), not surfaced as errors; compare the returned count with count_open_positions if it matters.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • close_position · get_open_positions

docs.title: Close Position (close_position)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Fully close a position by ticket; true if the server reported success.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.close_position(ticket)
  • Returns: Result<bool, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn close_position(&self, ticket: u64) -> Result<bool, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description ticket u64 Position (or pending) ticket. Output Type Description bool — true if returned_code == 10009.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Sends a close with volume: 0.0 (full close) and slippage: 0.
  • Why you need it: One-line exit by ticket.
  • Pendings: passing a pending order's ticket deletes the resting order.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.close_position(ticket)
  → MT5Service.close_order(OrderCloseRequest { ticket, volume: 0.0, slippage: 0 })
    → MT5Account.order_close(...)  (gRPC)
  → returns res.returned_code == 10009

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Exit a known ticket (from get_open_positions).

docs.title: 1) Close by ticket
docs.text:
let ok = sugar.close_position(123456).await?;
println!("closed: {ok}");

docs.title: 2) Close the first open position
docs.text:
if let Some(p) = sugar.get_open_positions().await?.first() {
    sugar.close_position(p.ticket).await?;
}

docs.title: 3) Close on profit target
docs.text:
if sugar.get_total_profit().await? >= 50.0 {
    for p in sugar.get_open_positions().await? { sugar.close_position(p.ticket).await?; }
}

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • close_position_partial · close_all_positions · get_open_positions

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• false is not an error. It means the server declined (bad ticket, already closed) — check it.
  • Slippage 0 can requote in fast markets; use close_position_partial (slippage 10) or the raw layer if needed.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • close_all_positions · close_position_partial

docs.title: Close Position Partial (close_position_partial)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Close part of a position by volume; true on success.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.close_position_partial(ticket, volume)
  • Returns: Result<bool, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn close_position_partial(&self, ticket: u64, volume: f64) -> Result<bool, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description ticket u64 Position ticket. volume f64 Lots to close (less than the position's size). Output Type Description bool — true if returned_code == 10009.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Scale out — close volume lots, leave the rest open.
  • Why you need it: Lock in partial profit, reduce risk while staying in.
  • Slippage: defaults to 10 points.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.close_position_partial(ticket, volume)
  → MT5Service.close_order(OrderCloseRequest { ticket, volume, slippage: 10 })
    → MT5Account.order_close(...)  (gRPC)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Scaling out at a first target; trimming exposure.

docs.title: 1) Close half of 0.10
docs.text: let ok = sugar.close_position_partial(123456, 0.05).await?;

docs.title: 2) Scale out, keep a runner
docs.text:
if let Some(p) = sugar.get_position_by_ticket(123456).await? {
    sugar.close_position_partial(p.ticket, p.volume / 2.0).await?;
}

docs.title: 3) Then move SL to breakeven on the rest
docs.text:
sugar.close_position_partial(123456, 0.05).await?;
sugar.modify_position_sl(123456, /* entry */ 1.08500).await?;

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • close_position · modify_position_sl · get_position_by_ticket

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Volume > position size → rejection.
  • Remainder stays open — the ticket persists after a partial close.
  • Respect volume step for the closed amount.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • close_position · close_all_positions

docs.title: Modify Position SL (modify_position_sl)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Move only the stop-loss of a position (take-profit preserved).

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.modify_position_sl(ticket, sl)
  • Returns: Result<bool, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar) — convenience over modify_position_sltp

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn modify_position_sl(&self, ticket: u64, sl: f64) -> Result<bool, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description ticket u64 Position ticket. sl f64 New stop-loss (absolute price). Output Type Description bool — true if returned_code == 10009.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: modify_position_sltp(ticket, Some(sl), None) — SL changes, TP kept.
  • Why you need it: Trailing stops and breakeven moves.
  • Absolute price.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.modify_position_sl(ticket, sl)
  → modify_position_sltp(ticket, Some(sl), None)
    → MT5Service.modify_order(...) → MT5Account.order_modify(...)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Move SL to breakeven, trail a stop manually.

docs.title: 1) Breakeven
docs.text:
let entry = 1.08500;
sugar.modify_position_sl(123456, entry).await?;

docs.title: 2) Trail behind price
docs.text:
let bid = sugar.bid(Some("EURUSD")).await?;
sugar.modify_position_sl(123456, bid - 0.0010).await?;  // 10 pips behind

docs.title: 3) Check the result
docs.text: if !sugar.modify_position_sl(123456, 1.08400).await? { println!("SL move rejected"); }

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • modify_position_tp · modify_position_sltp

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Too-tight SL (inside stops level) → rejection.
  • Unknown ticket → InvalidArgument.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • modify_position_tp · modify_position_sltp

docs.title: Modify Position SL/TP (modify_position_sltp)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Set stop-loss and/or take-profit on a position; the unspecified side is preserved.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.modify_position_sltp(ticket, sl, tp)
  • Returns: Result<bool, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn modify_position_sltp(
    &self,
    ticket: u64,
    sl: Option<f64>,
    tp: Option<f64>,
) -> Result<bool, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description ticket u64 Position ticket. sl Option<f64> New SL (absolute price), or None to keep the current SL. tp Option<f64> New TP (absolute price), or None to keep the current TP. Output Type Description bool — true if returned_code == 10009.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Reads the position, then re-sends SL/TP, defaulting each unspecified side to the position's current value.
  • Why you need it: Safe SL/TP edit without accidentally clearing the other side.
  • Prices are absolute — convert pips first with calculate_sltp.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.modify_position_sltp(ticket, sl, tp)
  → get_position_by_ticket(ticket)                       // to read existing sl/tp
  → MT5Service.modify_order(OrderModifyRequest {
        ticket,
        stop_loss: Some(sl.unwrap_or(pos.stop_loss)),
        take_profit: Some(tp.unwrap_or(pos.take_profit)),
    })
    → MT5Account.order_modify(...)  (gRPC)

If the ticket isn't an open position, it returns InvalidArgument.

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Adjust protection on a live trade (set a target, tighten a stop).

docs.title: 1) Set both
docs.text: let ok = sugar.modify_position_sltp(123456, Some(1.08300), Some(1.09000)).await?;

docs.title: 2) Set TP, keep SL
docs.text: sugar.modify_position_sltp(123456, None, Some(1.09200)).await?;

docs.title: 3) From pips
docs.text:
let (sl, tp) = sugar.calculate_sltp("EURUSD", true, Some(20.0), Some(40.0)).await?;
sugar.modify_position_sltp(123456, sl, tp).await?;

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • modify_position_sl · modify_position_tp · calculate_sltp

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Unknown ticket → InvalidArgument (it must be an open position).
  • Absolute prices, not distances.
  • Stops level — new SL/TP too close to market → rejection.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • modify_position_sl · modify_position_tp

docs.title: Modify Position TP (modify_position_tp)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Move only the take-profit of a position (stop-loss preserved).

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.modify_position_tp(ticket, tp)
  • Returns: Result<bool, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar) — convenience over modify_position_sltp

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn modify_position_tp(&self, ticket: u64, tp: f64) -> Result<bool, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description ticket u64 Position ticket. tp f64 New take-profit (absolute price). Output Type Description bool — true if returned_code == 10009.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: modify_position_sltp(ticket, None, Some(tp)) — TP changes, SL kept.
  • Why you need it: Extend or pull in a target as the trade develops.
  • Absolute price.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.modify_position_tp(ticket, tp)
  → modify_position_sltp(ticket, None, Some(tp))
    → MT5Service.modify_order(...) → MT5Account.order_modify(...)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Extend a target on momentum, or tighten it to bank sooner.

docs.title: 1) Set a target
docs.text: sugar.modify_position_tp(123456, 1.09200).await?;

docs.title: 2) Extend by 20 pips
docs.text:
if let Some(p) = sugar.get_position_by_ticket(123456).await? {
    sugar.modify_position_tp(p.ticket, p.take_profit + 0.0020).await?;
}

docs.title: 3) Check result
docs.text: if !sugar.modify_position_tp(123456, 1.09000).await? { println!("TP move rejected"); }

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • modify_position_sl · modify_position_sltp

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Too-tight TP (inside stops level) → rejection.
  • Unknown ticket → InvalidArgument.
