docs.text: • modify_position_sl · modify_position_sltp

docs.title: Count Open Positions (count_open_positions)
docs.text:
Sugar method: How many positions are open (optionally on a specific symbol).

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.count_open_positions(symbol)
  • Returns: Result<usize, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn count_open_positions(&self, symbol: Option<&str>) -> Result<usize, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol Option<&str> A specific symbol, or None for all. Output Type Description usize — Number of matching open positions.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Count from get_open_positions, optionally filtered by symbol.
  • Why you need it: Enforce max-position limits; dashboards.
  • None = all symbols.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.count_open_positions(symbol)
  → get_open_positions()
  → match symbol { Some(s) => count(p.symbol == s), None => len() }

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Position-limit checks before adding exposure.

docs.title: 1) Total count
docs.text: println!("{} open", sugar.count_open_positions(None).await?);

docs.title: 2) Per-symbol limit
docs.text:
if sugar.count_open_positions(Some("EURUSD")).await? >= 3 {
    println!("max EURUSD positions reached");
}

docs.title: 3) Only act when flat
docs.text:
if sugar.count_open_positions(None).await? == 0 {
    sugar.buy_market(Some("EURUSD"), 0.1, "", 0).await?;
}

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • has_open_position · get_open_positions

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• None = all symbols, not the default symbol.
  • For a plain yes/no, has_open_position is cheaper to read.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • has_open_position · get_open_positions

docs.title: Get Open Positions (get_open_positions)
docs.text:
Sugar method: All open positions as a Vec<PositionInfo>.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.get_open_positions()
  • Returns: Result<Vec<PositionInfo>, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn get_open_positions(&self) -> Result<Vec<pb::PositionInfo>, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text:
Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description Vec<PositionInfo> — Open positions (sorted by open time ascending).

PositionInfo key fields: ticket: u64, symbol, volume, price_open, price_current, stop_loss, take_profit, profit, swap, r#type (0 Buy / 1 Sell). Full table: low-level opened_orders.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: The base query the other position helpers build on.
  • Why you need it: Iterate live positions with full detail.
  • Pendings excluded: this returns position_infos only (not resting orders).

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.get_open_positions()
  → MT5Service.opened_orders(SortByOpenTimeAsc).position_infos
    → MT5Account.opened_orders(...)  (gRPC)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Dashboards, management loops, bulk operations.

docs.title: 1) List
docs.text:
for p in sugar.get_open_positions().await? {
    let side = if p.r#type == 0 { "BUY" } else { "SELL" };
    println!("#{} {side} {} {:.2} lot  P/L {:+.2}", p.ticket, p.symbol, p.volume, p.profit);
}

docs.title: 2) Total floating P/L
docs.text:
let total: f64 = sugar.get_open_positions().await?.iter().map(|p| p.profit).sum();
println!("floating {total:+.2}");

docs.title: 3) Close all losers
docs.text:
for p in sugar.get_open_positions().await? {
    if p.profit < 0.0 { sugar.close_position(p.ticket).await?; }
}

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • get_position_by_ticket · get_positions_by_symbol · count_open_positions

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Snapshot — profit/price_current are as-of the call.
  • Positions only — for pendings use the service/low-level opened_orders.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • get_total_profit · has_open_position

docs.title: Get Position By Ticket (get_position_by_ticket)
docs.text:
Sugar method: One open position by ticket, or None if not open.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.get_position_by_ticket(ticket)
  • Returns: Result<Option<PositionInfo>, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn get_position_by_ticket(&self, ticket: u64) -> Result<Option<pb::PositionInfo>, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description ticket u64 Position ticket. Output Type Description Option<PositionInfo> — Some(pos) if open, None otherwise.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Finds a position in the open list by ticket.
  • Why you need it: Read current SL/TP/volume/profit before modifying or closing.
  • Not found ≠ error: returns Ok(None).

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.get_position_by_ticket(ticket)
  → get_open_positions().into_iter().find(|p| p.ticket == ticket)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Before a modify/close that needs the position's current fields.

docs.title: 1) Read a position
docs.text:
if let Some(p) = sugar.get_position_by_ticket(123456).await? {
    println!("{} {:.2} lot @ {:.5}  P/L {:+.2}", p.symbol, p.volume, p.price_open, p.profit);
}

docs.title: 2) Move SL to breakeven using its entry
docs.text:
if let Some(p) = sugar.get_position_by_ticket(123456).await? {
    sugar.modify_position_sl(p.ticket, p.price_open).await?;
}

docs.title: 3) Exists?
docs.text: let still_open = sugar.get_position_by_ticket(123456).await?.is_some();

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • get_open_positions · get_positions_by_symbol

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• None means not open (closed or never existed) — not an error.
  • Fetches the whole list internally; if you need many lookups, call get_open_positions once and index yourself.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • get_open_positions · modify_position_sltp

docs.title: Get Positions By Symbol (get_positions_by_symbol)
docs.text:
Sugar method: All open positions on a given symbol.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.get_positions_by_symbol(symbol)
  • Returns: Result<Vec<PositionInfo>, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn get_positions_by_symbol(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<Vec<pb::PositionInfo>, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol &str Symbol to filter by (required — no default fallback here). Output Type Description Vec<PositionInfo> — Open positions whose symbol matches.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: get_open_positions() filtered by symbol.
  • Why you need it: Manage exposure on one instrument.
  • Required &str: pass the symbol explicitly.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.get_positions_by_symbol(symbol)
  → get_open_positions().into_iter().filter(|p| p.symbol == symbol)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Per-symbol management (net a symbol, scale a symbol).

docs.title: 1) List EURUSD positions
docs.text:
for p in sugar.get_positions_by_symbol("EURUSD").await? {
    println!("#{} {:.2} lot  P/L {:+.2}", p.ticket, p.volume, p.profit);
}

docs.title: 2) Net volume on a symbol
docs.text:
let net: f64 = sugar.get_positions_by_symbol("EURUSD").await?
    .iter().map(|p| if p.r#type == 0 { p.volume } else { -p.volume }).sum();
println!("net lots: {net:+.2}");

docs.title: 3) Count
docs.text: let n = sugar.get_positions_by_symbol("EURUSD").await?.len();

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • get_open_positions · get_profit_by_symbol · count_open_positions

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Exact match on the symbol string (broker suffixes matter: EURUSD vs EURUSD.m).
  • Fetches all then filters — one round-trip regardless.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • get_profit_by_symbol · get_open_positions

docs.title: Get Profit By Symbol (get_profit_by_symbol)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Floating profit summed over open positions on one symbol.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.get_profit_by_symbol(symbol)
  • Returns: Result<f64, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn get_profit_by_symbol(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol &str Symbol to sum over (required). Output Type Description f64 — Sum of profit for that symbol's open positions.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Per-symbol floating P/L.
  • Why you need it: Manage one instrument's exposure independently.
  • Zero if no positions on the symbol.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.get_profit_by_symbol(symbol)
  → get_open_positions().iter().filter(|p| p.symbol == symbol).map(|p| p.profit).sum()

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Per-symbol P/L display and symbol-level exit rules.

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text: println!("EURUSD P/L {:+.2}", sugar.get_profit_by_symbol("EURUSD").await?);

docs.title: 2) Close a symbol in profit
docs.text:
if sugar.get_profit_by_symbol("EURUSD").await? >= 30.0 {
    sugar.close_all_positions(Some("EURUSD")).await?;
}

docs.title: 3) Compare symbols
docs.text:
for s in ["EURUSD", "GBPUSD"] {
    println!("{s}: {:+.2}", sugar.get_profit_by_symbol(s).await?);
}

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • get_total_profit · get_positions_by_symbol

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Exact symbol match (broker suffixes).
  • Excludes swap/commission (sum of profit fields).

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • get_total_profit · get_positions_by_symbol

docs.title: Get Total Profit (get_total_profit)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Total floating profit across all open positions.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.get_total_profit()
  • Returns: Result<f64, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn get_total_profit(&self) -> Result<f64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description f64 — Sum of profit over all open positions.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Sums each position's floating P/L.
  • Why you need it: Position-level total (excludes swap/commission, unlike the account figure).
  • Vs floating_profit(): floating_profit reads the account-level ACCOUNT_PROFIT; this sums the per-position profit field.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.get_total_profit()
  → get_open_positions().iter().map(|p| p.profit).sum()

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Take-profit-all triggers keyed on open-position P/L.

docs.title: 1) Basic
docs.text: println!("open P/L {:+.2}", sugar.get_total_profit().await?);

docs.title: 2) Flatten on target
docs.text: if sugar.get_total_profit().await? >= 100.0 { sugar.close_all_positions(None).await?; }

docs.title: 3) Cut losses
docs.text: if sugar.get_total_profit().await? <= -50.0 { sugar.close_all_positions(None).await?; }

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • get_profit_by_symbol · floating_profit

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text: • Excludes swap/commission — it's the sum of profit fields. For the all-in account figure use floating_profit.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • get_profit_by_symbol · floating_profit

docs.title: Has Open Position (has_open_position)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Is any position open (optionally on a specific symbol)?

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.has_open_position(symbol)
  • Returns: Result<bool, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn has_open_position(&self, symbol: Option<&str>) -> Result<bool, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol Option<&str> A specific symbol, or None for any symbol. Output Type Description bool — true if at least one matching position is open.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: A yes/no exposure check.
  • Why you need it: Guard before opening (avoid stacking), or detect a pending's fill.
  • None = any symbol (this is a filter, not the default-symbol fallback).

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.has_open_position(symbol)
  → get_open_positions()
  → match symbol { Some(s) => any(p.symbol == s), None => !is_empty() }

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text:
• "Only one at a time" entry guards.
  • Pending-fill polling (see the Pending Bracket orchestrator).

docs.title: 1) Any position?
docs.text: if sugar.has_open_position(None).await? { println!("already in a trade"); }

docs.title: 2) On a symbol
docs.text:
if !sugar.has_open_position(Some("EURUSD")).await? {
    sugar.buy_market(Some("EURUSD"), 0.10, "entry", 1).await?;
}

docs.title: 3) Wait for a limit to fill
docs.text:
use std::time::Duration;
while !sugar.has_open_position(Some("EURUSD")).await? {
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(500)).await;
}

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • count_open_positions · get_open_positions

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• None = any symbol, not the default symbol.
  • Positions only — a resting pending order is not an open position yet.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • count_open_positions · get_positions_by_symbol

docs.title: Get Daily Stats (get_daily_stats)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Aggregated statistics for today's closed positions.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.get_daily_stats()
  • Returns: Result<DailyStats, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn get_daily_stats(&self) -> Result<DailyStats, MT5Error>

docs.title: DailyStats
docs.text:
pub struct DailyStats {
    pub deals: usize,   // number of closed positions today
    pub profit: f64,    // sum of profit
    pub wins: usize,    // profit > 0
    pub losses: usize,  // profit < 0
}

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description None — No parameters. Output Type Description DailyStats struct deals, profit, wins, losses for today.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Today's deals rolled up into a small summary.
  • Why you need it: A one-call end-of-day scorecard.
  • Break-even deals (profit == 0) count in deals but in neither wins nor losses.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.get_daily_stats()
  → get_deals(Period::Today)
  → aggregate: deals=len, profit=Σprofit, wins=count(>0), losses=count(<0)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Daily report / dashboard tile.

docs.title: 1) Print the scorecard
docs.text:
let s = sugar.get_daily_stats().await?;
println!("today: {} deals, {:+.2}, {}W/{}L", s.deals, s.profit, s.wins, s.losses);

docs.title: 2) Win rate
docs.text:
let s = sugar.get_daily_stats().await?;
let decided = s.wins + s.losses;
if decided > 0 { println!("win rate {:.1}%", s.wins as f64 / decided as f64 * 100.0); }

docs.title: 3) Stop trading after a bad day
docs.text:
let s = sugar.get_daily_stats().await?;
if s.profit <= -200.0 { println!("daily loss limit hit — stop"); }

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • get_deals · get_profit_today

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Today only — for other windows use get_deals/get_profit.
  • Gross profit (sum of profit); costs not deducted.
  • Break-even deals sit outside wins/losses.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • get_deals · get_profit_today

docs.title: Get Deals (get_deals)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Closed positions (deals) for a predefined Period.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.get_deals(period)
  • Returns: Result<Vec<PositionHistoryInfo>, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn get_deals(&self, period: Period) -> Result<Vec<pb::PositionHistoryInfo>, MT5Error>

docs.title: Period
docs.text: pub enum Period { Today, Yesterday, ThisWeek, ThisMonth }

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text:
Input Type Description period Period Predefined UTC window (Today / Yesterday / ThisWeek / ThisMonth). Output Type Description Vec<PositionHistoryInfo> — Closed positions opened within the window.

PositionHistoryInfo key fields: position_ticket, symbol, order_type, volume, open_price, close_price, profit, swap, commission, fee, open_time, close_time. Full table: low-level positions_history.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Resolves the Period to a [from, to] UTC range and fetches closed positions.
  • Why you need it: Trade journals, realized-P/L reports.
  • Range is by open time (see pitfalls).

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.get_deals(period)
  → period_range(period)  → (from, to)   (UTC, chrono)
  → deals_between(from, to)
    → MT5Service.positions_history(AhPositionOpenTimeAsc, from, to, page 0, 10_000)
      → MT5Account.positions_history(...)  (gRPC)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Period reports (today/yesterday/week/month) of closed trades.

docs.title: 1) Today's deals
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::sugar::Period;

let deals = sugar.get_deals(Period::Today).await?;
println!("{} closed today", deals.len());

docs.title: 2) This week's net
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::sugar::Period;

let net: f64 = sugar.get_deals(Period::ThisWeek).await?
    .iter().map(|d| d.profit + d.swap + d.commission + d.fee).sum();
println!("week net {net:+.2}");

docs.title: 3) Win rate this month
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::sugar::Period;

let d = sugar.get_deals(Period::ThisMonth).await?;
let wins = d.iter().filter(|x| x.profit > 0.0).count();
if !d.is_empty() { println!("win rate {:.1}%", wins as f64 / d.len() as f64 * 100.0); }

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • get_profit · get_deals_date_range · period shortcuts · get_daily_stats

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Filtered by open time, not close time — a trade opened before the window won't appear even if it closed inside it.
  • Cap: fetches up to 10,000 rows (page 0); very long windows may exceed that.

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • get_profit · get_deals_date_range

docs.title: Get Deals (Date Range) (get_deals_date_range)
docs.text:
Sugar method: Closed positions over an explicit UTC timestamp range.

API Information:

  • Method: sugar.get_deals_date_range(from, to)
  • Returns: Result<Vec<PositionHistoryInfo>, MT5Error>
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn get_deals_date_range(
    &self,
    from: prost_types::Timestamp,
    to: prost_types::Timestamp,
) -> Result<Vec<pb::PositionHistoryInfo>, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description from prost_types::Timestamp Range start (UTC). to prost_types::Timestamp Range end (UTC). Output Type Description Vec<PositionHistoryInfo> — Closed positions opened within [from, to].

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: Like get_deals but with an arbitrary range instead of a Period.
  • Why you need it: Custom report windows (a specific day, a backtest span).
  • Build timestamps as prost_types::Timestamp { seconds, nanos: 0 }.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.get_deals_date_range(from, to)
  → deals_between(from, to)
    → MT5Service.positions_history(AhPositionOpenTimeAsc, from, to, page 0, 10_000)

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Arbitrary windows not covered by Period.

docs.title: 1) Last 72 hours
docs.text:
fn ts(s: i64) -> prost_types::Timestamp { prost_types::Timestamp { seconds: s, nanos: 0 } }
let now = chrono::Utc::now().timestamp();
let deals = sugar.get_deals_date_range(ts(now - 3*86_400), ts(now)).await?;
println!("{} deals", deals.len());

docs.title: 2) A specific calendar day
docs.text:
use chrono::{TimeZone, Utc};
fn ts(s: i64) -> prost_types::Timestamp { prost_types::Timestamp { seconds: s, nanos: 0 } }
let start = Utc.with_ymd_and_hms(2026, 11, 5, 0, 0, 0).unwrap().timestamp();
let end   = start + 86_400;
let deals = sugar.get_deals_date_range(ts(start), ts(end)).await?;

docs.title: 3) Net over the range
docs.text:
let net: f64 = deals.iter().map(|d| d.profit + d.swap + d.commission + d.fee).sum();
println!("net {net:+.2}");

docs.title: Related Methods
docs.text: • get_deals · get_profit

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Open-time filter — same semantics as get_deals.
  • UTC — convert local/broker times before building the timestamps.
  • 10,000-row cap (single page).

docs.title: 📚 See Also
docs.text: • get_deals · get_daily_stats

docs.title: Deals Period Shortcuts (get_deals_today / _yesterday / _this_week / _this_month)
docs.text:
Sugar methods: Zero-argument shortcuts for the four Period deal queries.

API Information:

  • Methods: sugar.get_deals_today(), get_deals_yesterday(), get_deals_this_week(), get_deals_this_month()
  • Returns: Result<Vec<PositionHistoryInfo>, MT5Error> each
  • Layer: HIGH (MT5Sugar)

docs.title: Method Signatures
docs.text:
pub async fn get_deals_today(&self)      -> Result<Vec<pb::PositionHistoryInfo>, MT5Error>

docs.text:
Sugar method: Minimum SL/TP distance from price, in points (SYMBOL_TRADE_STOPS_LEVEL).

API Information:

  • Returns: Result<i64, MT5Error>

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text: pub async fn get_min_stop_level(&self, symbol: &str) -> Result<i64, MT5Error>

docs.title: ℹ️ Input / Output
docs.text: Input Type Description symbol &str Symbol name. Output Type Description i64 — Minimum stop distance in points.

docs.title: 🏛️ Essentials
docs.text:
• What it is: The broker-enforced floor for how close SL/TP (and some pendings) may sit to the market.
  • Why you need it: Validate SL/TP distances before sending — too-tight stops are rejected.
  • Units: points; convert pips → points as pips × 10 on 5/3-digit symbols.

docs.title: ⚡ Under the Hood
docs.text:
MT5Sugar.get_min_stop_level(symbol)
  → MT5Service.symbol_integer(symbol, SymbolTradeStopsLevel)
    → MT5Account.symbol_info_integer(...).value

docs.title: When to Use
docs.text: • Pre-trade SL/TP validation; clamping stop distances.

docs.title: 1) Read it
docs.text: println!("min stop {} points", sugar.get_min_stop_level("EURUSD").await?);

docs.title: 2) Validate a pip stop
docs.text:
let min_pts = sugar.get_min_stop_level("EURUSD").await?;
let sl_points = 8 * 10;   // 8 pips
if (sl_points as i64) < min_pts { println!("SL too tight: min {min_pts} points"); }

docs.title: 3) Clamp
docs.text:
let min_pts = sugar.get_min_stop_level("EURUSD").await?;
let sl_points = (5i64 * 10).max(min_pts);   // at least the broker minimum

docs.title: Presets & Shared Helpers
docs.text:
StrategyPreset (what to trade) and RiskPreset (how much, how to protect) — plus the ready-made catalog and the manage_position worker all three orchestrators share.

→ Source: src/helpers/strategies/mod.rs

Demo only

These drive demonstration orchestrators. Run on a demo account and review every value before trusting it.

docs.title: StrategyPreset — WHAT to trade
docs.text:
pub struct StrategyPreset {
    pub symbol: String,
    pub use_market: bool,        // true = market entry, false = pending at entry_price
    pub entry_price: Option<f64>,// pending price (when use_market = false)
    pub lots: Option<f64>,       // fixed lots; None = size by risk
    pub magic: u64,
    pub deviation_pips: f64,     // intended slippage budget (pips)
    pub comment: String,
}

Builder methods (chainable):

Method Effect StrategyPreset::new(symbol) Defaults: market entry, auto-size, magic 0, deviation 2.0, no comment. .market() Market entry (clears entry_price). .limit_at(price) Pending entry at price (use_market = false). .lots(l) Fixed lot size (skips risk sizing). .magic(m) Set the magic number. .comment(c) Set the order comment. 
use metarpc_mt5::strategies::StrategyPreset;

let sp = StrategyPreset::new("EURUSD").market().magic(777).comment("demo");
let pending = StrategyPreset::new("EURUSD").limit_at(1.0800).lots(0.10);

docs.title: RiskPreset — HOW MUCH to risk & how to protect
docs.text:
pub struct RiskPreset {
    pub risk_percent: f64,          // % of balance to risk (used when lots are auto-sized)
    pub sl_pips: f64,               // stop distance in pips
    pub tp_pips: Option<f64>,       // optional take-profit in pips
    pub trailing_pips: Option<f64>, // trail distance; None = no trailing
    pub be_trigger_pips: Option<f64>, // move to breakeven once this profit is reached
    pub be_plus_pips: f64,          // breakeven offset (entry + be_plus_pips)
}

Builder methods:

Method Effect RiskPreset::new(risk_percent, sl_pips) Base preset; no TP/trail/breakeven. .tp(pips) Set take-profit distance. .trailing(pips) Enable a trailing stop at this distance. .breakeven(trigger_pips, plus_pips) Move SL to entry + plus_pips once trigger_pips profit is reached. 
use metarpc_mt5::strategies::RiskPreset;

let rp = RiskPreset::new(1.0, 20.0).tp(40.0).trailing(15.0).breakeven(10.0, 2.0);

docs.title: Ready-made catalog
Shared helpers
docs.text:
The orchestrators share a few pub(crate) helpers (internal, but worth understanding):

Helper What it does size_lot(sugar, sp, rp) sp.lots if set, else sugar.calculate_position_size(symbol, risk%, sl_pips). pip_size(sugar, symbol) Pip size = get_symbol_info(symbol).point × 10. entry_price(sugar, ticket, symbol) The opened position's price_open (falls back to current ask).

docs.title: manage_position
docs.text:
The common management loop used by all three orchestrators:

async fn manage_position(
    sugar, ticket, symbol, entry, pip, rp: &RiskPreset,
    manage_secs: u64,         // how long to manage
    trail_activate_pips: f64, // profit cushion before trailing starts
) -> Result<(), MT5Error>

For a BUY position, every 500 ms until manage_secs elapses:

  1. Auto-breakeven — once (mid − entry) reaches be_trigger_pips, move SL to entry + be_plus_pips (once), if that's above the current stop.
  2. Trailing (ratchet up only) — once profit ≥ trail_activate_pips, set SL to mid − trailing_pips × pip whenever that's higher than the current stop; the stop never loosens.

The stop is tracked locally (cur_sl, starting at entry − sl_pips × pip) and sent via modify_position_sl only when it actually moves — avoiding redundant modify calls. A preset with neither be_trigger_pips nor trailing_pips simply holds for the duration.

The difference between orchestrators is mostly when trailing activates (trail_activate_pips) and what happens before management (immediate market, or wait-for-fill).

docs.title: Strategies — Master Overview
docs.text:
One page to orient fast: which orchestrators ship with the RustMT5 SDK, how to choose one, how to run it, and links to every spec.

Educational & demonstration purpose only

Every orchestrator here is a demonstration template that showcases the RustMT5 API. They are not production trading systems: entries are simplified (demo BUY side), risk controls are minimal, and there is no slippage/adverse-condition handling.

Use demo accounts only. Before anything live: understand every line, backtest, forward-test on demo, add real risk management and monitoring. Trading carries substantial risk of loss; the decisions are yours.

docs.title: The orchestrators
docs.text:
Three orchestrators, each its own module under src/helpers/strategies/, each a single async fn driven by [MT5Sugar]. A StrategyPreset says what to trade; a RiskPreset says how much and how to protect.

Strategy What it does Best for Entry point Market One-Shot Size → market entry with a pip bracket → manage (breakeven + trailing) → close. A simple, self-contained managed trade run_market_one_shot(sugar, sp, rp) Bracket + Trailing Market bracket, but trailing only starts after the trade is activate_at_pips in profit. "Let it prove itself before trailing" run_bracket_trailing(sugar, sp, rp, activate_at_pips) Pending Bracket Place a BUY LIMIT, wait for the fill (or cancel on timeout), then manage. Entering on a pullback run_pending_bracket(sugar, sp, rp, timeout_seconds)

docs.title: Pick one by goal
docs.text:
• One managed market trade, start to finish → Market One-Shot
  • Protect only once a cushion exists → Bracket + Trailing
  • Enter on a limit pullback, manage after fill → Pending Bracket

docs.title: How an orchestrator fits the SDK
docs.text:
Orchestrators sit on top of the three-layer API — plain async fns that drive MT5Sugar (and through it MT5Service / MT5Account):

ORCHESTRATORS  (src/helpers/strategies/)
  Market One-Shot · Bracket + Trailing · Pending Bracket
        │  size, enter, poll price, move the stop, close
        ▼
MT5Sugar      high-level helpers  (buy_market_with_pips, modify_position_sl, close_position, bid, …)
        ▼
MT5Service    typed facade        (place_order, modify_order, symbol_tick, …)
        ▼
MT5Account    low-level gRPC

All three manage a BUY demo position and poll the price with sugar.bid(...) on a short interval (the shared manage_position worker), then flatten what they opened.

docs.title: Shared pieces
docs.text:
• Presets: StrategyPreset (what), RiskPreset (how much), the builder methods, and the ready catalog (market_eurusd, limit_eurusd, conservative, balanced, aggressive).
  • manage_position: the common worker that applies auto-breakeven and a ratchet-up trailing stop from the RiskPreset. See Presets → manage_position.
  • Pips vs points: pip size is derived per symbol — point × 10 (so 1 pip = 10 points on 3/5-digit symbols).

docs.title: Run pattern
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt5::{MT5Account, MT5Service, MT5Sugar};
use metarpc_mt5::strategies::{run_market_one_shot, market_eurusd, balanced};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // 1) connect
    let account = MT5Account::new(12_345_678, "password", None);
    let mut sugar = MT5Sugar::new(MT5Service::new(account)).with_default_symbol("EURUSD");
    sugar.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;

    // 2) choose presets and run an orchestrator
    let sp = market_eurusd();       // StrategyPreset
    let rp = balanced();            // RiskPreset (trail 15, breakeven 10/+2)
    let ticket = run_market_one_shot(&sugar, &sp, &rp).await?;
    println!("done, ticket #{ticket}");

    // 3) disconnect
    sugar.disconnect(false).await?;
    Ok(())
}

The runnable demo of all three is examples/4_strategies/strategies_demo.rs:

cargo run --example strategies_demo

docs.title: Bracket + Trailing Orchestrator
docs.text:
Enter with a bracket, but only start trailing once the trade is activate_at_pips in profit — "let it prove itself before trailing".

Demonstration only — not production ready

Shows the strategy idea and the API calls behind it. Demo accounts only.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Same market-bracket entry as Market One-Shot, but the trailing stop stays off until the position has earned a cushion of activate_at_pips. Auto-breakeven (from be_trigger_pips) still applies earlier, at its own smaller threshold. This avoids trailing a trade that hasn't moved in your favor yet.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Size the lot (fixed or risk-based).
  2. Enter at market with buy_market_with_pips(symbol, lots, sl_pips, tp_pips, …).
  3. Read pip size and entry price; print the plan (breakeven at +be, trailing from +activate_at_pips).
  4. Manage for ~10 s via manage_position with trail_activate_pips = activate_at_pips:
  5. breakeven fires at be_trigger_pips (smaller);
  6. trailing only engages once profit ≥ activate_at_pips (larger).
  7. Close the position.

  • BUY EURUSD at market, SL 20 / TP 40 pips.
  • At +10 pips → SL to breakeven (entry +2). Trailing still off.
  • At +25 pips → trailing engages; SL = mid − 15 pips, ratcheting up only.

docs.title: Market One-Shot Orchestrator
docs.text:
The simplest end-to-end managed trade: size → market entry with a pip bracket → manage → close.

Demonstration only — not production ready

Shows the strategy idea and the API calls behind it. A real deployment needs proper sizing, slippage control, logging, monitoring and testing. Demo accounts only.

→ Source: src/helpers/strategies/market_one_shot.rs

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Opens a single BUY at market with a pip-based SL/TP bracket, manages it for a few seconds (auto-breakeven + trailing from the RiskPreset), then flattens. It's the reference template — the other two orchestrators are variations on the "enter → manage → close" shape.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Size the lot — sp.lots if fixed, else risk-based (risk_percent over sl_pips).
  2. Enter at market with buy_market_with_pips(symbol, lots, sl_pips, tp_pips, comment, magic).
  3. Read the entry price (the position's price_open) and the pip size (point × 10).
  4. Manage for ~5 s via the shared manage_position: breakeven at be_trigger_pips, trailing starting at trail_from = be_trigger_pips (or immediately — 0.0 — if no breakeven trigger is set).
  5. Close the position.

docs.title: Pending Bracket Orchestrator
docs.text:
Place a BUY LIMIT with a bracket, wait for the fill, then manage (auto-breakeven + trailing); if it isn't filled within timeout_seconds, cancel the pending order.

Demonstration only — not production ready

Shows the strategy idea and the API calls behind it. Demo accounts only.

→ Source: src/helpers/strategies/pending_bracket.rs

docs.title: What it does
docs.text: Enters on a pullback rather than at market: it places a BUY LIMIT below the current price and waits. If price trades down to the limit and fills, it manages the resulting position like the other orchestrators; if the fill never comes within the timeout, it cancels the resting order and exits cleanly.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Compute pip size; resolve the entry price — sp.entry_price if set, else 5 pips below the current bid (demo default).
  2. Size the lot and place the BUY LIMIT with buy_limit(symbol, lots, entry, comment, magic).
  3. Wait for the fill: poll has_open_position(symbol) every 500 ms until filled or until timeout_seconds elapses.
  4. Timeout: cancel the pending via close_position(ticket) and return.
  5. On fill: read the actual fill price, then manage via manage_position (trail_activate_pips = be_trigger_pips, ~5 s window).
  6. Close everything on the symbol (close_all_positions(symbol)).

pub async fn run_pending_bracket(
    sugar: &MT5Sugar,
    sp: &StrategyPreset,
    rp: &RiskPreset,
    timeout_seconds: u64,
) -> Result<u64, MT5Error>
Parameter Type Meaning sugar &MT5Sugar High-level API. sp &StrategyPreset What to trade; entry_price sets the limit (else 5 pips below bid). rp &RiskPreset Risk + protection. timeout_seconds u64 How long to wait for the fill before cancelling. returns u64 The order ticket (filled or cancelled).

docs.title: Example scenario
docs.text:
limit_eurusd(price) (or market_eurusd() for the auto 5-pip offset) + balanced(), timeout_seconds = 30:

  • Place BUY LIMIT ~5 pips below market (or at sp.entry_price).
  • Filled within 30 s: manage with breakeven 10/+2 and trailing 15, then flatten.
  • Not filled: after 30 s the pending order is cancelled; nothing is left resting.

    sugar.connect_by_server_name("MetaQuotes-Demo", 30).await?;

    let ticket = run_pending_bracket(&sugar, &market_eurusd(), &balanced(), 30).await?;
    println!("ticket #{ticket}");

    sugar.disconnect(false).await?;

}
